children.title: Fixed-Point Map Representation
children.top_down_role: Iteration-centered representation organized around a self-map and its fixed-point set.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Point Map Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Encodes a solver as repeated application of a self-map and identifies solutions with its fixed points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a nonempty set and let \(T:X\to X\) be a self-map. The associated fixed-point problem is
\[\operatorname{Fix}(T):=\{x\in X:T(x)=x\}.\]
A target \(x^\star\) is represented as a solution precisely when \(x^\star\in\operatorname{Fix}(T)\). Given \(x_0\in X\), the baseline solver generates the orbit \(x_{k+1}=T(x_k)\) for \(k\geq0\); a stopping test may use the fixed-point discrepancy between \(x_k\) and \(T(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver is represented by a self-map: solutions are its fixed points, and the baseline iteration repeatedly applies the map from an initial point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\text{ solves the represented problem}\iff x^\star\in\operatorname{Fix}(T)\), with \(x_{k+1}=T(x_k)\).

notation.meaning: set of fixed points of T

children.title: Residual Equation Representation
children.top_down_role: Root-finding representation supporting residual minimization and multisecant models.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Equation Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recasts a fixed-point problem as a root equation suitable for residual norms, linearizations, and multisecant models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a real normed vector space and let \(T:X\to X\). Define the fixed-point residual map \(F:=I-T\), so that \(F(x)=x-T(x)\). Then
\[x^\star\in\operatorname{Fix}(T)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F(x^\star)=0.\]
Thus fixed-point solution quality can be measured by \(\|F(x)\|\), while differences \(F(x_i)-F(x_j)\) provide the residual data used by secant and multisecant models. This representation does not by itself imply that residual minimization controls distance to a solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting the fixed-point map from the identity produces a residual whose roots are exactly the fixed points and whose differences support multisecant modeling.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a real normed vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Fix}(T)=F^{-1}(\{0\})\) for \(F=I-T\).

children.title: Operator-Inclusion Representation
children.top_down_role: Resolvent representation connecting fixed-point acceleration with monotone inclusions.

knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Inclusion Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents zeros of a monotone operator as fixed points of its resolvent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximally monotone, and choose \(\lambda>0\). Its resolvent is \(J_{\lambda A}:=(I+\lambda A)^{-1}:H\to H\). For every \(x\in H\),
\[0\in A(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x=J_{\lambda A}(x).\]
Consequently, the monotone inclusion \(0\in A(x)\) is represented by the fixed-point map \(T=J_{\lambda A}\), and its solution set equals \(\operatorname{Fix}(J_{\lambda A})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The zeros of a maximally monotone operator are exactly the fixed points of any positive-parameter resolvent of that operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{zer}(A)=\operatorname{Fix}(J_{\lambda A})\).

notation.meaning: set of x satisfying zero in A(x)

children.title: Linear Iteration Models
children.top_down_role: Linear or locally linearized fixed-point models used in spectral analysis.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Iteration Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specializes fixed-point iteration to an affine stationary map and exposes its linear error dynamics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional normed vector space, let \(G:X\to X\) be linear, and let \(c\in X\). The affine stationary iteration is
\[x_{k+1}=Gx_k+c.\]
If \(x^\star=Gx^\star+c\) and \(e_k:=x_k-x^\star\), then \(e_{k+1}=Ge_k\) and hence \(e_k=G^ke_0\). If \(I-G\) is invertible, the fixed point is unique and equals \(x^\star=(I-G)^{-1}c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine fixed-point iteration induces the linear error recurrence obtained by repeatedly applying its iteration matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_k=G^ke_0\); if \(I-G\) is invertible, then \(x^\star=(I-G)^{-1}c\).

notation.meaning: iteration error x_k minus x star

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: affine fixed-point substitution gives the stated linear error identity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine error identities are standard and correctly stated, but no inspectable source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Error-Polynomial Viewpoints
children.top_down_role: Polynomial representations of error propagation across fixed-point iterates.

knowledge_statements.title: Error-Polynomial Viewpoints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expresses affine combinations of stationary linear iterates as polynomials acting on the initial error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the linear error model \(e_j=G^je_0\), choose coefficients \(\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_m\) satisfying \(\sum_{j=0}^m\alpha_j=1\), and form \(\widehat{x}_m:=\sum_{j=0}^m\alpha_jx_j\). With \(p_m(z):=\sum_{j=0}^m\alpha_jz^j\), the accelerated error satisfies
\[\widehat{x}_m-x^\star=p_m(G)e_0,\qquad p_m(1)=1.\]
Thus selecting an affine combination of iterates is equivalent to selecting a degree-at-most-\(m\) error polynomial normalized at \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every affine combination of stationary linear iterates applies a normalized polynomial in the iteration operator to the initial error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat{x}_m-x^\star=p_m(G)e_0\) with \(p_m(1)=1\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct polynomial expansion of affine combinations in a stationary linear iteration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normalized error-polynomial representation is correct and fits the container, but it lacks a cited source and locator.

children.title: Spectral–Polynomial Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Connections between linear iteration spectra and attainable error-polynomial behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral–Polynomial Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relates polynomial error reduction for normal linear iterations to suppression over the operator spectrum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G\) be a normal linear operator on a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, and let \(p\) be a complex polynomial. The spectral theorem gives
\[\|p(G)\|_2=\max_{\lambda\in\sigma(G)}|p(\lambda)|.\]
Consequently, if an accelerated linear iteration has error \(e_m=p_m(G)e_0\), then
\[\|e_m\|_2\leq\max_{\lambda\in\sigma(G)}|p_m(\lambda)|\,\|e_0\|_2.\]
For normal iteration operators, worst-case polynomial acceleration is therefore exactly governed by uniform polynomial magnitude on the spectrum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a normal iteration operator, the norm of a polynomial in that operator equals the polynomial's maximum magnitude over the spectrum.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is normal on a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|p(G)\|_2=\max_{\lambda\in\sigma(G)}|p(\lambda)|\).

notation.meaning: polynomial functional calculus applied to G
induced Euclidean operator norm or vector norm

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite-dimensional spectral theorem for normal operators

children.title: Contractive Mapping Regime
children.top_down_role: Metric contraction setting for stable baseline iterations and local acceleration comparisons.

knowledge_statements.title: Contractive Mapping Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies the strict metric contraction regime used for stable fixed-point convergence comparisons.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((X,d)\) be a metric space and let \(T:X\to X\). The map \(T\) is contractive when there exists \(q\in[0,1)\) such that
\[d(Tx,Ty)\leq q\,d(x,y)\qquad\text{for all }x,y\in X.\]
The least admissible constant is the Lipschitz modulus of \(T\). This regime is stricter than nonexpansiveness because its defining modulus is uniformly below \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A map is contractive when it reduces every pairwise distance by one uniform factor strictly below one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists q\in[0,1)\ \forall x,y\in X:\ d(Tx,Ty)\leq qd(x,y)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence, uniqueness, and global convergence for contraction iteration on a Banach space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\mathcal V$ be a Banach space and let $T:\mathcal V\to\mathcal V$ be a contraction mapping. Then there exists a unique $v^*\in\mathcal V$ satisfying $Tv^*=v^*$. Moreover, for every $v^0\in\mathcal V$, the iteration $v^{n+1}=Tv^n$ converges to $v^*$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contraction from a Banach space to itself has a unique fixed point, and iteration from any initial point converges to that fixed point.
assumptions_latex: T:\mathcal V\to\mathcal V\text{ is a contraction mapping}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists!\,v^*\in\mathcal V:\ Tv^*=v^*,\qquad v^{n+1}=Tv^n\implies v^n\to v^*.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Contraction Mapping Principle with Geometric Error Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-point existence, uniqueness, and global convergence of Picard iteration for a contraction on Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be a contraction with factor \(q<1\), and define \(x^{k+1}=g(x^k)\). Then \(g\) has a unique fixed point \(x^*\). For every \(x^0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the iterates converge to \(x^*\), and \[\|x^k-x^*\|\leq \frac{q^k}{1-q}\|g(x^0)-x^0\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contraction has a unique fixed point, and repeated application of the mapping converges to it from every initial point with the stated geometric error bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists!\,x^*\in\mathbb{R}^n:\ g(x^*)=x^*,\qquad x^k\to x^*\ \forall x^0\in\mathbb{R}^n,\qquad \|x^k-x^*\|\leq \frac{q^k}{1-q}\|g(x^0)-x^0\|.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional contraction theorem with uniqueness and a global geometric error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n be closed and let T:X\to X satisfy \|T(x)-T(y)\|\leq\alpha\|x-y\| for all x,y\in X, where \alpha\in[0,1). Then T has a unique fixed point x^*\in X. For every x(0)\in X, the iteration x(t+1)=T(x(t)) converges to x^* and satisfies \|x(t)-x^*\|\leq\alpha^t\|x(0)-x^*\| for every t\geq0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contraction on a closed subset of finite-dimensional space has exactly one fixed point, and iteration from any initial point converges to it geometrically with factor alpha.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists!x^*\in X:T(x^*)=x^*,\qquad \|x(t)-x^*\|\leq\alpha^t\|x(0)-x^*\|\quad\forall x(0)\in X,\ t\geq0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Contractions, fixed points, and source-defined pseudocontractions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm-dependent definitions distinguishing pairwise contraction from contraction toward an assumed fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A map T:X\to Y, with X,Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n, is a contraction with modulus \alpha\in[0,1) in a specified norm if \|T(x)-T(y)\|\leq\alpha\|x-y\| for all x,y\in X. If T:X\to X, then x^*\in X is a fixed point when T(x^*)=x^*. A map T:X\to X is called a pseudocontraction in the source terminology if it has a fixed point x^*\in X and \|T(x)-x^*\|\leq\alpha\|x-x^*\| for every x\in X, for some \alpha\in[0,1). Contractions are continuous, whereas such pseudocontractions need not be continuous. Both properties depend on the chosen norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contraction shrinks every pairwise distance by a uniform factor below one. The source calls a map pseudocontractive when an included fixed point exists and every point moves closer to that fixed point by such a factor. Pseudocontractions need not be continuous, and both notions depend on the norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Pairwise contraction implies continuity; contraction only toward an assumed fixed point need not imply continuity.}

children.top_down_role: Weakly contractive setting underlying Mann and Halpern iteration theory.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonexpansive Mapping Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies the Hilbert-space geometry in which a map never increases pairwise distances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(C\subseteq H\) be nonempty, and let \(T:C\to C\). The map \(T\) is nonexpansive precisely when
\[\|Tx-Ty\|\leq\|x-y\|\qquad\text{for all }x,y\in C.\]
Equivalently, its global Lipschitz modulus is at most \(1\). Unlike a strict contraction, this condition permits directions in which distances are preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A self-map is nonexpansive when it does not increase the distance between any two points in its domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall x,y\in C:\ \|Tx-Ty\|\leq\|x-y\|\).

knowledge_statements.title: Averaged Mapping Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines averaged nonexpansiveness on a Hilbert space through a convex combination with a nonexpansive map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(T:H\to H\), and let \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). The map \(T\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged when there exists a nonexpansive map \(R:H\to H\) such that
\[T=(1-\alpha)I+\alpha R.\]
Equivalently, for all \(x,y\in H\),
\[\|Tx-Ty\|^2\leq\|x-y\|^2-\frac{1-\alpha}{\alpha}\|(I-T)x-(I-T)y\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A map on a Hilbert space is averaged when it is a convex combination of the identity and a nonexpansive map, equivalently when it satisfies the strengthened nonexpansive inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\text{ is }\alpha\text{-averaged}\iff \exists R:H\to H\text{ nonexpansive such that }T=(1-\alpha)I+\alpha R\).

children.title: Firmly Nonexpansive Mapping Regime
children.top_down_role: The stronger geometric regime common to resolvent-type maps.

knowledge_statements.title: Firmly Nonexpansive Mapping Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the strengthened nonexpansive geometry characteristic of projections and monotone resolvents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space and let \(T:H\to H\). The map \(T\) is firmly nonexpansive when, for every \(x,y\in H\),
\[\|Tx-Ty\|^2\leq\langle Tx-Ty,x-y\rangle.\]
Equivalently,
\[\|Tx-Ty\|^2+\|(I-T)x-(I-T)y\|^2\leq\|x-y\|^2.\]
This is also equivalent to \(T\) being \(1/2\)-averaged, that is, to the existence of a nonexpansive map \(R:H\to H\) such that \(T=\tfrac12 I+\tfrac12 R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A map on a Hilbert space is firmly nonexpansive exactly when it jointly controls image and residual differences, equivalently when it is one-half averaged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\text{ is firmly nonexpansive}\iff T\text{ is }1/2\text{-averaged}\).

notation.meaning: nonexpansive component in the one-half averaged representation

children.title: Resolvent Geometry Interface
children.top_down_role: How resolvent constructions place splitting maps within these geometric regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Resolvent Geometry Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies maximally monotone operators with firmly nonexpansive maps through the resolvent transformation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space. If \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximally monotone and \(\lambda>0\), then \(J_{\lambda A}:=(I+\lambda A)^{-1}\) is everywhere defined, single-valued, and firmly nonexpansive, with
\[\operatorname{Fix}(J_{\lambda A})=\operatorname{zer}(A).\]
Conversely, if \(T:H\to H\) is firmly nonexpansive, then the set-valued operator \(A:=T^{-1}-I\) is maximally monotone and \(T=J_A\). Thus resolvents provide the exact interface between maximal monotonicity and full-domain firm nonexpansiveness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resolvents of maximally monotone operators are firmly nonexpansive, and every full-domain firmly nonexpansive map is the resolvent of a maximally monotone operator.
assumptions_latex: \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximally monotone and \(\lambda>0\), or \(T:H\to H\) is firmly nonexpansive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\text{ maximally monotone}\Rightarrow J_{\lambda A}\text{ firmly nonexpansive}\), and \(T\text{ firmly nonexpansive}\Rightarrow T=J_{T^{-1}-I}\).

children.title: Smooth Local Residual Regime
children.top_down_role: Neighborhood-based regime supporting Jacobian and multisecant interpretations.

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Local Residual Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies local differentiability and regularity assumptions supporting Jacobian and multisecant residual models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(T:U\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be defined on an open neighborhood \(U\) of a fixed point \(x^\star\), and set \(F:=I-T\). The smooth local residual regime holds when \(F\) is continuously differentiable near \(x^\star\), \(F(x^\star)=0\), and there exist \(L>0\) and a neighborhood \(V\subseteq U\) such that
\[\|F'(x)-F'(y)\|\leq L\|x-y\|\qquad(x,y\in V),\]
with \(F'(x^\star)\) nonsingular. These conditions make local Jacobian and secant approximations well posed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a solution, the residual is continuously differentiable with Lipschitz Jacobian and a nonsingular derivative, enabling stable local Jacobian and multisecant models.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F'\text{ is locally Lipschitz near }x^\star\text{ and }F'(x^\star)\text{ is nonsingular}\).

notation.meaning: local fixed-point residual I minus T

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conventional smooth local root-finding regime, but no supplied locator fixes this exact hypothesis set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source fixes this exact combination of differentiability, Lipschitz-Jacobian, and nonsingularity assumptions. Moreover, these assumptions alone do not ensure that particular multisecant data systems are well posed.

children.title: Low-Regularity Mapping Regimes

children.title: Nonsmooth Mapping Regime
children.top_down_role: Fixed-point behavior when differentiable local residual models are unavailable.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsmooth Mapping Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Locally Lipschitz fixed-point mappings lacking classical differentiability near relevant iterates or solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The nonsmooth mapping regime consists of fixed-point problems \(x=T(x)\) for which \(T\) is locally Lipschitz near relevant iterates or fixed points but is not Fréchet differentiable at one or more such points. Equivalently, the residual \(R:=I-T\) is locally Lipschitz there but lacks a classical derivative at those points. Consequently, an acceleration model that explicitly requires \(R'(x)\) is not defined at every relevant point unless it is replaced or supplemented by an appropriate nonsmooth or derivative-free model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsmooth fixed-point map is locally Lipschitz but lacks a classical derivative at relevant points, so acceleration models that require that derivative are not everywhere defined.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(D\subseteq H\) is nonempty.
\(T:D\to H\) is locally Lipschitz near a point relevant to the iteration and is not Fréchet differentiable at that point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The residual \(R:=I-T\) is locally Lipschitz but is not Fréchet differentiable at that point, so models requiring \(R'(x)\) are not defined there.

children.title: Nonregular Mapping Regime
children.top_down_role: Fixed-point behavior under weakened local regularity or stability.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space, \(T:H\to H\), and \(S:=\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(\kappa>0\) and every neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\), some \(x\in U\) satisfies \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)>\kappa\|R(x)\|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonregularity is interpreted as failure of a local residual error bound at a fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\bar x\in S\). The residual is nonregular at \(\bar x\), in the metric-subregularity sense, when no neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and constant \(\kappa>0\) satisfy \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa\|R(x)\|\) for all \(x\in U\). Thus, for every \(\kappa>0\) and every neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\), there exists \(x\in U\) with \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)>\kappa\|R(x)\|\). In this regime, a small residual alone supplies no uniform local linear estimate of solution distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonregularity means that no local constant uniformly converts residual size into distance from the fixed-point set.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonregular Mapping Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed condition correctly negates a local residual error bound, but the leaf title does not establish that this is the intended meaning of nonregularity. An authoritative locator is needed to support this fixed-point-specific interpretation.

children.title: Globalization Requirements
children.top_down_role: Safeguarding needs arising when reliable smooth local models are absent.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A representative residual safeguard with an averaged fixed-point fallback.

children.title: Weak-Convergence Routes
children.top_down_role: Convergence structures typical of nonexpansive iterations in infinite-dimensional settings.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(T:H\to H\) is nonexpansive with \(\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(x_\star\in\operatorname{Fix}T\) such that \(x_k\rightharpoonup x_\star\) and \(\|x_k-Tx_k\|\to0\).

notation.meaning: weak convergence in the Hilbert space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Krasnosel'skii-Mann weak convergence with relaxation bounded away from both endpoints.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_0\in H\) and define the Krasnosel'skii-Mann iteration \(x_{k+1}=(1-\lambda_k)x_k+\lambda_kT x_k\). If \(T\) is nonexpansive, \(\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\), and \(\varepsilon\leq\lambda_k\leq1-\varepsilon\) for every \(k\) and some \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/2]\), then there exists \(x_\star\in\operatorname{Fix}T\) such that \(x_k\rightharpoonup x_\star\). Moreover, the fixed-point residual vanishes: \(\|x_k-Tx_k\|\to0\). The conclusion is weak convergence; norm convergence need not follow in an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A suitably relaxed iteration of a nonexpansive map converges weakly to a fixed point, and its residual tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak-Convergence Routes

children.title: Strong-Convergence Routes
children.top_down_role: Anchoring, viscosity, and projection mechanisms used to strengthen convergence.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(T:H\to H\) is nonexpansive with nonempty fixed-point set \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Halpern iterates satisfy \(x_k\to P_Su\) in norm.

notation.meaning: metric projection onto the closed convex set S

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Halpern anchoring for strong convergence and projection selection.

source_refs.locator: 12.2 Accelerated proximal point and optimized Halpern method p. 258

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S:=\operatorname{Fix}T\), choose an anchor \(u\in H\), and generate \(x_{k+1}=\alpha_k u+(1-\alpha_k)T x_k\). If \(T\) is nonexpansive, \(S\neq\varnothing\), \(\alpha_k\to0\), \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k=\infty\), and \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}|\alpha_{k+1}-\alpha_k|<\infty\), then \(x_k\to P_Su\) in norm. Thus anchoring strengthens the usual weak-convergence conclusion and simultaneously specifies which fixed point is selected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Halpern anchoring drives a nonexpansive fixed-point iteration strongly to the fixed point nearest the anchor.

children.title: Asymptotic-Regularity Theory
children.top_down_role: Residual-vanishing structures shared by relaxed and averaged iterations.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space, \(T:H\to H\) is nonexpansive, and \(z\in\operatorname{Fix}T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lambda_k(1-\lambda_k)\|x_k-Tx_k\|^2\leq\|x_0-z\|^2\); hence, if \(\sum_k\lambda_k(1-\lambda_k)=\infty\), then \(\liminf_k\|x_k-Tx_k\|=0\), and under standard monotonicity of these residuals they converge to zero.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Energy inequality underlying asymptotic regularity of relaxed nonexpansive iterations.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(z\in\operatorname{Fix}T\), the relaxed iteration obeys \(\|x_{k+1}-z\|^2\leq\|x_k-z\|^2-\lambda_k(1-\lambda_k)\|x_k-Tx_k\|^2\). Consequently, \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lambda_k(1-\lambda_k)\|x_k-Tx_k\|^2\leq\|x_0-z\|^2\). If \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lambda_k(1-\lambda_k)=\infty\), this estimate yields vanishing residual along a subsequence; together with the standard residual monotonicity for this iteration, it gives asymptotic regularity \(\|x_k-Tx_k\|\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxed nonexpansive iteration dissipates a weighted squared residual, leading under persistent relaxation to a vanishing fixed-point residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic-Regularity Theory

children.title: Fixed-Point Selection

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(T:H\to H\) is nonexpansive with \(S:=\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For anchor \(u\), the iteration \(x_{k+1}=\alpha_k u+(1-\alpha_k)Tx_k\) selects \(P_Su\), meaning \(x_k\to P_Su\) in norm.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because the fixed-point set \(S\) of a nonexpansive mapping is closed and convex, each anchor \(u\in H\) has a unique metric projection \(P_Su\). Under the stated weight conditions, the anchored iteration \(x_{k+1}=\alpha_k u+(1-\alpha_k)Tx_k\) converges in norm to \(P_Su\). Hence the anchor defines a deterministic selection rule among multiple fixed points: it selects the unique \(x_\star\in S\) satisfying \(\langle u-x_\star,z-x_\star\rangle\leq0\) for every \(z\in S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An anchor selects the unique fixed point nearest to it; Halpern iteration converges strongly to that projection.

children.title: Fixed-Point Residual Measures
children.top_down_role: Operator-residual measures used in termination and worst-case analysis.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Point Residual Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm residual for single-valued fixed-point mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The fixed-point residual measure of \(T\) at \(x\in D\) is \(r_T(x):=\|x-Tx\|\). It is nonnegative, is computable from one evaluation of \(T\), and satisfies \(r_T(x)=0\) if and only if \(x\in\operatorname{Fix}T\). For \(\varepsilon\geq0\), an iterate \(x\in D\) is an absolute \(\varepsilon\)-approximate fixed point when \(r_T(x)\leq\varepsilon\). This residual measures violation of \(x=T(x)\); without an error bound, it does not by itself quantify distance to the fixed-point set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The fixed-point residual is the norm of x minus T(x); it vanishes exactly at fixed points and, for a nonnegative tolerance, supports approximate termination tests.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a normed space, \(D\subseteq X\), and \(T:D\to X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_T(x):=\|x-Tx\|\geq0\), and \(r_T(x)=0\) if and only if \(x\in\operatorname{Fix}T\); moreover, \(r_T(x)\leq\varepsilon\) defines an absolute \(\varepsilon\)-approximate fixed point.

children.title: Solution-Distance Measures
children.top_down_role: Progress measures expressed through distance to a solution or fixed-point set.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Distance Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set distance as the canonical solution-error measure for nonunique fixed points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:X\to X\) have nonempty fixed-point set \(S:=\operatorname{Fix}T\). The solution-distance measure at \(x\in X\) is \(d_S(x):=\operatorname{dist}(x,S)=\inf_{z\in S}\|x-z\|\). It measures error relative to the entire fixed-point set and therefore remains meaningful when solutions are nonunique. One has \(d_S(x)=0\) if and only if \(x\in\overline S\); when \(S\) is closed, this is equivalent to \(x\in S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solution distance is the infimum of the distances from a point to all fixed points, so it accommodates nonunique solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a normed space and \(T:X\to X\) has nonempty fixed-point set \(S:=\operatorname{Fix}T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_S(x):=\inf_{z\in S}\|x-z\|\), with \(d_S(x)=0\) exactly when \(x\in\overline S\), and exactly when \(x\in S\) if \(S\) is closed.

children.top_down_role: Residual-sensitive bounds used to assess solution proximity.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a normed space, \(T:X\to X\), and \(S:=\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\).
\(U\subseteq X\) is a specified region and \(\kappa>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The residual error bound on \(U\) is the condition \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa\|x-Tx\|\) for every \(x\in U\).

source_refs.locator: 10 Maximality and monotone operator theory p. 215

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A residual error bound with modulus \(\kappa\) on \(U\) is the predicate \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa\|x-Tx\|\) for every \(x\in U\). It is local at \(\bar x\in S\) if such \(\kappa\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) exist, and global if \(U=X\). This condition is a metric-subregularity estimate for \(I-T\) at residual value \(0\) and converts a computable equation violation into a bound on solution distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An error bound upper-bounds distance to the fixed-point set by a constant times the computable fixed-point residual.

children.title: Residual-to-Distance Transfer
children.top_down_role: Interfaces that convert residual progress into solution-distance information.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori conversion of residual tolerance into solution-distance tolerance.

source_refs.locator: 10 Maximality and monotone operator theory p. 215
source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the residual error bound \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa\|x-Tx\|\) holds throughout \(U\). For any evaluated point \(x\in U\), the checkable inequality \(\|x-Tx\|\leq\varepsilon\) certifies \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa\varepsilon\). More generally, a residual estimate \(\|x_k-Tx_k\|\leq\rho_k\) transfers directly to \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,S)\leq\kappa\rho_k\), provided \(x_k\in U\). Thus residual rates transfer to solution-distance rates without changing their order, but only while the error bound remains valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under an error bound, a residual at most epsilon certifies solution distance at most kappa times epsilon.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-to-Distance Transfer

children.title: Minimal-Displacement Measures
children.top_down_role: Displacement-based progress objects for maps lacking fixed points.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(T:H\to H\) is nonexpansive.
\(\overline{\operatorname{ran}(I-T)}\) is the norm closure of the displacement range.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The minimal displacement vector is \(v:=P_{\overline{\operatorname{ran}(I-T)}}0\), and \(\|v\|=\inf_{x\in H}\|x-Tx\|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal displacement for nonexpansive mappings, including fixed-point-free cases.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The minimal displacement vector of \(T\) is \(v:=P_{\overline{\operatorname{ran}(I-T)}}0\). For a nonexpansive mapping, the closed displacement range is convex, so this projection is well defined and unique. Its norm satisfies \(\|v\|=\operatorname{dist}(0,\overline{\operatorname{ran}(I-T)})=\inf_{x\in H}\|x-Tx\|\). Hence \(\|v\|\) is the smallest achievable residual magnitude. If \(\|v\|>0\), then \(T\) has no fixed point; if \(v=0\), approximate fixed points exist, although an exact fixed point need not exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimal displacement is the smallest attainable residual magnitude; a positive value certifies that the mapping has no fixed point.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimal-Displacement Measures

children.title: Inconsistency Certificates
children.top_down_role: Indicators that distinguish inconsistent regimes from slow feasible progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Inconsistency Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal-displacement certificate for a nonexpansive fixed-point problem on a Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(T:H\to H\) be nonexpansive, and set \(D=\operatorname{Id}-T\). Assume \(C=\overline{\operatorname{ran}D}\) is convex, and define the minimal-displacement vector \(v=P_C(0)\). The datum \(v\), together with a verified inequality \(\lVert v\rVert>0\), is an inconsistency certificate: for every \(x\in H\), \[\lVert x-Tx\rVert\geq \operatorname{dist}(0,C)=\lVert v\rVert>0.\] Consequently, \(T\) has no fixed point. The certificate also supplies a uniform positive lower bound on every attainable fixed-point residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero minimal-displacement vector certifies that every residual is bounded away from zero and hence that the mapping has no fixed point.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(T:H\to H\) is nonexpansive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Fix}T=\varnothing\) and \(\lVert x-Tx\rVert\geq\lVert v\rVert>0\) for every \(x\in H\).

notation.meaning: Metric projection onto the closed convex set C.

Convexity conditions for the closed displacement range require source confirmation.

children.title: Fixed-Point-Free Regimes
children.top_down_role: Interpretive regimes in which displacement replaces solution residuals.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Point-Free Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and strong fixed-point inconsistency distinguished through the displacement range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a normed space and \(T:X\to X\). With \(D=\operatorname{Id}-T\), the fixed-point-free condition is \[\operatorname{Fix}T=\varnothing\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\notin\operatorname{ran}D.\] The regime is strongly inconsistent when \(0\notin\overline{\operatorname{ran}D}\), equivalently when \(\inf_{x\in X}\lVert x-Tx\rVert>0\). It is weakly inconsistent when \(0\in\overline{\operatorname{ran}D}\setminus\operatorname{ran}D\); then no fixed point exists although residuals can approach zero. Thus vanishing residuals alone do not certify existence without an attainment or compactness condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mapping is fixed-point-free exactly when zero is absent from its displacement range; residuals may nevertheless converge to zero when zero lies only in its closure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Fix}T=\varnothing\) exactly when \(0\notin\operatorname{ran}(\operatorname{Id}-T)\).

notation.meaning: Set of fixed points of T.

children.title: Splitting-Solver Progress Measures
children.top_down_role: Primal, dual, feasibility, and operator residual interfaces inherited from splitting solvers.

knowledge_statements.title: Splitting-Solver Progress Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator and KKT residual interfaces for finite-dimensional convex primal-dual splitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces, let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions, and let \(A:X\to Y\) be linear. For a decoded splitting iterate \((x^k,y^k)\in X\times Y\), define \[p_k=\operatorname{dist}\!\left(0,\partial f(x^k)+A^*y^k\right),\qquad q_k=\operatorname{dist}\!\left(Ax^k,\partial g^*(y^k)\right),\] with distance to the empty set defined as \(+\infty\). If a solver state satisfies \(z^{k+1}=Tz^k\), also define \(r_k^{\mathrm{op}}=\lVert z^k-Tz^k\rVert\). Then \(r_k^{\mathrm{KKT}}=(p_k^2+q_k^2)^{1/2}\) vanishes exactly when \(0\in\partial f(x^k)+A^*y^k\) and \(Ax^k\in\partial g^*(y^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Splitting progress can be represented by a fixed-point residual and by two primal-dual KKT distances; the combined KKT distance vanishes exactly when both optimality inclusions hold.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces.
\(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions.
The splitting state has a decoded pair \((x^k,y^k)\in X\times Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_k^{\mathrm{KKT}}=0\) if and only if \(0\in\partial f(x^k)+A^*y^k\) and \(Ax^k\in\partial g^*(y^k)\).

children.title: Picard Iteration Family
children.top_down_role: Unrelaxed baseline orbit used to define acceleration and fallback behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Picard Iteration Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unrelaxed fixed-point orbit and baseline residual stopping rule in a normed space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a normed space, let \(C\subseteq X\) be nonempty, let \(T:C\to C\), and choose \(x^0\in C\), a tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), and an iteration limit \(K\in\mathbb{N}\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots,K\), stop and return \(x^k\) if \(\lVert x^k-Tx^k\rVert\leq\varepsilon\) or \(k=K\); otherwise generate \[x^{k+1}=T(x^k).\] This unrelaxed orbit is the baseline trajectory for comparison with relaxed fixed-point updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Picard iteration repeatedly applies the mapping without relaxation and stops when its fixed-point residual reaches the tolerance or the iteration limit is reached.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a normed space and \(C\subseteq X\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each generated iterate satisfies \(x^{k+1}=T(x^k)\in C\), and termination occurs no later than index \(K\).

children.title: Krasnosel'skii Relaxation Family
children.top_down_role: Constant-relaxation fixed-point family.

knowledge_statements.title: Krasnosel'skii Relaxation Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constant convex relaxation of a fixed-point mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a convex subset of a normed space, let \(T:C\to C\), choose \(x^0\in C\), and fix \(\lambda\in(0,1)\). The Krasnosel'skii relaxed iteration is \[x^{k+1}=(1-\lambda)x^k+\lambda T(x^k),\qquad k=0,1,\ldots.\] Given a tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), stop at the first \(k\) for which \(\lVert x^k-Tx^k\rVert\leq\varepsilon\), or at a prescribed iteration limit, and return the last iterate. Convexity of \(C\) ensures that every relaxed iterate remains in \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Krasnosel'skii relaxation takes a constant convex combination of the current point and its image under the fixed-point mapping.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}=(1-\lambda)x^k+\lambda T(x^k)\in C\).

knowledge_statements.title: Krasnosel'skii–Mann Iteration Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable convex relaxation of a self-map on a convex subset of a normed space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a normed space, let \(C\subseteq X\) be convex, let \(T:C\to C\), and choose \(x^0\in C\). Prescribe \((\lambda_k)_{k\geq0}\subset[0,1]\), a tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), and an iteration limit \(K\in\mathbb{N}\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots,K\), stop and return \(x^k\) if \(\lVert x^k-Tx^k\rVert\leq\varepsilon\) or \(k=K\); otherwise generate \[x^{k+1}=(1-\lambda_k)x^k+\lambda_kT(x^k).\] Convexity of \(C\) ensures that every generated iterate belongs to \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Krasnosel'skii–Mann iteration uses a possibly different convex relaxation parameter at each application of the mapping.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a normed space and \(C\subseteq X\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every generated iterate satisfies \(x^{k+1}=(1-\lambda_k)x^k+\lambda_kT(x^k)\in C\).

children.title: Ishikawa Relaxation Family
children.top_down_role: The classical Ishikawa branch of multi-evaluation fixed-point iteration.

knowledge_statements.title: Ishikawa Relaxation Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage relaxation using two mapping evaluations per iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be convex, let \(T:C\to C\), choose \(x^0\in C\), and prescribe \(\alpha_k,\beta_k\in[0,1]\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), compute \[y^k=(1-\beta_k)x^k+\beta_kT(x^k),\qquad x^{k+1}=(1-\alpha_k)x^k+\alpha_kT(y^k).\] Stop when \(\lVert x^k-Tx^k\rVert\leq\varepsilon\) or at a prescribed iteration limit, and return the last iterate. The method generally requires evaluations of \(T(x^k)\) and \(T(y^k)\) at each completed iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ishikawa iteration forms an intermediate relaxed point, evaluates the mapping there, and uses that second value to update the main iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y^k\in C\) and \(x^{k+1}\in C\) for every completed iteration.

children.title: Multistage Relaxation Families
children.top_down_role: Broader staged relaxation schemes extending Mann-type iteration.

knowledge_statements.title: Multistage Relaxation Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-stage nested relaxation with configurable parameters at each stage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be convex, let \(T:C\to C\), fix a stage count \(s\geq1\), choose \(x^0\in C\), and prescribe \(a_{k,j}\in[0,1]\). At iteration \(k\), set \(y^{k,0}=x^k\) and compute \[y^{k,j}=(1-a_{k,j})y^{k,j-1}+a_{k,j}T(y^{k,j-1}),\qquad j=1,\ldots,s,\] followed by \(x^{k+1}=y^{k,s}\). Stop on a prescribed residual test or iteration limit. The cases \(s=1\) and larger \(s\) respectively recover one-stage relaxation and nested multi-evaluation relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multistage method applies successive relaxed mapping evaluations inside each outer iteration and adopts the final stage as the next iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}=y^{k,s}\in C\) after \(s\) relaxed mapping evaluations.

notation.meaning: Number of stages per outer iteration.
Stage-j point during outer iteration k.

A source is needed to align this generic parameterization with established named multistage schemes.

children.title: Multi-Evaluation Cost Regimes
children.top_down_role: Work regimes governing when additional map evaluations remain worthwhile.

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Evaluation Cost Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle cost of finite-stage relaxation measured in mapping evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the black-box oracle model, count one query whenever \(T(u)\) is evaluated at a previously supplied point \(u\). An \(s\)-stage nested relaxation iteration that evaluates \(T(y^{k,j-1})\) once at every stage uses exactly \(s\) mapping-oracle calls per completed outer iteration. Hence \(K\) completed outer iterations use \(sK\) calls, excluding any additional residual evaluation. If the stopping residual \(\lVert x^k-Tx^k\rVert\) cannot reuse a stage value, each tested iterate incurs one further call, so testing all \(K+1\) iterates yields at most \(sK+K+1\) calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An s-stage relaxation costs s mapping evaluations per outer iteration, plus at most one additional evaluation for each independently tested residual.
assumptions_latex: Each stage makes exactly one black-box query to \(T\).
Residual tests reuse cached values whenever available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_T=sK\) without extra residual queries, and \(N_T\leq sK+K+1\) when every iterate is tested separately.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the bound is an exact count under the explicitly stated oracle model.

children.title: Relaxation Parameter Regimes

children.title: Under-Relaxation
children.top_down_role: Conservative relaxation used to stabilize difficult mappings.

knowledge_statements.title: Under-Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservative convex-combination regime for a relaxed fixed-point update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a normed space, let \(C\subseteq X\) be convex, let \(T:C\to C\), and define \(T_\lambda=(1-\lambda)\operatorname{Id}+\lambda T\). The update is under-relaxed precisely when \(0<\lambda<1\). For every \(x\in C\), the point \(T_\lambda x\) lies on the segment joining \(x\) and \(Tx\), and \[T_\lambda x-x=\lambda(Tx-x),\qquad \lVert T_\lambda x-x\rVert=\lambda\lVert Tx-x\rVert.\] Moreover, \(\operatorname{Fix}T_\lambda=\operatorname{Fix}T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under-relaxation uses a parameter strictly between zero and one, shortening every mapping displacement while preserving all fixed points.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a normed space and \(C\subseteq X\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in C\), \(\lVert T_\lambda x-x\rVert=\lambda\lVert Tx-x\rVert\), and \(\operatorname{Fix}T_\lambda=\operatorname{Fix}T\).

children.title: Over-Relaxation
children.top_down_role: Aggressive relaxation whose admissibility depends on mapping geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Over-Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissible extrapolative relaxation for an averaged mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space and let \(T:H\to H\) be \(\alpha\)-averaged for some \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), meaning that \(T=(1-\alpha)\operatorname{Id}+\alpha R\) for a nonexpansive mapping \(R:H\to H\). Define \(T_\lambda=(1-\lambda)\operatorname{Id}+\lambda T\). The update is over-relaxed when \(\lambda>1\), and it remains averaged whenever \[1<\lambda<\frac{1}{\alpha}.\] In this interval, \(T_\lambda=(1-\lambda\alpha)\operatorname{Id}+\lambda\alpha R\), so \(T_\lambda\) is \(\lambda\alpha\)-averaged and \(\operatorname{Fix}T_\lambda=\operatorname{Fix}T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An alpha-averaged mapping with alpha below one permits over-relaxation beyond one and below the reciprocal of alpha while retaining averagedness and the same fixed points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_\lambda\) is \(\lambda\alpha\)-averaged and \(\operatorname{Fix}T_\lambda=\operatorname{Fix}T\).

children.title: Adaptive Relaxation
children.top_down_role: Feedback-controlled relaxation based on observed solver behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-ratio feedback with safeguarded variable relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:C\to C\), choose \(x^0\in C\), \(0<\lambda_{\min}\leq\lambda_{\max}\leq1\), \(\lambda_0\in[\lambda_{\min},\lambda_{\max}]\), and \(\eta>0\). Set \(r_k=\lVert x^k-Tx^k\rVert\) and update \[x^{k+1}=(1-\lambda_k)x^k+\lambda_kT(x^k).\] For \(k\geq1\), when \(r_k>0\), choose \[\lambda_{k+1}=\operatorname{clip}_{[\lambda_{\min},\lambda_{\max}]}\!\left(\lambda_k(r_{k-1}/r_k)^\eta\right);\] if \(r_k=0\), stop and return \(x^k\). Otherwise stop when \(r_k\leq\varepsilon\) or at the iteration limit. Safeguarding keeps every update under-relaxed or unrelaxed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This adaptive scheme enlarges or reduces relaxation according to the observed residual ratio while clipping every parameter to a safe interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_k\in[\lambda_{\min},\lambda_{\max}]\) for every generated iterate.

notation.meaning: Fixed-point residual norm at iteration k.
Projection of a scalar onto the safeguard interval.

review_flags: The residual-ratio controller is a precise representative adaptive scheme, but an authoritative source is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports this specific residual-ratio controller. Its indexing is also incomplete: lambda_1 is never defined, while the ratio observed at index k is assigned to lambda_{k+1} after the update using lambda_k.

children.title: Linesearched Relaxation
children.top_down_role: Relaxation selected through residual or merit-based acceptance.

knowledge_statements.title: Linesearched Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backtracking relaxation accepted by decrease of a fixed-point residual merit function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:C\to C\), \(r(x)=T(x)-x\), and \(\Phi(x)=\tfrac12\lVert r(x)\rVert^2\). Given \(x_0\in C\), trial bound \(\bar\lambda>0\), contraction factor \(\beta\in(0,1)\), and \(c\in(0,1)\), at iteration \(k\) test \(\lambda_{k,j}=\bar\lambda\beta^j\) in increasing order of \(j\geq0\). Accept the first feasible candidate \(z_{k,j}=x_k+\lambda_{k,j}r(x_k)\in C\) satisfying \(\Phi(z_{k,j})\leq(1-c\lambda_{k,j})\Phi(x_k)\), and set \(x_{k+1}=z_{k,j}\). Stop when \(\lVert r(x_k)\rVert\leq\varepsilon\); output \(x_k\). If no trial is accepted, report linesearch failure rather than taking an uncertified step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backtrack the relaxation parameter until a feasible relaxed fixed-point step decreases the residual merit function; otherwise report failure.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty subset of a Hilbert space and every accepted candidate belongs to \(C\).
\(T:C\to C\) can be evaluated and \(\Phi(x)=\tfrac12\lVert T(x)-x\rVert^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\lambda_k(T(x_k)-x_k)\) satisfies the stated merit-decrease test whenever the linesearch succeeds.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the Linesearched Relaxation container and explicitly reports failure when no trial is accepted. However, no source supports this particular residual-merit acceptance rule, so its status must remain needs_source.

children.title: Classical Halpern Family
children.top_down_role: Canonical anchored iteration and its standard control-sequence regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Classical Halpern Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong convergence of the classical anchored iteration for a nonexpansive Hilbert-space mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a nonempty closed convex subset of a real Hilbert space, let \(T:C\to C\) be nonexpansive with \(F=\operatorname{Fix}(T)\neq\varnothing\), and fix an anchor \(u\in C\). From any \(x_0\in C\), define \(x_{k+1}=\alpha_{k+1}u+(1-\alpha_{k+1})T x_k\). If \(0<\alpha_k<1\), \(\alpha_k\to0\), \(\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\alpha_k=\infty\), and \(\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}|\alpha_{k+1}-\alpha_k|<\infty\), then \(x_k\to P_Fu\) in norm. Thus the anchor selects the fixed point nearest to \(u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the standard vanishing, nonsummable, bounded-variation control regime, Halpern iterates converge strongly to the fixed point nearest the anchor.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex in a real Hilbert space; \(T:C\to C\) is nonexpansive and \(\operatorname{Fix}(T)\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\to P_{\operatorname{Fix}(T)}u\) strongly.

children.title: Optimized Halpern Family
children.top_down_role: Worst-case-designed anchored schemes for fixed-point residual reduction.

assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex in a real Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert x_k-Tx_k\rVert\leq 2\lVert x_0-x_\star\rVert/(k+1)\) for every \(k\geq1\); consequently, checking residuals before forming the next iterate requires at most \(\lceil 2\lVert x_0-x_\star\rVert/\varepsilon\rceil\) evaluations of \(T\) to certify the stated tolerance.

source_refs.locator: 12.2 Accelerated proximal point and optimized Halpern method p. 258

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:C\to C\) be nonexpansive on a nonempty closed convex subset \(C\) of a real Hilbert space, let \(x_0\in C\), and suppose \(x_\star\in\operatorname{Fix}(T)\). Define the anchored oracle iteration \(x_{k+1}=\frac{1}{k+2}x_0+\frac{k+1}{k+2}T x_k\) for \(k\geq0\). Using one evaluation of \(T\) to check the residual at \(x_k\) and, when necessary, form \(x_{k+1}\), the residual obeys \(\lVert x_k-Tx_k\rVert\leq\frac{2\lVert x_0-x_\star\rVert}{k+1}\) for \(k\geq1\). Hence, for \(\varepsilon>0\), some index \(k\leq\lceil2\lVert x_0-x_\star\rVert/\varepsilon\rceil-1\) satisfies \(\lVert x_k-Tx_k\rVert\leq\varepsilon\), and checking through that index uses at most \(\lceil2\lVert x_0-x_\star\rVert/\varepsilon\rceil\) evaluations of \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The optimized anchored schedule has a worst-case residual bound of order one over the iteration count; when each evaluated residual is checked before the next iterate is formed, certifying the resulting tolerance bound uses one more operator evaluation than the terminal iterate index.

children.title: Prior-Free Halpern Variant Family

children.title: Adaptive Halpern Families
children.top_down_role: Anchored variants whose controls respond to observed solver behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Halpern Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: History-dependent anchoring with explicit safeguards on the adaptive control sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:C\to C\), choose an anchor \(u\in C\), an initial point \(x_0\in C\), and bounds \(0<\ell_k\leq h_k<1\). At iteration \(k\), evaluate \(T x_k\), form the observable history \(\mathcal H_k=(x_0,Tx_0,\ldots,x_k,Tx_k)\), and select \(\alpha_{k+1}=A_k(\mathcal H_k)\in[\ell_{k+1},h_{k+1}]\). Set \(x_{k+1}=\alpha_{k+1}u+(1-\alpha_{k+1})T x_k\). Stop when \(\lVert x_k-Tx_k\rVert\leq\varepsilon\), and output \(x_k\). For strong-convergence variants, the safeguards must additionally enforce \(\alpha_k\to0\), \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\), and the regularity condition required by the selected Halpern theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose each anchoring weight from observed iterates and residuals while safeguarding the control conditions needed by the applicable Halpern convergence theorem.
assumptions_latex: \(T:C\to C\), \(u,x_0\in C\), and all convex-combination iterates remain in \(C\).
\(A_k\) depends only on the observable history \(\mathcal H_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=\alpha_{k+1}u+(1-\alpha_{k+1})Tx_k\) with a history-adapted, safeguarded \(\alpha_{k+1}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a coherent abstract template for history-adapted Halpern weights and fits the leaf, but no cited source establishes this family or identifies the exact regularity condition needed for convergence.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a nonempty convex subset of a real Hilbert space, let \(T:C\to C\), choose an anchor \(u\in C\), and set \(x_0=u\). Define \(\alpha_{k+1}=1/(k+2)\) and \(x_{k+1}=\alpha_{k+1}u+(1-\alpha_{k+1})T x_k\) for \(k\geq0\). The coefficient is determined solely by the iteration index: it uses no Lipschitz, metric-regularity, error-bound, solution-distance, or terminal-horizon estimate. Evaluate \(T\) once per step and stop when the observable residual \(\lVert x_k-Tx_k\rVert\) is at most \(\varepsilon\); output \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a convex domain, use the reciprocal index schedule, which needs no problem constant or prescribed horizon, and stop using the directly observable fixed-point residual.

children.title: Unknown-Constant Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Unknown-Constant Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information restriction defining implementability when analytic tuning constants are unavailable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\theta\) denote an unavailable problem constant, such as a Lipschitz, error-bound, metric-subregularity, or solution-distance parameter. A Halpern control policy is admissible in the unknown-constant regime if, for every \(k\), its weight and restart decision satisfy \(\alpha_{k+1}=A_k(\mathcal H_k)\) and \(q_{k+1}=Q_k(\mathcal H_k)\), where \(\mathcal H_k\) contains only previously computed iterates, operator values, residuals, accepted tests, and fixed user tolerances. Neither \(A_k\) nor \(Q_k\) may depend on \(\theta\) or a certified bound for \(\theta\). Any claimed guarantee must therefore be uniform over all values of \(\theta\) compatible with the observed history.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A method handles unknown constants only when its weights and restarts use observable history, and its guarantee is uniform over compatible hidden constants.
assumptions_latex: \(\theta\) is unavailable to the algorithm and is not bounded by supplied data.
\(\mathcal H_k\) contains only information computed by time \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_{k+1}\) and \(q_{k+1}\) are measurable functions of \(\mathcal H_k\) alone, and guarantees are uniform over compatible \(\theta\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is the appropriate content kind for an information-restriction leaf, but the proposed formal history model and uniformity requirement are uncited and are not uniquely determined by the title.

children.title: Restarted Halpern Families
children.top_down_role: Restarted anchoring for changing residual or local-regularity regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Restarted Halpern Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epochwise Halpern iteration with anchors reset from computed iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose restart times \(0=\tau_0<\tau_1<\cdots\), set \(a_0=x_0\), and let \((\alpha_j)_{j\geq1}\subset(0,1)\) be an inner control schedule. During epoch \(m\), initialize \(x_{\tau_m}=a_m\) and, for \(j=0,\ldots,\tau_{m+1}-\tau_m-1\), set \(x_{\tau_m+j+1}=\alpha_{j+1}a_m+(1-\alpha_{j+1})T x_{\tau_m+j}\). At the epoch boundary set \(a_{m+1}=x_{\tau_{m+1}}\). Restart times may be fixed or selected from observable residual tests. Stop and output \(x_k\) when \(\lVert x_k-Tx_k\rVert\leq\varepsilon\). Convergence or acceleration requires a separate condition on epoch lengths and restart tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run Halpern steps in epochs, replacing the anchor by the latest epoch endpoint; use fixed or residual-triggered restart times.
assumptions_latex: \(T:C\to C\), \(x_0\in C\), and all generated convex combinations lie in \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each epoch is a Halpern iteration anchored at \(a_m=x_{\tau_m}\), with output certified only by the stated residual test.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The epochwise construction fits Restarted Halpern Families and avoids an unconditional convergence claim. A source is still required to establish that this restart convention represents a recognized family and to specify usable epoch or trigger conditions.

children.title: Strong-Convergence Anchoring Extensions
children.top_down_role: Anchoring extensions aimed at strong convergence or distinguished fixed-point selection.

children.title: Viscosity Approximation Methods
children.top_down_role: Contractive-selection extensions of anchored fixed-point iteration.

knowledge_statements.title: Viscosity Approximation Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contractive viscosity selection for a nonexpansive fixed-point set in Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a nonempty closed convex subset of a real Hilbert space, let \(T:C\to C\) be nonexpansive with \(F=\operatorname{Fix}(T)\neq\varnothing\), and let \(f:C\to C\) be a contraction with modulus \(q<1\). Define \(x_{k+1}=\alpha_k f(x_k)+(1-\alpha_k)T x_k\). If \(0<\alpha_k<1\), \(\alpha_k\to0\), \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\), and \(\sum_k|\alpha_{k+1}-\alpha_k|<\infty\), then \(x_k\) converges strongly to the unique \(p\in F\) satisfying \(p=P_F f(p)\), equivalently \(\langle p-f(p),z-p\rangle\geq0\) for every \(z\in F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing the fixed anchor by a contraction selects the unique fixed point solving the associated variational inequality and yields strong convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex; \(T:C\to C\) is nonexpansive with \(F\neq\varnothing\).
\(f:C\to C\) is a contraction with modulus \(q<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\to p\) strongly, where \(p=P_Ff(p)\) is the unique viscosity-selected fixed point.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem has the correct role and local meaning, and the stated viscosity-selected limit is standard. Because no citation is supplied for the exact control-sequence hypotheses and conclusion, authoritative source support is required.

children.title: Hybrid Projection Methods
children.top_down_role: Projection-assisted fixed-point selection and strong-convergence families.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Projection Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: CQ-type projection construction for strong convergence to a selected fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a nonempty closed convex subset of a real Hilbert space, let \(T:C\to C\) be nonexpansive with \(F=\operatorname{Fix}(T)\neq\varnothing\), and choose \(x_0\in C\). For \(k\geq0\), choose \(\alpha_k\in[0,1)\), set \(y_k=\alpha_kx_k+(1-\alpha_k)Tx_k\), define \(C_k=\{z\in C:\lVert y_k-z\rVert\leq\lVert x_k-z\rVert\}\) and \(Q_k=\{z\in C:\langle x_k-z,x_0-x_k\rangle\geq0\}\), and update \(x_{k+1}=P_{C_k\cap Q_k}x_0\). Under the standard safeguard \(\sup_k\alpha_k<1\), the iterates converge strongly to \(P_Fx_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project the initial point onto two separating half-spaces generated by the current fixed-point step; the iterates converge strongly to the nearest fixed point.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex in a real Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=P_{C_k\cap Q_k}x_0\) is well-defined and \(x_k\to P_Fx_0\) strongly.

notation.meaning: Metric projection onto a closed convex set S.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and strong-convergence claim fit Hybrid Projection Methods, but the precise half-space orientation, well-definedness, and sufficiency of the stated safeguard require an inspectable theorem or algorithm citation.

children.title: Shrinking-Projection Methods
children.top_down_role: Nested-feasible-set variants used in strong-convergence constructions.

knowledge_statements.title: Shrinking-Projection Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested-set projection variant retaining fixed points while shrinking the feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_0=C\), where \(C\) is a nonempty closed convex subset of a real Hilbert space, and let \(T:C\to C\) be nonexpansive with \(F=\operatorname{Fix}(T)\neq\varnothing\). Choose \(x_0\in C\). For \(k\geq0\), set \(y_k=\alpha_kx_k+(1-\alpha_k)Tx_k\), define \(C_{k+1}=\{z\in C_k:\lVert y_k-z\rVert\leq\lVert x_k-z\rVert\}\), and update \(x_{k+1}=P_{C_{k+1}}x_0\). Then \(F\subseteq C_{k+1}\subseteq C_k\). Under \(0\leq\alpha_k<1\) and \(\sup_k\alpha_k<1\), the sequence converges strongly to \(P_Fx_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly retain the half-space containing every fixed point and project the initial point onto the resulting nested sets.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex in a real Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq C_{k+1}\subseteq C_k\) and \(x_k\to P_Fx_0\) strongly.

notation.meaning: Metric projection onto the current set.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nested-set algorithm fits the shrinking-projection leaf and its fixed-point containment calculation is plausible. The exact strong-convergence theorem and parameter safeguard are unsupported by a citation.

children.title: Relaxation-Anchoring Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Parameter and transient regimes in which relaxation or anchoring loses its intended benefit.

children.title: Inadmissible Over-Relaxation
children.top_down_role: Instability outside geometry-compatible relaxation ranges.

knowledge_statements.title: Inadmissible Over-Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar nonexpansive example showing divergence beyond the admissible relaxation interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On the real Hilbert space \(\mathbb R\), let \(T(x)=-x\), so \(T\) is nonexpansive and \(\operatorname{Fix}(T)=\{0\}\). For a constant relaxation \(\lambda>0\), the relaxed mapping is \(R_\lambda=(1-\lambda)I+\lambda T=(1-2\lambda)I\), and the iteration satisfies \(x_{k+1}=(1-2\lambda)x_k\). If \(\lambda>1\) and \(x_0\neq0\), then \(|1-2\lambda|>1\), hence \(|x_k|=|1-2\lambda|^k|x_0|\to\infty\). At \(\lambda=1\), nonzero iterates alternate and do not converge. Thus nonexpansiveness alone does not permit relaxation \(\lambda\geq1\) for this mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the reflection mapping on the real line, relaxation at one cycles and any larger relaxation diverges geometrically.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration cycles for \(\lambda=1\) and diverges for \(\lambda>1\).

children.title: Anchor-Induced Transient Slowdown
children.top_down_role: Practical slowdown caused by anchor placement and conservative schedules.

children.title: Anchor Bias
children.top_down_role: Solution-selection distortion associated with anchor placement.

knowledge_statements.title: Anchor Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of the strong-limit selection on the chosen anchor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonexpansive mapping \(T:C\to C\) with nonempty closed convex fixed-point set \(F\), a strongly convergent Halpern iteration with anchor \(u\) selects \(P_Fu\). Consequently, anchors \(u\) and \(v\) can produce different limits whenever \(P_Fu\neq P_Fv\), even though the operator and its fixed-point set are unchanged. Concretely, for \(C=\mathbb R\) and \(T=P_{[0,1]}\), one has \(F=[0,1]\); anchors \(u=-1\) and \(v=2\) select limits \(0\) and \(1\), respectively. Anchor bias is therefore a selection effect, not a nonzero fixed-point residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Halpern anchoring selects the fixed point nearest the anchor, so different anchors may lead to different exact fixed points.
assumptions_latex: \(T:C\to C\) is nonexpansive and \(F=\operatorname{Fix}(T)\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
The employed Halpern control sequence ensures strong convergence to \(P_Fu\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The limiting selection depends on \(u\), while every selected limit still belongs to \(F\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selection property and concrete projection example are mathematically consistent with classical Halpern convergence. No source is supplied, and the record should also be supported as an anchor-bias phenomenon within the transient-slowdown failure branch rather than merely as a neutral selection property.

children.title: Slow Anchor Transients
children.top_down_role: Prolonged early behavior caused by conservative anchoring schedules.

knowledge_statements.title: Slow Anchor Transients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A scalar contraction shows that an early anchoring phase can create a long post-anchor transient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\mathbb{R}\), \(T(x)=qx\) with \(0<q<1\), anchor \(u\ne0\), and \(x_0=0\). For fixed \(a\in(0,1)\) and integer \(N\ge1\), set \(\alpha_n=a\) for \(n<N\) and \(\alpha_n=0\) thereafter, and iterate \(x_{n+1}=\alpha_nu+(1-\alpha_n)T(x_n)\). Then
\[x_N=\frac{a\bigl(1-((1-a)q)^N\bigr)}{1-(1-a)q}u,\qquad x_{N+m}=q^m x_N.\]
Thus, although anchoring is eventually removed and the unique fixed point is \(0\), reaching \(|x_{N+m}|\le\varepsilon\) requires \(m\ge \log(|x_N|/\varepsilon)/(-\log q)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite anchoring phase can displace an iterate from the fixed point, after which a weak contraction needs logarithmically many additional steps to remove that displacement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{N+m}=q^m x_N\), with \(m\ge \log(|x_N|/\varepsilon)/(-\log q)\) necessary for \(|x_{N+m}|\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: anchoring weight during the initial phase

children.title: Anchor-Placement Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Performance boundaries associated with poorly positioned anchors.

knowledge_statements.title: Anchor-Placement Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies dependence of Halpern-type iterates on the chosen anchor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be a convex subset of a Hilbert space, let \(T:C\to C\) be nonexpansive, and let \(\alpha_n\in[0,1]\). From a common initial point define \(x_{n+1}^{u}=\alpha_nu+(1-\alpha_n)T(x_n^{u})\) and \(x_{n+1}^{v}=\alpha_nv+(1-\alpha_n)T(x_n^{v})\). Then
\[\|x_n^{u}-x_n^{v}\|\le\left(1-\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}(1-\alpha_j)\right)\|u-v\|.\]
Consequently, if \(\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\alpha_j=\infty\), the worst-case sensitivity factor approaches one; changing the anchor need not have an asymptotically vanishing effect.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two runs with different anchors may separate by nearly the full anchor distance when the cumulative anchoring weight is infinite.

children.title: Control-Sequence Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Failures associated with unsuitable asymptotic parameter behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Control-Sequence Failure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete examples expose two essential asymptotic requirements on Halpern control sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(x_{n+1}=\alpha_nu+(1-\alpha_n)T(x_n)\) on \(\mathbb{R}\). Failure of \(\alpha_n\to0\) can prevent convergence to a fixed point: with \(T(x)=0\), \(u=1\), and \(\alpha_n\equiv a>0\), one has \(x_{n+1}=a\notin\operatorname{Fix}T\). Failure of \(\sum_n\alpha_n=\infty\) can prevent anchor-selected convergence: with \(T(x)=x\), \(u=0\), \(x_0=1\), and \(\sum_n\alpha_n<\infty\),
\[x_n=\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}(1-\alpha_j),\]
whose limit is positive whenever \(0\le\alpha_j<1\) and the product is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonvanishing controls can create anchor bias, while summable controls can exert too little total influence to select the anchor-prescribed fixed point.
assumptions_latex: The iteration is the Halpern relaxation-anchoring scheme on \(\mathbb{R}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dropping either \(\alpha_n\to0\) or \(\sum_n\alpha_n=\infty\) permits failure in a nonexpansive scalar example.
