children.title: Persistent-Evaluation Error Regimes
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of relaxed and anchored iterations to persistent evaluation errors.

children.title: Persistent Perturbation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Solver behavior under sustained disturbances in map evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Perturbation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A persistent additive evaluation perturbation produces a nonzero asymptotic fixed-point error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\mathbb{R}\), \(T(x)=qx\) with \(0\le q<1\), and evaluate \(T\) with a constant additive perturbation \(e\ne0\). The iteration \(x_{n+1}=T(x_n)+e\) satisfies
\[x_n=q^nx_0+\frac{1-q^n}{1-q}e\longrightarrow\frac{e}{1-q}.\]
Since \(\operatorname{Fix}T=\{0\}\), the limiting point is not a fixed point of the unperturbed map. Hence boundedness of evaluation errors alone does not ensure convergence to \(\operatorname{Fix}T\); persistent bias is amplified by \((1-q)^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant evaluation bias shifts the limit away from the true fixed point, with amplification inversely proportional to the contraction margin.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_n\to e/(1-q)\notin\operatorname{Fix}T\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The persistent-bias counterexample is mathematically correct and appropriately classified, but no inspectable source is supplied for the perturbed iteration claim.

children.title: Computational-Error Regimes
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity to finite-precision or approximate computational work.

knowledge_statements.title: Computational-Error Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative computational errors can destroy contractivity when their gain exceeds the contraction margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T(x)=qx\) on \(\mathbb{R}\), where \(0<q<1\), and suppose the computed evaluation is \(\widetilde T_n(x)=T(x)+e_n(x)\) with \(|e_n(x)|\le\eta|x|\). For the admissible deterministic error \(e_n(x)=\eta x\), the computed iteration is
\[x_{n+1}=(q+\eta)x_n.\]
It converges to the fixed point \(0\) when \(q+\eta<1\), stagnates when \(q+\eta=1\), and diverges in magnitude for \(q+\eta>1\) whenever \(x_0\ne0\). Thus the sharp worst-case relative-error boundary is \(\eta=1-q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative evaluation error preserves convergence only while its gain remains below the contraction margin; at or above that margin stagnation or divergence is possible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Worst-case convergence holds only for \(q+\eta<1\); failure is possible when \(q+\eta\ge1\).

notation.meaning: computed map evaluation at iteration n

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relative-error boundary is correct for the stated scalar worst-case error model, but the record has no citation or locator supporting this inexact fixed-point regime.

children.title: Error-Accumulation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where evaluation errors overwhelm the benefit of orbit modification.

knowledge_statements.title: Error-Accumulation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted error propagation identifies when perturbations vanish rather than accumulate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T:C\to C\) be nonexpansive on a Hilbert space and compare the exact and perturbed anchored iterations
\[x_{n+1}=\alpha_nu+(1-\alpha_n)T(x_n),\qquad y_{n+1}=\alpha_nu+(1-\alpha_n)(T(y_n)+e_n).\]
Writing \(d_n=\|y_n-x_n\|\), one has
\[d_n\le d_0\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}(1-\alpha_j)+\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(1-\alpha_k)\|e_k\|\prod_{j=k+1}^{n-1}(1-\alpha_j).\]
Therefore perturbations are asymptotically harmless whenever both terms on the right tend to zero; failure is possible when the weighted error convolution has positive limsup.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perturbations vanish only if the control sequence suppresses both the initial discrepancy and the accumulated, appropriately weighted evaluation errors.
assumptions_latex: \(\alpha_n\in[0,1]\) and all displayed iterates remain in \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the displayed product and weighted convolution tend to zero, then \(\|y_n-x_n\|\to0\).

notation.meaning: distance between perturbed and exact iterates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed propagation inequality and sufficient vanishing condition are internally correct, and condition fits the leaf. An authoritative source with a specific locator is absent.

children.title: Sequence-Polynomial Acceleration Family
children.top_down_role: Classical accelerators based on transformed iterate sequences, error polynomials, and residual subspaces.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Fixed-point, polynomial, Krylov, and Anderson acceleration chapters

children.title: Scalar Sequence Acceleration
children.top_down_role: Classical scalar transformations motivating vector and fixed-point extrapolation.

children.title: Aitken Delta-Squared Family
children.top_down_role: Low-order scalar convergence acceleration.

knowledge_statements.title: Aitken Delta-Squared Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar three-term extrapolation for eliminating a locally geometric leading error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given three consecutive scalar values \(s_n,s_{n+1},s_{n+2}\), define \(\Delta s_n=s_{n+1}-s_n\) and \(\Delta^2s_n=s_{n+2}-2s_{n+1}+s_n\). If \(\Delta^2s_n
e0\), the Aitken transform is
\[\widehat s_n=s_n- rac{(\Delta s_n)^2}{\Delta^2s_n}.\]
If \(s_n=s+c\lambda^n\) with \(c
e0\) and \(\lambda
otin\{0,1\}\), then \(\widehat s_n=s\) exactly. An implementation outputs \(\widehat s_n\) when the denominator passes a prescribed safeguarding test and otherwise retains \(s_n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aitken extrapolation uses three scalar iterates to cancel one geometric error mode, subject to a nonzero and numerically safe second difference.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat s_n=s_n-(\Delta s_n)^2/\Delta^2s_n\), and a single geometric error mode is eliminated exactly.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Aitken formula and exact cancellation of one geometric mode are correct, and algorithm is the appropriate kind. No authoritative source or locator is provided.

children.title: Steffensen Family
children.top_down_role: Fixed-point specialization of scalar sequence acceleration.

knowledge_statements.title: Steffensen Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative-free fixed-point acceleration obtained by applying Aitken extrapolation to two map evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g:D\subseteq\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\). Given \(x_n\in D\), compute \(y_n=g(x_n)\) and \(z_n=g(y_n)\). When \(z_n-2y_n+x_n\ne0\), set
\[x_{n+1}=x_n-\frac{(y_n-x_n)^2}{z_n-2y_n+x_n}.\]
If the denominator is zero or fails a numerical safeguard, use a declared fallback such as \(x_{n+1}=y_n\). Stop when a prescribed residual test such as \(|g(x_{n+1})-x_{n+1}|\le\varepsilon\) is satisfied; otherwise repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Steffensen iteration accelerates a scalar fixed-point map using two evaluations per step and an Aitken correction, with safeguarding for a small denominator.
assumptions_latex: The Aitken denominator is nonzero unless the fallback is used.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Steffensen update is correctly stated as an Aitken acceleration using two map evaluations, but it lacks an authoritative citation with a specific locator.

children.title: Shanks Transformation Family
children.top_down_role: Higher-order scalar extrapolation based on finite sequence histories.

knowledge_statements.title: Shanks Transformation Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-k scalar extrapolation characterized by annihilation of successive forward differences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For scalar data \(s_n,\ldots,s_{n+2k}\), choose coefficients \(\gamma_0,\ldots,\gamma_k\) satisfying
\[\sum_{i=0}^{k}\gamma_i=1,\qquad \sum_{i=0}^{k}\gamma_i\Delta s_{n+i+j}=0\quad(0\le j<k),\]
provided this linear system is nonsingular. The order-\(k\) Shanks transform is
\[e_k(s_n)=\sum_{i=0}^{k}\gamma_i s_{n+i}.\]
For \(k=1\) it equals the Aitken delta-squared transform. If \(s_n=s+\sum_{r=1}^{k}c_r\lambda_r^n\) with distinct \(\lambda_r\notin\{0,1\}\), the transform returns \(s\) whenever its defining system is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The order-k Shanks transform chooses normalized coefficients that annihilate k shifted difference relations and thereby removes k distinct geometric error modes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_k(s_n)=\sum_{i=0}^{k}\gamma_i s_{n+i}\), with exact elimination of \(k\) admissible geometric modes.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is plausible and consistent with the Shanks family, but the coefficient characterization and exact multimode-elimination claim require an authoritative, inspectable source.

children.title: Epsilon-Algorithm Family
children.top_down_role: Recursive realization of Shanks-type transformations.

knowledge_statements.title: Epsilon-Algorithm Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Wynn's scalar epsilon recursion computes the Shanks table without solving each coefficient system explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a scalar sequence \((s_n)\), initialize \(\varepsilon_{-1}^{(n)}=0\) and \(\varepsilon_{0}^{(n)}=s_n\). For \(k\ge0\), compute
\[\varepsilon_{k+1}^{(n)}=\varepsilon_{k-1}^{(n+1)}+\frac{1}{\varepsilon_k^{(n+1)}-\varepsilon_k^{(n)}},\]
whenever the denominator is nonzero and numerically safe. The even entries are approximations and satisfy \(\varepsilon_{2k}^{(n)}=e_k(s_n)\), the order-\(k\) Shanks transform; odd entries are auxiliary. A safeguarded implementation skips or restarts an update when its reciprocal denominator is too small.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Wynn's epsilon algorithm recursively builds Shanks transforms; even table entries are accelerated estimates and odd entries are auxiliary reciprocals.
assumptions_latex: The required scalar sequence values are available.
Every performed reciprocal has a nonzero safeguarded denominator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varepsilon_{2k}^{(n)}=e_k(s_n)\) for every well-defined table entry.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Wynn's epsilon recursion and its even-entry relationship to Shanks transforms are stated consistently, but no source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Vector Extrapolation Families
children.top_down_role: Sequence-only accelerators for vector iterates.

children.title: Minimal Polynomial Extrapolation
children.top_down_role: Polynomial error-elimination family based on vector differences.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Polynomial Extrapolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vector extrapolation using a normalized dependence among consecutive first differences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given vectors \(x_0,\ldots,x_{k+1}\) in a finite-dimensional inner-product space, form \(u_i=x_{i+1}-x_i\). Determine \(c_0,\ldots,c_{k-1}\) from
\[\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}c_i u_i=-u_k,\qquad c_k=1,\]
using the exact solution when it exists or a declared least-squares solution otherwise. If \(\sigma=\sum_{i=0}^{k}c_i\ne0\), set \(\gamma_i=c_i/\sigma\) and output
\[s_k=\sum_{i=0}^{k}\gamma_i x_i.\]
The step is undefined without regularization when the coefficient problem is unsolvable under the chosen convention or \(\sigma=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MPE finds a dependence among vector differences, normalizes its coefficients to sum to one, and combines the associated iterates into an extrapolated estimate.
assumptions_latex: \(x_0,\ldots,x_{k+1}\) lie in a finite-dimensional inner-product space.
The coefficient solve and any least-squares convention are specified.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The core MPE coefficient construction is plausible, but the declared least-squares extension and undefined-case conventions need support from an authoritative vector-extrapolation source.

children.title: Reduced Rank Extrapolation
children.top_down_role: Residual-minimizing vector extrapolation with Krylov connections.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced Rank Extrapolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vector extrapolation defined by constrained minimization of a combined first difference.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given vectors \(x_0,\ldots,x_{k+1}\) in a finite-dimensional inner-product space, set \(u_i=x_{i+1}-x_i\) for \(0\le i\le k\). Choose
\[\gamma\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\sum_{i=0}^{k}\gamma_i=1}\left\|\sum_{i=0}^{k}\gamma_i u_i\right\|,
\qquad s_k=\sum_{i=0}^{k}\gamma_i x_i.\]
If the constrained minimizer is not unique, a declared convention such as the minimum-Euclidean-norm coefficient vector selects one. The minimized vector \(\sum_i\gamma_i u_i\) is the residual surrogate used by reduced rank extrapolation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: RRE combines iterates with coefficients summing to one while minimizing the norm of the same combination of their first differences.
assumptions_latex: \(x_0,\ldots,x_{k+1}\) lie in a finite-dimensional inner-product space.
A tie-breaking convention is specified when minimizers are nonunique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_k=\sum_{i=0}^{k}\gamma_i x_i\) for coefficients minimizing \(\|\sum_i\gamma_i(x_{i+1}-x_i)\|\) subject to \(\sum_i\gamma_i=1\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The constrained residual-minimization formulation is appropriate for reduced rank extrapolation and algorithm fits the container, but no authoritative citation with a locator is provided.

children.title: Modified Minimal Polynomial Extrapolation
children.top_down_role: Test-vector-based minimal-polynomial variants.

knowledge_statements.title: Modified Minimal Polynomial Extrapolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional MMPE using prescribed test vectors to determine an extrapolating polynomial.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given iterates \(x_n,\ldots,x_{n+k}\in\mathbb{K}^d\), set \(u_j=x_{n+j+1}-x_{n+j}\). Choose test vectors \(y_1,\ldots,y_k\in\mathbb{K}^d\) and solve for \(c_0,\ldots,c_{k-1}\) with \(c_k=1\) such that \[\sum_{j=0}^{k}c_j\langle y_i,u_j\rangle=0,\qquad i=1,\ldots,k.\] If \(\sigma=\sum_{j=0}^{k}c_j\neq0\), define \(\gamma_j=c_j/\sigma\) and return \[s_{n,k}=\sum_{j=0}^{k}\gamma_jx_{n+j}.\] The step fails when the projected system is singular or \(\sigma=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MMPE determines normalized extrapolation weights by annihilating successive differences against prescribed test vectors, then forms their affine combination of the iterates.
assumptions_latex: The projected coefficient system is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_{n,k}=\sum_{j=0}^{k}\gamma_jx_{n+j}\) is the MMPE extrapolate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the displayed system uses u_k and therefore requires x_{n+k+1}, contrary to the opening iterate range. An authoritative MMPE source is needed to settle the indexing and pairing convention.

children.title: Vector Epsilon Algorithms

knowledge_statements.title: Vector Epsilon Algorithms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Wynn-type vector epsilon recursion with the Euclidean vector inverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a sequence \((s_n)\subset\mathbb{K}^d\), initialize \(\varepsilon_{-1}^{(n)}=0\) and \(\varepsilon_0^{(n)}=s_n\). For \(k,n\geq0\), compute \[\varepsilon_{k+1}^{(n)}=\varepsilon_{k-1}^{(n+1)}+\bigl(\varepsilon_k^{(n+1)}-\varepsilon_k^{(n)}\bigr)^{-1},\qquad v^{-1}=\frac{v}{\langle v,v\rangle}.\] Each required difference must have nonzero squared norm. The accelerated approximants are the even entries \(\varepsilon_{2m}^{(n)}\); computation stops at a requested order or when an inverse is undefined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The vector epsilon algorithm applies Wynn’s tableau recursion using a vector inverse; its even tableau entries are accelerated sequence estimates.
assumptions_latex: Every inverted tableau difference has nonzero squared norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The order-\(m\) accelerated estimate is \(\varepsilon_{2m}^{(n)}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but vector epsilon algorithms have variant- and field-dependent inverse conventions. No source supports this particular recursion or its use over the stated scalar field.

children.title: Topological Epsilon Algorithms
children.top_down_role: Epsilon transformations constructed through topological duality interfaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Topological Epsilon Algorithms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First topological epsilon algorithm on a vector space paired with its dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be paired with \(E^*\), fix \(y\in E^*\setminus\{0\}\), and initialize \(\varepsilon_{-1}^{(n)}=0\in E^*\), \(\varepsilon_0^{(n)}=s_n\in E\). Define alternating entries by \[\varepsilon_{2k+1}^{(n)}=\varepsilon_{2k-1}^{(n+1)}+\frac{y}{\langle y,\varepsilon_{2k}^{(n+1)}-\varepsilon_{2k}^{(n)}\rangle},\] \[\varepsilon_{2k+2}^{(n)}=\varepsilon_{2k}^{(n+1)}+\frac{\varepsilon_{2k}^{(n+1)}-\varepsilon_{2k}^{(n)}}{\langle\varepsilon_{2k+1}^{(n+1)}-\varepsilon_{2k+1}^{(n)},\varepsilon_{2k}^{(n+1)}-\varepsilon_{2k}^{(n)}\rangle}.\] Provided all denominators are nonzero, return the even entries as extrapolates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Topological epsilon recursion alternates primal and dual tableau entries, using a fixed functional to replace the vector inverse.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) and \(E^*\) form a separating dual pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each \(\varepsilon_{2k}^{(n)}\in E\) is a topological epsilon extrapolate.

notation.meaning: dual space paired with the sequence space

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but the primal-dual recursion and denominator ordering are variant-specific and unsupported by a citation.

children.title: Epsilon-Family Correspondences
children.top_down_role: Structural relationships between vector and topological variants.

knowledge_statements.title: Epsilon-Family Correspondences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection correspondence between a topological epsilon tableau and Wynn’s scalar epsilon tableau.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\varepsilon_k^{(n)})\) be the first topological epsilon tableau generated from \((s_n)\subset E\) with fixed \(y\in E^*\), and let \((e_k^{(n)})\) be Wynn’s scalar epsilon tableau generated from \(a_n=\langle y,s_n\rangle\). Whenever both recursions are defined, their even entries satisfy \[e_{2k}^{(n)}=\langle y,\varepsilon_{2k}^{(n)}\rangle.\] Thus applying the test functional to a topological epsilon extrapolate gives exactly the corresponding scalar epsilon extrapolate of the projected sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection by the defining functional maps each even topological epsilon estimate to the matching scalar epsilon estimate of the projected sequence.
assumptions_latex: Both epsilon tableaux use compatible initialization and indexing.
All denominators required through order \(2k\) are nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_{2k}^{(n)}=\langle y,\varepsilon_{2k}^{(n)}\rangle\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits this correspondence leaf, but the asserted equality depends on the exact topological epsilon variant and compatible indexing. No source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(A\) is symmetric positive definite and \(\gamma>0\) is sufficiently small, then the JOR and Richardson iterations converge to the solution of \(Ax=b\).

children.title: Richardson Iteration
children.top_down_role: The Richardson branch of stationary linear fixed-point iteration.

knowledge_statements.title: Richardson Iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationary Richardson iteration for a finite-dimensional linear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb{K}^{d\times d}\), \(b\in\mathbb{K}^d\), \(x_0\in\mathbb{K}^d\), relaxation parameter \(\omega\neq0\), and tolerance \(\tau\geq0\), generate \[r_k=b-Ax_k,\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+\omega r_k.\] Stop when \(\lVert r_k\rVert\leq\tau\) and return \(x_k\). If \(A\) is Hermitian positive definite and \(0<\omega<2/\lambda_{\max}(A)\), define \(x_*=A^{-1}b\) and \(e_k=x_k-x_*\). Then \[e_{k+1}=(I-\omega A)e_k,\qquad e_k=(I-\omega A)^ke_0,\] and \(x_k\to x_*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Richardson iteration repeatedly adds a fixed multiple of the linear residual; for a Hermitian positive-definite system it converges under the standard spectral stepsize condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\to A^{-1}b\) and \(e_k=(I-\omega A)^ke_0\).

notation.meaning: error x_k-x_* relative to the solution

children.title: Linear Mixing
children.top_down_role: Baseline mixing schemes for combining current iterates with residual information.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Mixing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constant-relaxation mixing of a fixed-point map with the identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G:C\to C\) be a fixed-point map on a convex set \(C\) in a normed space. Given \(x_0\in C\), mixing parameter \(\alpha\), and tolerance \(\tau\geq0\), compute \[x_{k+1}=(1-\alpha)x_k+\alpha G(x_k)=x_k+\alpha\bigl(G(x_k)-x_k\bigr).\] Stop when \(\lVert G(x_k)-x_k\rVert\leq\tau\) and return \(x_k\). If \(0\leq\alpha\leq1\), convexity ensures that every iterate remains in \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear mixing relaxes a fixed-point update by taking an affine combination of the current point and its image.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha(G(x_k)-x_k)\in C\).

children.title: Polynomial Mixing Interpretation

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Mixing Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-polynomial representation of variable linear mixing for an affine fixed-point map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G(x)=Mx+c\) have a fixed point \(x_*\), and apply variable mixing \(x_{j+1}=(1-\alpha_j)x_j+\alpha_jG(x_j)\). With \(e_j=x_j-x_*\), one has \[e_k=p_k(M)e_0,\qquad p_k(z)=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\bigl((1-\alpha_j)+\alpha_jz\bigr),\qquad p_k(1)=1.\] Thus the mixing parameters determine a factored polynomial whose magnitude can be controlled on a spectral region containing \(\sigma(M)\), subject to the normalization \(p_k(1)=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an affine fixed-point map, successive variable-mixing steps apply a factored polynomial in the iteration matrix to the initial error.

notation.meaning: linear part of the affine fixed-point map

children.title: Chebyshev Semi-Iteration
children.top_down_role: Spectrally tuned polynomial acceleration.

knowledge_statements.title: Chebyshev Semi-Iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chebyshev minimax acceleration for a positive-definite linear system with known spectral bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be Hermitian positive definite with \(\sigma(A)\subset[a,b]\), where \(0<a<b\), and let \(x_*=A^{-1}b_0\). Define \[p_k(\lambda)=\frac{T_k\!\left((a+b-2\lambda)/(b-a)\right)}{T_k\!\left((a+b)/(b-a)\right)},\qquad p_k(0)=1,\] and compute \(x_k\) by the three-term Chebyshev recurrence so that \[x_k-x_*=p_k(A)(x_0-x_*).\] Stop when the residual norm meets the prescribed tolerance. The polynomial minimizes \(\max_{\lambda\in[a,b]}|p(\lambda)|\) over degree-at-most-\(k\) polynomials satisfying \(p(0)=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Chebyshev semi-iteration uses known spectral bounds to apply the minimax residual polynomial through a short three-term recurrence.
assumptions_latex: The spectral bounds are available to the iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k-x_*=p_k(A)(x_0-x_*)\) with \(p_k\) minimax on \([a,b]\).

notation.meaning: Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind
spectral enclosure for the system matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal-Residual Polynomial Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean minimal-residual polynomial acceleration for a nonsingular linear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Ax=b\), choose \(x_0\) and set \(r_0=b-Ax_0\). At order \(k\), select \[p_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{p\in\mathcal P_k,\ p(0)=1}\lVert p(A)r_0\rVert_2.\] Write \(p_k(z)=1-zq_{k-1}(z)\), set \[x_k=x_0+q_{k-1}(A)r_0,\qquad r_k=p_k(A)r_0,\] and stop when \(\lVert r_k\rVert_2\leq\tau\). In exact arithmetic this is the polynomial characterization of a Krylov minimal-residual iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method chooses the normalized degree-k polynomial that minimizes the Euclidean residual over the associated Krylov affine space.
assumptions_latex: Arithmetic is exact for the stated polynomial equivalence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert r_k\rVert_2=\min_{p\in\mathcal P_k,\ p(0)=1}\lVert p(A)r_0\rVert_2\).

notation.meaning: polynomials of degree at most k

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Step Polynomial Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-step stationary acceleration of an affine fixed-point iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G(x)=Mx+c\) have fixed point \(x_*\). Given \(x_0,x_1\) and scalars \(\alpha,\beta\), generate \[x_{k+1}=(1+\beta-\alpha)x_k+\alpha G(x_k)-\beta x_{k-1},\qquad k\geq1.\] Stop when the fixed-point residual meets a prescribed tolerance. For \(e_k=x_k-x_*\), the update is \[e_{k+1}=\bigl((1+\beta-\alpha)I+\alpha M\bigr)e_k-\beta e_{k-1},\] so each error is obtained from the initial states by a degree-growing matrix polynomial recurrence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two-step acceleration combines the current mapped state, current state, and previous state, producing a second-order polynomial error recurrence.
assumptions_latex: Initial states \(x_0,x_1\) and parameters \(\alpha,\beta\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The errors obey a second-order polynomial recurrence in \(M\).

notation.meaning: error relative to the fixed point

knowledge_statements.title: Momentum Polynomial Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constant-momentum acceleration of a relaxed affine fixed-point update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G(x)=Mx+c\) have fixed point \(x_*\). Given \(x_{-1}=x_0\), relaxation \(\alpha\), momentum \(\beta\), and tolerance \(\tau\), iterate \[x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha\bigl(G(x_k)-x_k\bigr)+\beta(x_k-x_{k-1}).\] Stop when \(\lVert G(x_k)-x_k\rVert\leq\tau\) and return \(x_k\). The errors satisfy \[e_{k+1}=\bigl((1-\alpha+\beta)I+\alpha M\bigr)e_k-\beta e_{k-1},\] which defines a momentum-dependent polynomial filter on each spectral mode of \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Momentum acceleration adds the previous displacement to a relaxed fixed-point correction, yielding a second-order polynomial filter of the iteration matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_{k+1}=((1-\alpha+\beta)I+\alpha M)e_k-\beta e_{k-1}\).

children.title: State-Augmented Error Dynamics

knowledge_statements.title: State-Augmented Error Dynamics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Companion-matrix representation of two-step affine fixed-point error dynamics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the two-step error recurrence is \(e_{k+1}=He_k-\beta e_{k-1}\), where \(H=(1-\alpha+\beta)I+\alpha M\). Introduce the augmented state \(z_k=(e_k,e_{k-1})\). Then \[z_{k+1}=\mathcal H z_k,\qquad \mathcal H=\begin{pmatrix}H&-\beta I\\ I&0\end{pmatrix}.\] Consequently, in finite dimensions the two-step iteration converges to the fixed point for every initial augmented state if and only if \(\rho(\mathcal H)<1\). For an eigenvalue \(\lambda\) of \(M\), the associated scalar mode has characteristic equation \[r^2-(1-\alpha+\beta+\alpha\lambda)r+\beta=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stacking consecutive errors converts a two-step method into a first-order companion system whose spectral radius exactly determines convergence for every initial augmented state.
assumptions_latex: The underlying fixed-point map is affine with linear part \(M\).
The state space is finite dimensional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The error dynamics converge for all initial augmented states exactly when \(\rho(\mathcal H)<1\).

notation.meaning: spectral radius of the augmented dynamics

children.title: Nonlinear GMRES
children.top_down_role: Nonlinear minimization over recent solver-generated subspaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear GMRES
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-minimizing nonlinear GMRES with a solver-generated affine search space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) and let \(M:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be a base nonlinear solver. Given \(x_k\) and memory \(m_k\), form \(y_k=M(x_k)\) and \(S_k=[y_k-x_k,\,x_k-x_{k-1},\ldots,x_{k-m_k+1}-x_{k-m_k}]\). Choose \(\alpha_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\in\mathbb{R}^{m_k+1}}\|F(y_k+S_k\alpha)\|_2\), exactly or approximately. Set \(x_{k+1}=y_k+S_k\alpha_k\), optionally accepting a safeguarded point on the segment from \(y_k\) to this candidate. Stop when \(\|F(x_{k+1})\|_2\leq\varepsilon\), and return \(x_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonlinear GMRES minimizes the residual over an affine space generated by a base-solver step and recent iterate differences, with optional safeguarding.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(M\) are defined at every trial point.
The residual minimization admits a computed approximate minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}\in y_k+\operatorname{range}(S_k)\) is selected to reduce \(\|F\|_2\) over the current solver-generated affine space.
review_flags: Exact N-GMRES variants differ in subspace construction, nonlinear least-squares approximation, and globalization.
A method-specific authoritative source and locator are required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the Nonlinear GMRES leaf, but no method-specific source or locator is supplied. The statement also places alpha_k in an exact argmin while allowing an approximate minimizer, and neither an arbitrary approximate solve nor the optional segment safeguard guarantees residual reduction. The search-matrix indexing and globalization convention require authoritative variant-specific correction.

children.title: Nonlinear GCR
children.top_down_role: Conjugate-residual-inspired nonlinear acceleration.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear GCR
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-memory nonlinear GCR based on residual changes along generated directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), choose \(x_0\), and set \(r_0=F(x_0)\). At iteration \(k\), obtain a nonzero trial direction \(p_k\), compute \(q_k=F(x_k+p_k)-F(x_k)\), and orthogonalize the pair against all stored residual-change vectors: for \(j<k\), set \(\beta_{jk}=-\langle q_j,q_k\rangle/\langle q_j,q_j\rangle\), then replace \(p_k\) by \(p_k+\sum_{j<k}\beta_{jk}p_j\) and recompute \(q_k=F(x_k+p_k)-F(x_k)\). Choose \(\alpha_k\) to minimize \(\|F(x_k+\alpha p_k)\|_2\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), and stop when the residual tolerance holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonlinear GCR generates directions whose nonlinear residual changes are conjugate-like, then performs residual minimization along each new direction.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is evaluable at all trial points.
Each one-dimensional residual minimization produces an acceptable step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stored residual-change vectors are orthogonalized, and \(x_{k+1}\) minimizes or approximately minimizes the residual norm along \(x_k+\operatorname{span}\{p_k\}\).

notation.meaning: residual change associated with the direction

review_flags: Nonlinear GCR has multiple nonequivalent recurrences and orthogonalization conventions.
The stated finite-difference residual-change version requires authoritative sourcing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the Nonlinear GCR leaf, but no source supports this particular recurrence. Coefficients computed from the initial residual change do not generally make the residual change recomputed after the combined nonlinear direction orthogonal to the stored vectors. A method-specific source is needed to determine the correct sequential orthogonalization and residual-update convention.

children.title: Truncated Nonlinear GCR
children.top_down_role: Bounded-memory nonlinear residual-subspace acceleration.

knowledge_statements.title: Truncated Nonlinear GCR
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-memory nonlinear GCR retaining only the most recent residual-change pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a memory bound \(m\geq1\). At iteration \(k\), generate a trial direction \(p_k\) and its residual change \(q_k=F(x_k+p_k)-F(x_k)\). With \(J_k=\{\max(0,k-m),\ldots,k-1\}\), orthogonalize using only retained pairs: set \(\beta_{jk}=-\langle q_j,q_k\rangle/\langle q_j,q_j\rangle\) for \(j\in J_k\), update \(p_k\leftarrow p_k+\sum_{j\in J_k}\beta_{jk}p_j\), and recompute \(q_k\). Choose \(\alpha_k\) by minimizing or sufficiently reducing \(\|F(x_k+\alpha p_k)\|_2\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), and discard pairs older than \(m\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Truncated nonlinear GCR applies GCR-style residual-change orthogonalization against at most the latest m stored pairs, bounding storage and orthogonalization work.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is evaluable at all trial points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At most \(m\) prior pairs are retained, so stored-vector memory is \(O(mn)\) while residual minimization remains restricted to generated directions.

notation.meaning: maximum number of retained prior pairs
indices of retained pairs at iteration k

review_flags: Truncation and nonlinear residual-change conventions vary across nonlinear GCR formulations.

children.title: Sequence-Acceleration Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Error-model and numerical boundaries of sequence and polynomial acceleration.

children.title: Asymptotic-Model Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Failure when the observed sequence lacks the presumed error structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic-Model Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a linear-recurrence extrapolator when sequence errors do not obey its presumed model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_n=s+e_n\), and suppose an extrapolator chooses coefficients \(c_0,\ldots,c_m\) satisfying \(\sum_{j=0}^m c_j=1\) and the model-cancellation equations \(\sum_{j=0}^m c_j\lambda_i^j=0\) for prescribed modes \(\lambda_i\). Its transformed error is \(\widehat s_n-s=\sum_{j=0}^m c_je_{n+j}\). If the actual errors cannot be decomposed as \(e_{n+j}=\sum_i a_i\lambda_i^j+\delta_{n,j}\) with \(\|\sum_jc_j\delta_{n,j}\|<\|e_n\|\), then the cancellation model gives no acceleration guarantee; in particular, \(\|\widehat s_n-s\|\geq\|e_n\|\) is possible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cancellation of assumed asymptotic modes does not ensure acceleration when the actual error contains a sufficiently large unmodeled component.
assumptions_latex: \(s_n\) lies in a normed vector space and converges to \(s\).
The coefficients satisfy the stated affine and model-cancellation equations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Model mismatch can yield \(\|\widehat s_n-s\|\geq\|s_n-s\|\), so the extrapolator need not accelerate the sequence.
review_flags: The algebraic failure mechanism is standard, but no supplied locator specifically supports sequence-model mismatch.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind matches the leaf and the cancellation mechanism is plausible, but no supporting locator is supplied. The index set for the prescribed modes and the domains of the mode amplitudes are not introduced, so an authoritative source is needed to fix the exact model-mismatch condition and its quantifiers.

children.title: Recursive Transformation Breakdown Regimes
children.top_down_role: Instability of recursive sequence transformations.

children.title: Small-Denominator Instability
children.top_down_role: Instability caused by poorly scaled denominators in recursive transformations.

knowledge_statements.title: Small-Denominator Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instability of Aitken-type recursive transformations near a vanishing second difference.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a scalar sequence \(s_n\), Aitken's transformation is \(T_n=s_n-(\Delta s_n)^2/\Delta^2s_n\), where \(\Delta s_n=s_{n+1}-s_n\) and \(\Delta^2s_n=s_{n+2}-2s_{n+1}+s_n\). If computed data are perturbed by \(|\eta_j|\leq u\), the denominator perturbation can have magnitude at most \(4u\). Hence, when \(|\Delta^2s_n|\) is comparable to or smaller than \(4u\), its relative error is uncontrolled; if simultaneously \(|\Delta s_n|\) is not small, the quotient may become arbitrarily large. Exact vanishing with \(\Delta s_n\neq0\) causes breakdown.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aitken acceleration becomes unstable when its second-difference denominator is at the noise scale, and breaks down when that denominator vanishes.
assumptions_latex: The observed values are \(\widetilde s_j=s_j+\eta_j\) with \(|\eta_j|\leq u\).
Arithmetic after data acquisition is treated as exact for this sensitivity statement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(|\Delta^2s_n|\lesssim4u\), the transformed value is ill-conditioned; if \(\Delta^2s_n=0\) and \(\Delta s_n\neq0\), it is undefined.
review_flags: A source specifically treating recursive sequence-transformation breakdown was not supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the leaf, and the 4u absolute perturbation bound for the second difference is algebraically consistent. However, no cited source with a specific locator supports the conditioning and breakdown interpretation for this recursive transformation.

children.title: Near-Breakdown Regimes
children.top_down_role: Numerical regimes approaching loss of a reliable extrapolation transform.

knowledge_statements.title: Near-Breakdown Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-aware near-breakdown condition for quotient-based recursive sequence transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a transformation step \(T=N/D\) evaluated from observed data, with perturbation bounds \(|\delta N|\leq\eta_N\) and \(|\delta D|\leq\eta_D\). For a prescribed safety factor \(\tau>1\), the step is in a near-breakdown regime when \(|D|\leq\tau\eta_D\), or when the first-order relative sensitivity indicator \(\kappa_T=\eta_N/|N|+\eta_D/|D|\) exceeds a chosen tolerance. In this regime the perturbed denominator may approach or cross zero, and the relative error of \(T\) is not reliably controlled even though \(D\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near-breakdown occurs when a recursive transformation denominator is not safely separated from its perturbation scale or its estimated relative sensitivity is excessive.
assumptions_latex: \(N\neq0\), \(D\neq0\), and finite perturbation bounds are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The predicate \(|D|\leq\tau\eta_D\) or excessive \(\kappa_T\) identifies a numerically unsafe, though not necessarily exact, breakdown regime.

notation.meaning: numerator and denominator of one transformation step

review_flags: The safety factor and indicator are implementation-dependent.
A numerical sequence-transformation source is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits a near-breakdown container, but the predicate is an implementation-defined safeguard rather than a source-established universal condition. The first-order indicator is stated without a small-perturbation qualification, and the tolerance is not defined. A numerical-analysis source is required to establish a defensible formulation.

children.title: Breakdown Detection Indicators
children.top_down_role: Observable indicators used to recognize impending transformation failure.

knowledge_statements.title: Breakdown Detection Indicators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable certificate for rejecting an unsafe quotient-based transformation step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a computed transformation \(T=N/D\), let \(\widehat D\) be the evaluated denominator, let \(b_D\) bound its absolute evaluation error, and choose \(\tau>1\). The indicator \(\chi_D=|\widehat D|/(b_D+u_D)\), where \(u_D>0\) is a rounding-scale floor, certifies numerical breakdown when \(\widehat D=0\) and flags near-breakdown when \(\chi_D\leq\tau\). A second verifiable flag is excessive amplification \(\chi_A=|N/D|/S\geq\Gamma\), where \(S>0\) is a local data scale and \(\Gamma\) is a prescribed cap. A flagged step must be rejected, restarted, or replaced by an untransformed value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Denominator separation and output-amplification ratios provide computable indicators for rejecting exact or near breakdown in quotient-based transformations.
assumptions_latex: Valid bounds \(b_D\) and positive scales \(u_D,S\) are computable.
Thresholds \(\tau>1\) and \(\Gamma>1\) are fixed in advance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tests \(\widehat D=0\), \(\chi_D\leq\tau\), or \(\chi_A\geq\Gamma\) provide directly verifiable breakdown warnings.
review_flags: Threshold choices are safeguards rather than universal constants.
A source supporting these specific indicators is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind is appropriate for a detection-indicator leaf, but the proposed ratios, rounding floor, scale, thresholds, and mandatory response are unsourced safeguards rather than a recognized certificate. The amplification test also mixes the computed setting with the notation N/D without identifying evaluated quantities. A source is needed before selecting the exact indicators.

children.title: Pseudospectral Acceleration Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Polynomial-acceleration failures not predicted by eigenvalue-only models.

children.title: Nonnormal Transients
children.top_down_role: Short- or medium-horizon growth caused by nonnormal iteration structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonnormal Transients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stable eigenvalues do not preclude large transient errors for a nonnormal fixed-point linearization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<\lambda<1\) and \(K>0\), let \(A=\begin{pmatrix}\lambda&K\\0&\lambda\end{pmatrix}\). Then \(\rho(A)=\lambda<1\), but \(A^k=\begin{pmatrix}\lambda^k&kK\lambda^{k-1}\\0&\lambda^k\end{pmatrix}\). With \(e_0=(0,1)^{\mathsf T}\), one has \(\|A^ke_0\|_2\geq kK\lambda^{k-1}\), which can be arbitrarily large for fixed \(k\) as \(K\to\infty\), despite eventual convergence to zero. Thus eigenvalue-based asymptotic models can severely underestimate intermediate error growth and destabilize finite-window acceleration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stable nonnormal iteration matrix can amplify errors arbitrarily before convergence, invalidating acceleration predictions based only on eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Although \(\rho(A)<1\), the transient amplification \(\|A^ke_0\|_2\) is unbounded as \(K\to\infty\) for every fixed \(k\geq1\).
review_flags: The counterexample is explicit, but no supplied source locator addresses nonnormal transient growth.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample kind fits this leaf, and the Jordan-block calculation correctly demonstrates arbitrarily large finite-time amplification despite spectral stability. No source locator is supplied, however, and the additional claim that this behavior destabilizes finite-window acceleration is not established by the counterexample alone.

children.title: Spectral-Model Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Failure of eigenvalue-only models to predict accelerator behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral-Model Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of eigenvalue-only polynomial predictions for nonnormal fixed-point iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the linear error iteration \(e_{k+1}=Ae_k\), a degree-\(m\) polynomial extrapolator produces an error of the form \(p(A)e_k\), with \(p(1)=1\) under the usual affine constraint. If \(A\) is normal, then \(\|p(A)\|_2=\max_{\lambda\in\sigma(A)}|p(\lambda)|\). For nonnormal \(A\), this equality can fail by an arbitrarily large factor. Consequently, selecting \(p\) solely by minimizing its magnitude on an assumed spectral set does not control \(\|p(A)e_k\|_2\) unless normality, diagonalization conditioning, or a stronger functional-calculus bound is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomial acceleration designed only from eigenvalues may fail for nonnormal iterations because polynomial matrix norms can greatly exceed spectral values.
assumptions_latex: The local error propagation is linear with matrix \(A\).
The extrapolated error is representable as \(p(A)e_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without additional control of nonnormality, \(\max_{\lambda\in\sigma(A)}|p(\lambda)|\) is not a reliable bound for \(\|p(A)\|_2\).
review_flags: A source on polynomial bounds for nonnormal matrices is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind matches the leaf and the normal-versus-nonnormal distinction is mathematically standard. No authoritative locator is supplied for the polynomial norm claim, its arbitrarily large discrepancy, or the conditions under which diagonalization or stronger functional-calculus bounds restore control.

children.title: Pseudospectral Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity information relevant when spectral predictions are unreliable.

knowledge_statements.title: Pseudospectral Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pseudospectral control of polynomial amplification for nonnormal iteration matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}\) and \(\varepsilon>0\), define \(\sigma_\varepsilon(A)=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:\|(zI-A)^{-1}\|_2>\varepsilon^{-1}\}\), including \(\sigma(A)\). If a polynomial \(p\) is used in a residual or error extrapolation, then large values of \(|p(z)|\) on \(\sigma_\varepsilon(A)\) signal sensitivity to perturbations of size below \(\varepsilon\). When \(\sigma_\varepsilon(A)\) extends far beyond \(\sigma(A)\), small perturbations can move eigenvalues into regions where \(|p|\) is large, so eigenvalue-optimized acceleration lacks robustness even if \(|p|\) is small on \(\sigma(A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Broad pseudospectra reveal that small perturbations can expose large polynomial amplification missed by eigenvalue-only acceleration models.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is the polynomial induced by the acceleration step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A large pseudospectral extent makes spectral polynomial acceleration perturbation-sensitive unless \(|p|\) is controlled on an appropriate \(\sigma_\varepsilon(A)\).
review_flags: The pseudospectral interpretation is standard, but no relevant authoritative locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the leaf, but no authoritative pseudospectral source is cited. The definition should explicitly use a union with sigma(A), since the resolvent expression is not defined on the spectrum, and the perturbation interpretation requires a stated matrix-norm convention and source.

children.title: Extrapolation Noise Amplification
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of transformed sequences to evaluation and rounding errors.

knowledge_statements.title: Extrapolation Noise Amplification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case propagation of bounded evaluation noise through affine sequence extrapolation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let observed vectors be \(\widetilde s_j=s_j+\eta_j\) in a normed vector space, with \(\|\eta_j\|\leq\delta_j\), and let an affine extrapolator return \(\widetilde t=\sum_{j=0}^m c_j\widetilde s_j\), where \(\sum_{j=0}^m c_j=1\). Relative to the exact-data transform \(t=\sum_{j=0}^m c_js_j\), the perturbation satisfies \(\|\widetilde t-t\|\leq\sum_{j=0}^m|c_j|\delta_j\). For a common bound \(\delta_j\leq\delta\), the noise amplification factor is at most \(\|c\|_1\), and this bound is attainable for aligned scalar perturbations. Large extrapolation coefficients therefore amplify noise and rounding errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine extrapolator amplifies bounded input noise by its coefficient one-norm, with the worst-case bound attained by aligned errors.
assumptions_latex: The sequence values lie in a normed vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\widetilde t-t\|\leq\sum_j|c_j|\delta_j\leq\|c\|_1\max_j\delta_j\).

children.title: Anderson Formulations
children.top_down_role: Equivalent algebraic formulations used in theory and implementation.

children.title: Affine Residual-Mixing Form
children.top_down_role: Original affine-combination view of residual mixing.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Residual-Mixing Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constrained affine residual minimization followed by mixing of fixed-point images.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), define \(f_i=G(x_i)-x_i\), and choose a memory bound \(m\). At iteration \(k\), set \(I_k=\{k-m_k,\ldots,k\}\), where \(m_k=\min(m,k)\). Compute \(\alpha^{(k)}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha}\|\sum_{i\in I_k}\alpha_if_i\|_2\) subject to \(\sum_{i\in I_k}\alpha_i=1\). For mixing parameter \(\beta_k\in(0,1]\), update \(x_{k+1}=\sum_{i\in I_k}\alpha_i^{(k)}[(1-\beta_k)x_i+\beta_kG(x_i)]\). Stop when \(\|f_{k+1}\|_2\leq\varepsilon\), and return \(x_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Anderson residual mixing chooses an affine combination minimizing stored residuals, then combines the corresponding damped fixed-point images.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is defined at all stored and generated iterates.
The constrained least-squares problem has a selected minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coefficients minimize the norm of the affine residual combination, and the next iterate is the matching affine combination of damped fixed-point images.
review_flags: The supplied fixed-point and acceleration locators do not specifically identify Anderson's affine formulation.
An Anderson-acceleration source with an exact algorithm locator is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind correctly matches the affine residual-mixing formulation leaf, and the displayed update resembles a standard damped Anderson form. No Anderson-acceleration source or exact algorithm locator is supplied, so the residual sign, damping placement, history convention, and least-squares formulation cannot be accepted as a specific sourced variant.

children.title: Difference-Basis Form
children.top_down_role: Residual- and iterate-difference formulation used in limited-memory implementations.

knowledge_statements.title: Difference-Basis Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Undamped Type-II Anderson iteration expressed through recent iterate and residual differences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), \(r(x)=x-G(x)\), and \(m_k=\min\{m,k\}\). Form \(X_k=[x_{k-m_k+1}-x_{k-m_k},\ldots,x_k-x_{k-1}]\) and \(R_k=[r_{k-m_k+1}-r_{k-m_k},\ldots,r_k-r_{k-1}]\), where \(r_j=r(x_j)\). Choose \(\gamma_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\gamma\in\mathbb{R}^{m_k}}\|r_k-R_k\gamma\|_2\), and set \[x_{k+1}=x_k-r_k-(X_k-R_k)\gamma_k.\] For \(m_k=0\), set \(x_{k+1}=G(x_k)\). Stop when a prescribed residual or step tolerance is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize the current residual over recent residual differences, then apply the corresponding correction formed from iterate and residual differences.
assumptions_latex: \(G:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is evaluable at every generated iterate.
The least-squares problem is solved using a specified minimum-norm convention if its minimizer is nonunique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k-r_k-(X_k-R_k)\gamma_k\).
review_flags: exact Anderson difference-basis formula lacks a supplied supporting locator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the difference-basis leaf, and the sign convention is internally consistent with r(x)=x-G(x). However, no citation or inspectable locator supports the exact Type-II difference-basis formula, so the record cannot be accepted as candidate-review knowledge.

children.title: Multisecant Inverse-Model Form
children.top_down_role: Quasi-Newton interpretation based on simultaneous secant information.

knowledge_statements.title: Multisecant Inverse-Model Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Type-II Anderson represented as a minimum-change inverse residual-Jacobian model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r(x)=x-G(x)\), and let \(X_k,R_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\) collect matched iterate and residual differences. If \(R_k\) has full column rank, define \[H_k=I+(X_k-R_k)(R_k^{\mathsf T}R_k)^{-1}R_k^{\mathsf T}.\] Then \(H_kR_k=X_k\), and \(H_k\) is the unique minimizer of \(\|H-I\|_F\) subject to \(HR_k=X_k\). The inverse-model step \(x_{k+1}=x_k-H_kr_k\) equals \(x_k-r_k-(X_k-R_k)\gamma_k\), where \(\gamma_k=(R_k^{\mathsf T}R_k)^{-1}R_k^{\mathsf T}r_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Anderson’s Type-II step applies the minimum-change inverse model satisfying all stored residual-to-iterate secant equations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_kR_k=X_k\) and \(x_{k+1}=x_k-H_kr_k\).
review_flags: minimum-change multisecant characterization lacks a supplied supporting locator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the multisecant inverse-model leaf. The displayed full-column-rank formula, multisecant identity, and Frobenius minimum-change characterization are mathematically coherent, but the exact characterization and its association with Type-II Anderson require a supporting source and specific locator.

children.title: Nonlinear Residual-Minimization Form
children.top_down_role: Local residual-model interpretation connecting Anderson and nonlinear least squares.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Residual-Minimization Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact residual minimization over the affine space generated by recent iterate differences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r(x)=x-G(x)\), and let \(X_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\) contain recent iterate differences. Compute \[\gamma_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\gamma\in\mathbb{R}^{p}}\|r(x_k-X_k\gamma)\|_2,\qquad z_k=x_k-X_k\gamma_k,\] and output \(x_{k+1}=G(z_k)\). Stop when \(\|r(z_k)\|_2\) or \(\|x_{k+1}-z_k\|_2\) meets the prescribed tolerance. Replacing \(r(x_k-X_k\gamma)\) by its multisecant model \(r_k-R_k\gamma\) produces the usual Anderson least-squares coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exactly minimize the nonlinear residual over a recent affine trial space; linearizing that residual model yields Anderson’s standard least-squares subproblem.
assumptions_latex: \(G:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is evaluable on the trial affine space.
The displayed nonlinear least-squares problem has a selected minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=G(x_k-X_k\gamma_k)\).
review_flags: exact trial-space convention requires a supporting source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind is plausible for this formulation leaf, but exact nonlinear residual minimization over x_k-range(X_k), followed by G, is not a uniquely standard Anderson formulation. A source is required to establish this trial-space convention and the claimed connection to the usual Anderson least-squares model.

children.title: Anderson Variant Families
children.top_down_role: Algebraic, memory, damping, and metric variants of Anderson acceleration.

children.title: Type-I Anderson Acceleration
children.top_down_role: Jacobian-oriented member of the Anderson family.

knowledge_statements.title: Type-I Anderson Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Jacobian-oriented multisecant Anderson method with an identity baseline model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r(x)=x-G(x)\), and form matched difference matrices \(X_k,R_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\). When \(X_k\) has full column rank, define \[B_k=I+(R_k-X_k)(X_k^{\mathsf T}X_k)^{-1}X_k^{\mathsf T}.\] This matrix satisfies \(B_kX_k=R_k\) and minimizes \(\|B-I\|_F\) subject to those multisecant equations. Compute \(s_k\) from \(B_ks_k=-r_k\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\), and stop under a prescribed residual or step test. Rank loss requires truncation, restart, or regularized solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build the minimum-change residual-Jacobian model satisfying stored secant equations, then take its quasi-Newton step.
assumptions_latex: \(B_ks=-r_k\) is solvable under the stated implementation convention.
review_flags: Type-I naming and baseline conventions vary across sources
exact formula lacks a supplied supporting locator

Nevertheless, Type-I naming and baseline conventions vary, no source is supplied, and the conclusion writes B_k^{-1} although the assumptions establish only solvability under an unspecified convention rather than invertibility.

children.title: Type-II Anderson Acceleration

knowledge_statements.title: Type-II Anderson Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse-Jacobian-oriented multisecant Anderson method with an identity baseline model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r(x)=x-G(x)\), and form matched difference matrices \(X_k,R_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\). When \(R_k\) has full column rank, define \[H_k=I+(X_k-R_k)(R_k^{\mathsf T}R_k)^{-1}R_k^{\mathsf T}.\] This matrix satisfies \(H_kR_k=X_k\) and minimizes \(\|H-I\|_F\) subject to those inverse multisecant equations. Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k-H_kr_k\), equivalently using the residual-difference least-squares coefficients, and stop under a prescribed residual or step test.

children.title: Finite-Window Anderson Acceleration
children.top_down_role: Bounded-history family for storage-controlled acceleration.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Window Anderson Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Anderson acceleration retaining at most a prescribed number of recent difference pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a memory bound \(m\geq 0\). At iteration \(k\), let \(p_k=\min\{m,k\}\), retain only the latest \(p_k\) columns in \(X_k\) and \(R_k\), and solve \(\gamma_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\gamma\in\mathbb{R}^{p_k}}\|r_k-R_k\gamma\|_2\). Set \[x_{k+1}=x_k-r_k-(X_k-R_k)\gamma_k.\] When \(p_k=0\), use \(x_{k+1}=G(x_k)\). Thus coefficient storage is at most \(m\), while storing dense history matrices requires at most \(2mn\) scalars, apart from current vectors and factorization workspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply Anderson acceleration using only the newest bounded number of iterate and residual differences.
assumptions_latex: A minimum-norm least-squares convention is used when necessary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_k\leq m\) and \(x_{k+1}=x_k-r_k-(X_k-R_k)\gamma_k\).

children.title: Restarted Anderson Acceleration

knowledge_statements.title: Restarted Anderson Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Anderson acceleration with periodic or condition-triggered deletion of accumulated history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{T}\) be a prescribed restart rule depending only on available iteration data. Before iteration \(k\), if \(\mathcal{T}(k,x_k,r_k,X_k,R_k)=1\), replace \(X_k\) and \(R_k\) by matrices with zero columns. Compute the next iterate from the remaining history by \(\gamma_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\gamma}\|r_k-R_k\gamma\|_2\) and \[x_{k+1}=x_k-r_k-(X_k-R_k)\gamma_k.\] A periodic restart uses \(\mathcal{T}=1\) whenever \(k\) is a positive multiple of a fixed period; triggered variants may restart after rank, conditioning, or acceptance tests fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Erase Anderson history on a fixed schedule or a specified diagnostic event, then resume acceleration from the base fixed-point step.
assumptions_latex: The restart predicate is specified before execution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{T}=1\) implies an empty-history step \(x_{k+1}=G(x_k)\).
review_flags: restart triggers are family-defining rather than canonical
supporting Anderson restart source is absent
