children.title: Damped Anderson Acceleration
children.top_down_role: Mixing families that moderate aggressive extrapolation.

knowledge_statements.title: Damped Anderson Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Type-II difference-basis iteration with a controlled base fixed-point relaxation parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r(x)=x-G(x)\), choose \(\beta_k\in(0,1]\), and compute \(\gamma_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\gamma}\|r_k-R_k\gamma\|_2\) from the retained history. Define \[x_{k+1}=x_k-\beta_kr_k-(X_k-\beta_kR_k)\gamma_k.\] With empty history this is the relaxed fixed-point step \(x_{k+1}=(1-\beta_k)x_k+\beta_kG(x_k)\); with \(\beta_k=1\) it reduces to the undamped difference-basis form. The sequence \((\beta_k)\) may be fixed or selected by a prescribed acceptance rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scale the base fixed-point component and its matching residual-difference correction to moderate Anderson extrapolation.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\beta_k\leq1\) is fixed or chosen by a specified rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\beta_kr_k-(X_k-\beta_kR_k)\gamma_k\).
review_flags: damping conventions vary between coefficient mixing and step relaxation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the damped-family leaf, and the displayed update has the claimed empty-history and beta_k=1 reductions. Because Anderson damping may instead act on affine coefficients, extrapolated points, or accepted steps, the selected convention requires an authoritative source and locator.

children.title: Regularized Anderson Acceleration
children.top_down_role: Stabilized coefficient models for ill-conditioned residual histories.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Anderson Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ridge-regularized residual-difference coefficients for rank-deficient or ill-conditioned histories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r(x)=x-G(x)\), retain difference matrices \(X_k,R_k\), and choose \(\lambda_k>0\). Compute the unique coefficient vector \[\gamma_k=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\gamma}\bigl(\|r_k-R_k\gamma\|_2^2+\lambda_k\|\gamma\|_2^2\bigr),\] equivalently \(\gamma_k=(R_k^{\mathsf T}R_k+\lambda_kI)^{-1}R_k^{\mathsf T}r_k\), and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k-r_k-(X_k-R_k)\gamma_k\). Stop under a prescribed residual or step test. The positive regularization makes the coefficient normal matrix positive definite even when \(R_k\) is rank deficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add a positive quadratic penalty to the Anderson coefficient fit, ensuring a unique stabilized solution for ill-conditioned histories.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_k=(R_k^{\mathsf T}R_k+\lambda_kI)^{-1}R_k^{\mathsf T}r_k\).
review_flags: regularized Anderson formula lacks a supplied supporting locator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the regularized-family leaf. The ridge subproblem, normal-equation formula, uniqueness, and positive-definiteness claim are mathematically consistent for lambda_k>0, but no source identifies this exact ridge coefficient model as the intended regularized Anderson variant.

children.title: Metric-Aware Anderson Family
children.top_down_role: Metric-aware families for heterogeneous residual components.

children.title: Weighted Anderson Acceleration
children.top_down_role: Anderson variants using weighted residual metrics.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Anderson Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Anderson coefficient fitting in a fixed symmetric positive-definite residual metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite and define \(\|v\|_W^2=v^{\mathsf T}Wv\). Given \(r(x)=x-G(x)\) and history matrices \(X_k,R_k\), compute \[\gamma_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\gamma}\|r_k-R_k\gamma\|_W^2\] and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k-r_k-(X_k-R_k)\gamma_k\). If \(R_k^{\mathsf T}WR_k\) is nonsingular, then \(\gamma_k=(R_k^{\mathsf T}WR_k)^{-1}R_k^{\mathsf T}Wr_k\). For \(W=I\), the method is ordinary Euclidean Type-II Anderson acceleration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fit Anderson coefficients using a chosen positive-definite residual metric, then apply the usual difference-basis correction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\gamma}\|r_k-R_k\gamma\|_W^2\).
review_flags: weighted Anderson formulation lacks a supplied supporting locator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the weighted Anderson leaf. The SPD-weighted least-squares formula and Euclidean specialization are coherent, but the record lacks a citation and specific locator supporting this metric-weighted Anderson formulation.

children.title: Preconditioned Anderson Acceleration
children.top_down_role: Anderson variants transformed by residual or variable preconditioners.

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioned Anderson Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Anderson acceleration applied to a fixed-point map whose residual is left-preconditioned.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r(x)=x-G(x)\), choose a nonsingular linear preconditioner \(P\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), and define the preconditioned map \(G_P(x)=x-Pr(x)\) with residual \(q(x)=Pr(x)\). Form iterate differences \(X_k\) and preconditioned residual differences \(Q_k\). Compute \(\gamma_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\gamma}\|q_k-Q_k\gamma\|_2\), and set \[x_{k+1}=x_k-q_k-(X_k-Q_k)\gamma_k.\] With empty history, the update is \(x_{k+1}=x_k-Pr(x_k)\). Stop according to a prescribed norm of the original or preconditioned residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply Anderson acceleration to a preconditioned fixed-point map, using differences of the preconditioned residual in coefficient fitting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k-q_k-(X_k-Q_k)\gamma_k\), where \(q_k=Pr_k\).
review_flags: preconditioned Anderson has several inequivalent conventions
left-preconditioned-map version selected without a supporting locator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the preconditioned Anderson leaf, and applying the difference-basis method to G_P(x)=x-Pr(x) gives the stated update. Preconditioned Anderson has inequivalent left-, right-, nonlinear-, and variable-preconditioner conventions, so the fixed left-preconditioned-map interpretation requires a supporting source and locator.

children.title: Metric–Preconditioner Interaction
children.top_down_role: Compatibility between weighting choices and preconditioning transformations.

knowledge_statements.title: Metric–Preconditioner Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effective raw-residual metric induced by weighting a fixed left-preconditioned residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x)=Pr(x)\), let \(Q_k=PR_k\), and let \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) weight the preconditioned residual space. Then, for every coefficient vector \(\gamma\), \[\|q_k-Q_k\gamma\|_W^2=(r_k-R_k\gamma)^{\mathsf T}P^{\mathsf T}WP(r_k-R_k\gamma)=\|r_k-R_k\gamma\|_{P^{\mathsf T}WP}^2.\] If \(P\) is nonsingular, \(P^{\mathsf T}WP\) is symmetric positive definite. Hence weighting after left preconditioning is exactly equivalent, at the coefficient-fitting level, to weighting the original residual by the pullback metric \(P^{\mathsf T}WP\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighting preconditioned residuals is equivalent to weighting raw residuals by the pullback metric formed from the preconditioner and chosen weight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|q_k-Q_k\gamma\|_W=\|r_k-R_k\gamma\|_{P^{\mathsf T}WP}\).
review_flags: algebraic interaction is standard but no supplied locator addresses Anderson metrics and preconditioning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the metric-preconditioner interaction leaf. The pullback identity and positive definiteness of P^{\mathsf T}WP for nonsingular P are algebraically correct, but the evidence contract requires a source and specific locator for this nontrivial Anderson-specific interaction claim.

children.title: Anderson Equivalence Families
children.top_down_role: Linear and application-specific correspondences connecting Anderson with established accelerator families.

children.title: GMRES Equivalence Family
children.top_down_role: Full-memory linear correspondence with minimal-residual Krylov iteration.

assumptions_latex: The fixed-point map is affine: \(g(x)=Mx+b\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), with \(A=I-M\).
Anderson acceleration uses full history, type-II residual minimization, and unit mixing.
Before termination, the residual-difference matrices have the ranks required by the unconstrained least-squares problems.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_k=x_0+K_k(A,r_0)\) minimizes \(\lVert b-Az\rVert_2\) over \(x_0+K_k(A,r_0)\), and the corresponding Anderson update is \(x_{k+1}=g(z_k)\).

notation.meaning: Linear-system residual at the initial point

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Full-memory type-II Anderson acceleration for affine maps has the standard GMRES residual-minimization correspondence.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine, unrestarted, full-memory type-II correspondence before rank loss or Krylov stagnation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g(x)=Mx+b\), set \(A=I-M\), and define the fixed-point residual \(f(x)=g(x)-x=b-Ax\). Starting from \(x_0\), suppose full-memory type-II Anderson acceleration with unit mixing is well defined through step \(k\). Its affine residual-minimization point \(z_k\) satisfies
\[
z_k\in x_0+K_k(A,r_0),\qquad \lVert b-Az_k\rVert_2=\min_{z\in x_0+K_k(A,r_0)}\lVert b-Az\rVert_2,
\]
where \(r_0=f(x_0)\). Thus \(z_k\) is the unrestarted GMRES iterate for \(Ax=b\), and the Anderson iterate obeys \(x_{k+1}=g(z_k)\). The correspondence holds until exact convergence, rank loss, or GMRES stagnation invalidates the required coefficient identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an affine fixed-point problem, full-memory type-II Anderson acceleration computes the fixed-point image of the corresponding unrestarted GMRES residual minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: GMRES Equivalence Family

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No Anderson-specific citation supports the exact GMRES indexing, rank/stagnation boundaries, or update relation. Also, conclusion_latex incorrectly writes z_k=x_0+K_k(A,r_0); it must use set membership.

children.title: Arnoldi Equivalence Family
children.top_down_role: Type-I linear correspondence with full orthogonalization.

assumptions_latex: Type-I Anderson acceleration retains full history and uses unit mixing.
The projected Krylov systems and multisecant matrices remain nonsingular through the stated step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The type-I extrapolation point \(z_k\) is characterized by \(z_k\in x_0+K_k(A,r_0)\) and \(b-Az_k\perp K_k(A,r_0)\), and \(x_{k+1}=g(z_k)\).

notation.meaning: Linear operator associated with the affine fixed-point equation
Krylov subspace generated from the initial residual

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Full-memory type-I Anderson multisecant conditions correspond to a full-orthogonalization Krylov projection in the affine case.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine full-memory type-I correspondence with the full orthogonalization method, before breakdown.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g(x)=Mx+b\), \(A=I-M\), and \(r_0=b-Ax_0\). Assume full-memory type-I Anderson acceleration is well defined and its multisecant matrices have full required rank. Then its extrapolation point \(z_k\) is the full-orthogonalization Krylov point characterized by
\[
z_k\in x_0+K_k(A,r_0),\qquad b-Az_k\perp K_k(A,r_0).
\]
Equivalently, when an Arnoldi basis \(V_k\) is used, \(z_k=x_0+V_ky_k\), where \(y_k\) solves the projected system \(V_k^{\mathsf T}AV_k y_k=V_k^{\mathsf T}r_0\). The associated Anderson iterate is \(x_{k+1}=g(z_k)\). Breakdown or singularity of the projected system ends this equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an affine problem, full-memory type-I Anderson acceleration corresponds to a full-orthogonalization Krylov projection, provided its projected systems do not break down.
knowledge_statements.title: Arnoldi Equivalence Family

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The type-I Anderson/FOM correspondence, projected system, indexing, and breakdown hypotheses require a specific authoritative source. The theorem kind fits the equivalence-family container.

children.title: Anderson-Pulay Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between Anderson mixing and direct inversion in the iterative subspace.

children.title: Pulay DIIS
children.top_down_role: Direct inversion in the iterative subspace as a mixing family.

assumptions_latex: Stored vectors \(x_{k-m},\ldots,x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and residuals \(f_i=g(x_i)-x_i\) are available.
A norm or weighted norm used in the residual minimization is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is \(x_{k+1}=\sum_{i=k-m}^k c_i g(x_i)\), where \(c\) minimizes the combined residual subject to \(\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}c=1\).

notation.meaning: Fixed-point residual at stored iterate i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Pulay DIIS is conventionally formulated as constrained minimization of an affine combination of stored residuals.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-point form of Pulay direct inversion in the iterative subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given stored iterates \(x_{k-m},\ldots,x_k\), form residuals \(f_i=g(x_i)-x_i\) and \(F_k=[f_{k-m},\ldots,f_k]\). Compute
\[
c\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}d=1}\lVert F_kd\rVert_W,
\]
where \(\lVert v\rVert_W=(v^{\mathsf T}Wv)^{1/2}\) for a specified positive-definite weight \(W\); the Euclidean implementation takes \(W=I\). Set
\[
x_{k+1}=\sum_{i=k-m}^k c_i g(x_i).
\]
If the constrained problem is nonunique, a prescribed minimum-norm or rank-truncated solution must be selected. Stop when \(\lVert f_k\rVert_W\) meets the chosen tolerance, and return the current iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pulay DIIS minimizes an affine combination of stored residuals, then applies the same coefficients to the corresponding fixed-point images.
knowledge_statements.title: Pulay DIIS

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Pulay DIIS conventions differ over residual definitions and whether coefficients combine iterates, fixed-point images, or other trial vectors. A primary or authoritative source is required for this precise algorithm.

children.title: Anderson–Pulay Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between Anderson mixing and Pulay DIIS.

assumptions_latex: Both methods use the same iterate history, residual definition, norm, memory window, and coefficient-selection rule.
Anderson acceleration is written in its affine-combination form with unit mixing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pulay DIIS and affine-combination Anderson acceleration solve the same constrained problem and produce the same \(x_{k+1}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Anderson acceleration and Pulay DIIS share an algebraically identical constrained residual-minimization form under matched conventions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic correspondence under matched residual, metric, history, and mixing conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For residuals \(f_i=g(x_i)-x_i\), let \(F_k=[f_{k-m},\ldots,f_k]\). Pulay DIIS chooses
\[
c\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}d=1}\lVert F_kd\rVert_W
\]
and outputs \(\sum_i c_i g(x_i)\). Anderson acceleration in affine-combination form makes the same update when it uses the same stored indices, weight \(W\), unit mixing, and the same rule for resolving rank deficiency or nonuniqueness. Hence the two coefficient vectors and next iterates coincide whenever the constrained minimizer is uniquely selected. Difference-variable implementations of Anderson are equivalent after the standard elimination of the affine constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With identical residuals, history, metric, mixing, and rank handling, Pulay DIIS and affine-combination Anderson acceleration generate the same next iterate.
knowledge_statements.title: Anderson–Pulay Correspondence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The correspondence is plausible under matched conventions, but no citation supports the claimed identity or the difference-variable elimination. The property kind fits the correspondence container.

children.title: Anderson–Pulay Equivalence Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Modeling or implementation choices that limit the correspondence.

assumptions_latex: Pulay DIIS and Anderson acceleration are compared from the same current iterate.
At least one residual, metric, history, mixing, constraint, or rank-handling convention differs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coefficient problems need not coincide, so equality of the resulting next iterates is not guaranteed.

notation.meaning: Residual history used by one method

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Algebraic equivalence requires identical optimization problems and identical reconstruction rules.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions outside which the usual algebraic Anderson–Pulay identification does not apply.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Anderson–Pulay identification is not invariant under arbitrary implementation choices. It may fail when the methods use different residual maps, different weights \(W\), unequal history windows, regularized rather than unregularized least squares, distinct rank truncations, or different affine constraints. It also fails in general when Anderson uses damping \(\beta_k\ne1\) but Pulay DIIS applies the unmodified update \(\sum_i c_i g(x_i)\). In any such case, the two methods solve different coefficient problems or reconstruct different trial points. Consequently, even from identical stored iterates, their coefficients and next iterates need not agree; equivalence must be re-established for the particular conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Anderson–Pulay equivalence can fail when residuals, metrics, windows, regularization, rank decisions, affine constraints, or mixing rules differ.
knowledge_statements.title: Anderson–Pulay Equivalence Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but the listed convention changes and the nonunit-mixing claim need a source establishing the precise Anderson and Pulay formulations being compared.

children.title: Limited-Memory Equivalence Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits of full-memory Krylov correspondences under bounded histories and restarts.

children.title: Truncation Effects
children.top_down_role: Changes to Krylov correspondence caused by bounded history depth.

assumptions_latex: The affine problem is \(Ax=b\) with initial residual \(r_0=b-Ax_0\).
Anderson acceleration retains at most \(m\) residual or iterate differences, with \(m<k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At step \(k\), the Anderson search space generally has dimension at most \(m\) and need not equal \(x_0+K_k(A,r_0)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: A sliding window discards directions and therefore changes the full-memory Krylov search space.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of full Krylov correspondence caused by a fixed sliding history window.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the affine problem \(Ax=b\), full-memory Anderson acceleration can accumulate directions spanning \(K_k(A,r_0)\). If only the most recent \(m<k\) differences are retained, the coefficient problem is restricted to their span, whose dimension is at most \(m\). Unless the discarded directions lie in the retained span or are otherwise redundant, this moving subspace is not \(K_k(A,r_0)\). Therefore the limited-memory iterate need not minimize the residual over \(x_0+K_k(A,r_0)\), need not equal the corresponding unrestarted Krylov iterate, and may have a different residual norm. Truncation preserves the full-memory correspondence only in exceptional cases where deletion does not alter the effective search space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discarding old history restricts Anderson acceleration to a moving subspace, generally destroying its full unrestarted Krylov correspondence.
knowledge_statements.title: Truncation Effects

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A limited-memory Anderson source is needed for the asserted dimension bound and its relationship to the full Krylov affine space. The failure-boundary kind is appropriate.

children.title: Restart Effects
children.top_down_role: Changes to equivalence caused by periodic or triggered history resets.

assumptions_latex: All acceleration history is discarded at prescribed restart indices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After a restart at \(s\), subsequent search spaces are generated from \(r_s=b-Ax_s\), not from the complete space \(K_k(A,r_0)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Clearing Anderson history resets the associated Krylov construction at the current residual.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine correspondence between restarted Anderson history and restarted Krylov cycles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose all Anderson history is cleared at iteration \(s\) and acceleration resumes from \(x_s\). For an affine fixed-point map, the next cycle constructs directions from \(r_s=b-Ax_s\), so after \(j\) post-restart steps its full-cycle search space is contained in
\[
x_s+K_j(A,r_s).
\]
Under the same nonbreakdown hypotheses as the full-memory correspondence, that cycle matches the corresponding restarted Krylov cycle. It does not generally reproduce the unrestarted space \(x_0+K_{s+j}(A,r_0)\), because directions accumulated before \(s\) have been discarded. Consequently restart may delay convergence, alter residual minimization, and prevent finite termination at the unrestarted minimal-polynomial degree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restarting clears accumulated directions and begins a new Krylov-like cycle from the current residual, so unrestarted equivalence generally disappears.
knowledge_statements.title: Restart Effects

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reset-space observation is plausible, but exact equivalence to a restarted Krylov cycle and the finite-termination consequence require a cited theorem with matching indexing and nonbreakdown assumptions.

children.title: Full-Memory Correspondence Failure
children.top_down_role: Loss of full-memory Krylov interpretations under restricted histories.

assumptions_latex: The comparison is between an Anderson variant and an unrestarted full-memory Krylov method.
At least one full-memory correspondence hypothesis is violated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equality with the unrestarted Krylov iterate cannot be inferred and may fail at the first step affected by the violated hypothesis.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Full-memory Krylov equivalence depends on affinity, complete history, matching norms, mixing, and nonbreakdown.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Principal mechanisms invalidating exact full-memory Anderson–Krylov identities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Exact full-memory correspondence is not guaranteed if \(g\) is nonlinear, if a history limit \(m<k\) or restart deletes directions, if regularization changes the least-squares problem, if \(\beta_k\ne1\) changes reconstruction, or if rank loss or Krylov stagnation invalidates the coefficient mapping. In the nonlinear case, residual differences represent secants rather than repeated action of one fixed matrix \(A\), so they need not generate \(K_k(A,r_0)\) for any single \(A\). Under truncation or restart, the available span is smaller or differently based. Thus equality with an unrestarted GMRES, Arnoldi, or full-orthogonalization sequence cannot be concluded beyond the first affected step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonlinearity, truncation, restart, regularization, nonunit mixing, rank loss, or stagnation can invalidate exact full-memory Anderson–Krylov correspondence.
knowledge_statements.title: Full-Memory Correspondence Failure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits, but no source or explicit cited counterexample supports the combined claims about nonlinearity, truncation, regularization, mixing, rank loss, and stagnation.

children.title: Anderson Numerical Linear Algebra
children.top_down_role: Least-squares kernels, history maintenance, and rank control governing numerical reliability.

children.title: Least-Squares Kernels
children.top_down_role: Alternative numerical kernels for computing mixing coefficients.

children.title: Normal-Equation Implementations
children.top_down_role: Classical small-system implementation and its conditioning boundary.

assumptions_latex: The matrix \(F\) has full column rank in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Solving \((F^{\mathsf T}F)c=F^{\mathsf T}r\) yields the least-squares minimizer, but \(\kappa_2(F^{\mathsf T}F)=\kappa_2(F)^2\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Normal equations characterize full-rank least squares and square the spectral condition number.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal-equation kernel for an Anderson least-squares subproblem and its conditioning limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the Anderson least-squares problem \(\min_c\lVert r-Fc\rVert_2\), form the Gram matrix \(G=F^{\mathsf T}F\) and vector \(h=F^{\mathsf T}r\), solve
\[
Gc=h,
\]
and use \(c\) in the prescribed Anderson reconstruction. If \(F\) has full column rank, \(G\) is positive definite and this solution is the unique least-squares minimizer. However,
\[
\kappa_2(G)=\kappa_2(F)^2,
\]
so forming normal equations amplifies conditioning difficulties and can lose accuracy when residual-history columns are nearly dependent. A stable implementation should reject, regularize, or refactor the history when a condition or factorization diagnostic crosses its specified threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normal equations solve the small Anderson least-squares problem cheaply, but they square the history matrix's condition number and become unreliable near dependence.
knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Equation Implementations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normal-equation characterization and squared condition number are standard and correctly scoped to full column rank, but the record supplies no inspectable numerical-linear-algebra citation.

children.title: QR Implementations
children.top_down_role: Orthogonal-factorization implementations for stable residual-history processing.

assumptions_latex: A numerically stable QR factorization \(F=QR\) is maintained or computed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A least-squares coefficient vector satisfies \(Rc=Q^{\mathsf T}r\), with residual norm determined by the component orthogonal to \(\operatorname{range}(Q)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: QR reduction is the standard orthogonal-factorization solution of a full-rank least-squares problem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: QR-based solution of the small residual-history least-squares problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min_c\lVert r-Fc\rVert_2\), compute a thin QR factorization \(F=QR\), where \(Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I\) and \(R\) is upper triangular. If \(F\) has full column rank, solve
\[
Rc=Q^{\mathsf T}r
\]
by triangular substitution and use \(c\) in the Anderson update. The minimized residual satisfies
\[
\min_c\lVert r-Fc\rVert_2=\lVert (I-QQ^{\mathsf T})r\rVert_2.
\]
Householder QR or carefully reorthogonalized Gram–Schmidt avoids explicit formation of \(F^{\mathsf T}F\) and therefore does not square the conditioning of \(F\). Rank deficiency still requires pivoting, truncation, or another declared rank policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: QR solves Anderson's residual-history least squares through an orthogonal projection and triangular system without explicitly squaring the matrix conditioning.
knowledge_statements.title: QR Implementations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The QR least-squares algorithm is mathematically standard and fits the implementation leaf, but no source with a section, theorem, or page locator is cited.

children.title: Rank-Revealing Implementations
children.top_down_role: Rank-detection and truncation for dependent residual histories.

assumptions_latex: A rank threshold \(\tau>0\) and a rank-revealing factorization are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Retaining numerical rank \(r\) produces a reduced least-squares problem on an independent history subspace and discards directions below the declared threshold.

notation.meaning: Numerical rank selected by the threshold

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Pivoted QR and truncated SVD are standard rank-revealing least-squares kernels.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical-rank detection and history truncation for dependent Anderson residual differences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(\min_c\lVert b-Fc\rVert_2\), compute either a pivoted QR factorization \(F\Pi=QR\) or a singular value decomposition \(F=U\Sigma V^{\mathsf T}\). Select numerical rank \(r\) by a declared rule, such as \(\sigma_{r+1}\le\tau\sigma_1<\sigma_r\). Solve the reduced problem using only the retained factors; for truncated SVD,
\[
c_r=V_r\Sigma_r^{-1}U_r^{\mathsf T}b.
\]
Use \(c_r\), transformed back to the Anderson coefficient convention, for the update. The procedure removes unresolved or dependent history directions and bounds inversion to singular values larger than the threshold, but it changes the unregularized full-history step whenever truncation occurs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pivoted QR or truncated SVD detects dependent history, solves on the retained independent subspace, and makes the rank threshold explicit.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Revealing Implementations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but the pivoted-QR/SVD rank selection and truncation claims require an inspectable source. The singular-value threshold shown directly describes SVD, not by itself a pivoted-QR rank rule.

children.title: Moving-Window Factorizations
children.top_down_role: Factorization maintenance for bounded Anderson histories.

children.title: QR Downdating
children.top_down_role: Orthogonal-factorization maintenance as old history leaves the window.

assumptions_latex: A thin factorization \(F_k=Q_kR_k\) represents the current moving history window.
The oldest column is deleted and a new history column may subsequently be appended.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Orthogonal transformations restore triangular form after deletion, yielding a QR factorization of the shortened window without recomputing it from scratch.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: QR column deletion is performed by orthogonal transformations that chase the resulting bulge and restore triangular form.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stable maintenance of a QR factorization when the oldest Anderson history column leaves the window.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(F_k=Q_kR_k\) and the oldest column of \(F_k\) is removed. Delete the corresponding column of \(R_k\), producing a matrix that is generally upper Hessenberg rather than triangular. Apply a sequence of Givens rotations or Householder transformations from the left to eliminate its subdiagonal entries. Apply the same orthogonal transformations to \(Q_k\), implicitly when appropriate, obtaining
\[
F_k^{\mathrm{del}}=Q_k^{\mathrm{del}}R_k^{\mathrm{del}},
\]
with orthonormal \(Q_k^{\mathrm{del}}\) and upper-triangular \(R_k^{\mathrm{del}}\). A new column can then be orthogonalized and appended. Rank diagnostics on the updated diagonal determine whether reorthogonalization, truncation, or complete refactorization is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: QR downdating deletes an expired history column and uses orthogonal transformations to restore triangular form before the next column is appended.
knowledge_statements.title: QR Downdating

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches the QR-downdating leaf, but the column-deletion transformation and corresponding update of Q require a specific numerical-linear-algebra citation; the phrase 'same transformations to Q' also needs convention-level clarification.

children.title: Simple Downdating
children.top_down_role: Lower-overhead moving-window factorization maintenance.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G_{k+1}=\begin{bmatrix}G_k(2{:}m_k,2{:}m_k)&F_k(:,2{:}m_k)^{\mathsf T}\Delta f_k\\ \Delta f_k^{\mathsf T}F_k(:,2{:}m_k)&\|\Delta f_k\|_2^2\end{bmatrix}.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: deleting one history column deletes the corresponding Gram row and column before one bordered update
exact intended meaning of simple downdating requires an Anderson-specific source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal-equations downdating, not orthogonal-factor downdating.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(G_k=F_k^{\mathsf T}F_k\), delete the oldest history column and append \(\Delta f_k\). Without recomputing all inner products, form the next Gram matrix by deleting the first row and column of \(G_k\), computing the cross-products with the retained columns, and bordering the result:
\[
G_{k+1}=\begin{bmatrix}G_k(2{:}m_k,2{:}m_k)&F_k(:,2{:}m_k)^{\mathsf T}\Delta f_k\\ \Delta f_k^{\mathsf T}F_k(:,2{:}m_k)&\|\Delta f_k\|_2^2\end{bmatrix}.
\]
Solve the resulting small least-squares normal equations and discard the oldest stored difference when the window exceeds \(m_{\max}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete the oldest Gram row and column, append inner products involving the newest residual difference, and solve the updated small normal equations.
knowledge_statements.title: Simple Downdating

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No Anderson-specific citation is supplied. The displayed bordered formula is valid only when the oldest column is actually deleted, but the statement also covers a growing window before the cap is reached; that case requires appending without deleting the first Gram row and column. A source is also needed for the intended normal-equations implementation.

children.title: Truncated Gram–Schmidt Anderson
children.top_down_role: Windowed orthogonalization variant avoiding full QR downdating.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q_{\mathrm{new}}=v/\|v\|_2\quad\text{when}\quad \|v\|_2>\tau\|\Delta f_k\|_2.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: windowed modified Gram-Schmidt is a standard incremental least-squares implementation
Anderson-specific recurrence and reorthogonalization convention need source confirmation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed modified Gram–Schmidt realization of Anderson least squares.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain orthonormal columns \(Q_k=[q_1,\ldots,q_{m_k}]\) for the active residual-difference window. If \(m_k=m_{\max}\), discard the oldest stored history direction. For the newest difference, set \(v=\Delta f_k\) and perform modified Gram–Schmidt over the retained columns: \(h_j=q_j^{\mathsf T}v\) and \(v\leftarrow v-q_jh_j\). If \(\|v\|_2>\tau\|\Delta f_k\|_2\), append \(q_{\mathrm{new}}=v/\|v\|_2\) and its triangular coefficients; otherwise reject the dependent direction. Compute the Anderson coefficients from the resulting reduced triangular least-squares problem and output the corresponding accelerated iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discard expired history, orthogonalize the newest residual difference against retained directions, reject near dependence, and solve the reduced triangular Anderson problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Truncated Gram–Schmidt Anderson

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but deleting the oldest basis vector from a sequential Gram–Schmidt factorization does not by itself establish a valid factorization of the retained raw history columns. An Anderson-specific recurrence, triangular-factor update, and reorthogonalization convention must be sourced.

children.title: Anderson History Conditioning System
children.top_down_role: Mechanisms for retaining informative residual differences.

children.title: History-Window Selection Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Memory-depth choices balancing model richness and overhead.

children.title: History-Depth Selection
children.top_down_role: Selection of the maximum historical model depth.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m_k=|J_k|\leq\min\{k,m_{\max},n\},\qquad \sigma_{\min}(F_k(:,J_k))\geq\tau\sigma_{\max}(F_k(:,J_k)).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: singular-value thresholding gives a precise conditioning-aware depth rule
specific adaptive-depth policy is not identified by the supplied sources
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning-aware depth selection for Euclidean Anderson least squares.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose a cap \(m_{\max}\) and tolerance \(\tau\). At iteration \(k\), select the largest depth \(m_k\leq\min\{k,m_{\max},n\}\) for which some retained index set \(J_k\) of that cardinality satisfies
\[
\sigma_{\min}(F_k(:,J_k))\geq\tau\sigma_{\max}(F_k(:,J_k)).
\]
If no nonempty set satisfies the inequality, take \(m_k=0\) and use the unaccelerated fixed-point step. Thus depth may increase only while the admitted residual-difference model remains numerically identifiable at the prescribed relative singular-value threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use the largest permitted history depth whose residual-difference matrix passes a relative smallest-singular-value test; otherwise take an unaccelerated step.
knowledge_statements.title: History-Depth Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed largest-depth subset policy is not supported by a citation. Moreover, the displayed singular-value inequality admits an all-zero selected matrix because both sides vanish, contrary to the stated numerical-identifiability interpretation; a positive-rank condition or equivalent qualification is required.

children.title: Active-Window Selection
children.top_down_role: Selection of the currently retained block of residual history.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: J_k\text{ is admissible iff }\operatorname{rank}(W^{1/2}F_k(:,J_k))=|J_k|\text{ and }\kappa_2(W^{1/2}F_k(:,J_k))\leq\tau^{-1}.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: rank and condition-number screening precisely define a stable active subset
selection priorities among several admissible subsets require a source or implementation policy
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subset selection after fixing the maximum available history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An active window \(J_k\subseteq\{1,
\ldots,p\}\) is admissible when its weighted history matrix has full column rank and controlled condition number:
\[
\operatorname{rank}(W^{1/2}F_k(:,J_k))=|J_k|,
\qquad \kappa_2(W^{1/2}F_k(:,J_k))\leq\tau^{-1}.
\]
Among admissible subsets, select one of maximal cardinality; among ties, prefer the subset containing the most recent indices. If no nonempty subset is admissible, set \(J_k=\varnothing\). The Anderson least-squares model and update then use only columns indexed by \(J_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select the largest well-conditioned, full-rank subset of history differences, breaking ties toward recent data; use no history when none is admissible.
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Window Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind is appropriate, and the rank and condition-number test is mathematically coherent. However, no source supports this particular maximal-cardinality and recency-tie-breaking active-window policy.

children.title: Model-Richness Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Balance between historical model richness and computational overhead.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho_K\leq\rho_J,\qquad \sigma_{\min}(W^{1/2}F_k(:,K))\leq\sigma_{\min}(W^{1/2}F_k(:,J)).

notation.meaning: optimal weighted model residual for subset J

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nested least-squares spaces reduce the optimal residual while added columns cannot increase the smallest singular value
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic nested-window tradeoff in weighted least squares.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each active set \(J\), define \(\rho_J=\min_{\gamma}\|W^{1/2}(f_k-F_k(:,J)\gamma)\|_2\). If \(J\subseteq K\), enlargement of the history model gives
\[
\rho_K\leq\rho_J,
\qquad
\sigma_{\min}(W^{1/2}F_k(:,K))\leq
\sigma_{\min}(W^{1/2}F_k(:,J)).
\]
Hence additional history cannot worsen the exact least-squares fit, but it cannot improve the smallest singular value and may amplify coefficient sensitivity. Window selection therefore balances approximation richness against numerical identifiability rather than maximizing depth unconditionally.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding history can only improve the exact least-squares fit, but can reduce the smallest singular value and increase coefficient sensitivity.
knowledge_statements.title: Model-Richness Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nested least-squares residual claim is standard, but the smallest-singular-value comparison needs dimensional and nonempty-set conventions, especially if an enlarged matrix can have more columns than rows. No inspectable citation supports the Anderson-specific tradeoff or the coefficient-sensitivity interpretation.

children.title: Dependent-History Filtering
children.top_down_role: Removal or truncation of nearly redundant history directions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|(I-Q_{j-1}Q_{j-1}^{\mathsf T})W^{1/2}d_j\|_2>\tau\|W^{1/2}d_j\|_2\quad\text{for every retained }d_j.

notation.meaning: basis of previously accepted weighted directions

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: relative orthogonal-projection tests are standard rank-revealing history filters
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential relative-dependence filtering in a weighted residual norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Process candidate columns \(d_j\) in the chosen temporal order. Let \(Q_{j-1}\) contain an orthonormal basis for the previously accepted weighted columns and compute
\[
u_j=(I-Q_{j-1}Q_{j-1}^{\mathsf T})W^{1/2}d_j.
\]
Accept \(d_j\) exactly when \(\|u_j\|_2>\tau\|W^{1/2}d_j\|_2\), then append \(u_j/\|u_j\|_2\) to the basis; otherwise discard \(d_j\) as numerically dependent. Form the Anderson least-squares system only from accepted columns. An empty accepted set produces the underlying fixed-point update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain a history difference only when its weighted component orthogonal to accepted directions exceeds a relative threshold; otherwise discard it as redundant.
knowledge_statements.title: Dependent-History Filtering

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind matches the filtering leaf and the projection test is precise, but the accepted set depends on temporal processing order. No source establishes this particular weighted Anderson filtering rule, threshold convention, or empty-history fallback.

children.title: Residual Component-Balance Interface
children.top_down_role: Numerical scaling for heterogeneous or poorly balanced residual components.

children.title: Residual Scaling
children.top_down_role: Componentwise or blockwise scaling for heterogeneous residuals.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \gamma_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\gamma}\|D(f_k-F_k\gamma)\|_2.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: diagonal residual scaling is weighted Euclidean least squares
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed positive component scaling within one Anderson solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given positive component scales \(s_i\), define \(D=\operatorname{diag}(s_1^{-1},\ldots,s_n^{-1})\). Residual scaling replaces every residual and residual difference in the Anderson coefficient problem by its scaled counterpart:
\[
\gamma_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\gamma}
\|D(f_k-F_k\gamma)\|_2
=
\operatorname*{argmin}_{\gamma}(f_k-F_k\gamma)^{\mathsf T}D^2(f_k-F_k\gamma).
\]
Thus scaling is exactly weighted least squares with weight \(D^2\). The same fixed \(D\) must be applied to the current residual and all active history columns during that solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Divide residual components by positive scales and solve the resulting weighted Anderson least-squares problem, applying the same scaling to current and historical residuals.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Scaling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted least-squares identity is mathematically correct and representation is a suitable kind, but no citation supports its placement as the intended Anderson residual-scaling convention or the requirement that the same fixed scaling be used across the active solve.

children.title: Residual Normalization
children.top_down_role: Magnitude normalization used before history comparison or mixing.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat f_k=f_k/\eta_k,\qquad \widehat{\Delta f}_j=f_{j+1}/\eta_{j+1}-f_j/\eta_j.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: consistent differencing of normalized residuals defines an unambiguous normalized history model
normalization convention may vary across Anderson implementations
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-iterate scalar normalization with consistent history reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose a positive scalar \(\eta_k\), commonly \(\eta_k=\max\{\|f_k\|_2,\eta_{\min}\}\) with \(\eta_{\min}>0\), and define \(\widehat f_k=f_k/\eta_k\). Construct normalized history differences from normalized residuals,
\[
\widehat{\Delta f}_j=
\widehat f_{j+1}-\widehat f_j
=f_{j+1}/\eta_{j+1}-f_j/\eta_j,
\]
not by independently normalizing the already formed differences. Residual normalization means that the Anderson coefficient problem uses \(\widehat f_k\) and the columns \(\widehat{\Delta f}_j\); the physical fixed-point images remain in their original units when the iterate is assembled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize each residual by a positive scalar, form history differences from those normalized residuals, and use them only in the Anderson coefficient problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Normalization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formulas consistently difference normalized residuals, but this is one implementation convention rather than a universal definition of Anderson residual normalization. An exact source is required to distinguish it from normalizing already formed differences or using a single per-solve factor.

children.title: Component-Balance Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Assessment of imbalance across residual components or blocks.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B(r)=\frac{\max_{1\leq i\leq q}e_i(r)}{\min_{1\leq i\leq q}e_i(r)}\geq1.

notation.meaning: scaled root-mean-square residual in component block i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: extrema of blockwise scaled RMS values provide a directly verifiable imbalance certificate
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise diagnostic for scaled residual contributions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each nonempty component block \(\mathcal I_i\), compute
\[
e_i(r)=\left(|\mathcal I_i|^{-1}
\sum_{j\in\mathcal I_i}(r_j/s_j)^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
When every \(e_i(r)>0\), define \(B(r)=\max_i e_i(r)/\min_i e_i(r)\); set \(B(r)=+\infty\) if some but not all block values vanish, and \(B(0)=1\). The displayed block values certify which components dominate the scaled least-squares norm. Exact block balance is equivalent to \(B(r)=1\), while a large value identifies a scaling mismatch or strongly uneven residual progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare scaled RMS residuals across component blocks; their maximum-to-minimum ratio certifies balance, imbalance, or a vanishing-block mismatch.
knowledge_statements.title: Component-Balance Diagnostics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The piecewise imbalance ratio is internally defined, and certificate is plausible for a diagnostic leaf. No citation supports this specific blockwise RMS certificate, however, and a large ratio alone cannot distinguish scaling mismatch from genuinely uneven residual progress.

children.title: Anderson Convergence Theory
children.top_down_role: Theory organized by linear structure, nonlinear regularity, and safeguard dependence.

children.title: Linear Anderson Theory
children.top_down_role: Spectral, Krylov, finite-memory, and termination behavior for linear maps.

children.title: Full-Memory Linear Regime
children.top_down_role: Exact-arithmetic theory under unrestricted history.

assumptions_latex: \text{full-memory type-II Anderson with unit mixing does not stagnate}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|b-Ax_k^{\mathrm{AA}}\|_2=\min_{x\in x_0+\mathcal K_k(A,r_0)}\|b-Ax\|_2.

notation.meaning: linear-system matrix induced by the affine map

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nonstagnating full-memory type-II Anderson is classically equivalent to GMRES on an affine map
exact indexing and stagnation hypotheses require an Anderson-specific theorem source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic type-II Anderson–GMRES equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G(x)=Mx+c\), set \(A=I-M\) and \(b=c\), and apply full-memory type-II Anderson acceleration with unit mixing to \(x=G(x)\). In exact arithmetic, at every step before Anderson or GMRES stagnation, the accelerated iterate has the GMRES residual-minimization property
\[
\|b-Ax_k^{\mathrm{AA}}\|_2=
\min_{x\in x_0+\mathcal K_k(A,r_0)}
\|b-Ax\|_2,
\qquad
\mathcal K_k(A,r_0)=
\operatorname{span}\{r_0,Ar_0,
\ldots,A^{k-1}r_0\}.
\]
Consequently, if the Krylov grade of \(r_0\) is \(d\) and no earlier stagnation occurs, Anderson reaches the solution in at most \(d\) accelerated steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an affine fixed-point map, nonstagnating full-memory type-II Anderson has the same residual-minimization property and finite-termination bound as GMRES.
knowledge_statements.title: Full-Memory Linear Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind fits the exact-arithmetic full-memory leaf, but Anderson–GMRES equivalence is formulation- and index-sensitive. An exact theorem citation is required to verify whether the stated Anderson iterate itself has the GMRES minimization property and whether the claimed grade-based termination index follows under the stated nonstagnation hypothesis.

children.title: Finite-Memory Linear Regime
children.top_down_role: Linear behavior under truncation and restart.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_{k+1}\in G(x_k)+\operatorname{span}\{\Delta x_j,\Delta f_j:j=k-m_k,\ldots,k-1\},\qquad m_k\leq m.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: truncation restricts the multisecant correction space and removes the full-memory finite-termination implication
precise equivalence to restarted or truncated Krylov methods depends on the Anderson variant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: What is lost when linear Anderson history is capped.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the affine map \(G(x)=Mx+c\), finite-memory Anderson with cap \(m\) forms each correction using at most the latest \(m_k=
\min\{m,k\}\) iterate and residual differences. Thus
\[
x_{k+1}
\in G(x_k)+
\operatorname{span}\{\Delta x_j,
\Delta f_j:j=k-m_k,
\ldots,k-1\}.
\]
Once \(k>m\), this space need not contain all earlier Krylov directions. Therefore the full-memory GMRES residual-minimization identity and the grade-based finite-termination conclusion do not follow merely from nonsingularity of \(A=I-M\); truncation or restart can discard a direction needed for subsequent exact residual cancellation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Capping history restricts each correction to recent differences, so full-memory GMRES equivalence and grade-based finite termination need not survive truncation or restart.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Memory Linear Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure boundary is the correct role for describing what truncation loses. Nevertheless, the displayed correction-space inclusion and its relationship to truncated or restarted Krylov behavior depend on the precise Anderson update, which is not defined or cited.

children.title: Symmetric Linear Regime
children.top_down_role: Short-recurrence and specialized convergence structures for symmetric problems.

assumptions_latex: \omega\neq0\text{ and full-memory Anderson does not stagnate}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|b-Ax_k^{\mathrm{AA}}\|_2=\min_{x\in x_0+\mathcal K_k(A,r_0)}\|b-Ax\|_2,\quad \mathcal K_k\text{ is generated by symmetric Lanczos recurrence}.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: GMRES residual minimization on a real symmetric matrix is MINRES and admits symmetric Lanczos generation
Anderson indexing and nonstagnation conditions require an exact source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-memory affine Anderson inherited through symmetric GMRES/MINRES structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\) be nonsingular and apply full-memory type-II Anderson acceleration with unit mixing to \(G(x)=x-\omega(Ax-b)\), where \(\omega\neq0\). Before stagnation, its linear residual satisfies
\[
\|b-Ax_k^{\mathrm{AA}}\|_2=
\min_{x\in x_0+
\mathcal K_k(A,r_0)}
\|b-Ax\|_2.
\]
Because \(A\) is real symmetric, the Krylov basis can be generated by the three-term symmetric Lanczos recurrence, and this residual-minimizing process is MINRES. The short recurrence concerns Krylov basis generation; it does not by itself make a naively stored Anderson history short-memory equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a symmetric affine problem, nonstagnating full-memory Anderson inherits MINRES residual minimization and Lanczos basis generation, though naive Anderson storage remains long-memory.
knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric Linear Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role fits the symmetric linear regime, and symmetric residual minimization is compatible with MINRES/Lanczos structure. An exact source is needed to verify the Anderson indexing and nonstagnation assumptions and to separate short-recurrence Krylov basis generation from the storage requirements of the stated Anderson implementation.

children.title: Nonlinear Local Anderson Theory
children.top_down_role: Local convergence structures for smooth fixed-point residuals.

children.title: Contractive Nonlinear Regime
children.top_down_role: Anderson behavior inherited from a locally or globally contractive baseline.

knowledge_statements.title: Contractive Nonlinear Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual geometry and safeguarded Anderson convergence for a contraction on a complete normed space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G:X\to X\) satisfy \(\|G(x)-G(y)\|\le q\|x-y\|\) for all \(x,y\in X\), where \(0\le q<1\), and let \(x^*\) be its unique fixed point. For \(r(x)=G(x)-x\),
\[(1-q)\|x-x^*\|\le \|r(x)\|\le(1+q)\|x-x^*\|.\]
Consequently, any safeguarded Anderson sequence satisfying \(\|r(x_{k+1})\|\le\rho\|r(x_k)\|\) with a uniform \(\rho<1\) converges to \(x^*\), and
\[\|x_k-x^*\|\le \frac{\rho^k}{1-q}\|r(x_0)\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a contraction, residual and fixed-point error are equivalent. Uniform residual contraction of safeguarded Anderson iterates therefore gives linear convergence to the unique fixed point.
assumptions_latex: The accepted iterates satisfy a uniform residual reduction factor \(\rho<1\).

children.title: Multisecant Fast-Convergence Regime
children.top_down_role: Local fast behavior associated with increasingly accurate inverse models.

knowledge_statements.title: Multisecant Fast-Convergence Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dennis–Moré-type local condition for Anderson viewed as an inverse multisecant method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuously differentiable near a root \(x^*\), with nonsingular \(J_*=Dr(x^*)\). Write an Anderson-type step as \(x_{k+1}=x_k-H_k r(x_k)\), where \(H_k\) satisfies the retained inverse multisecant equations. The fast-convergence regime is characterized by
\[\frac{\|(I-H_kJ_*)s_k\|}{\|s_k\|}\longrightarrow0,\qquad s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k,\]
together with \(x_k\to x^*\). Under these conditions and bounded \(H_k\), the errors satisfy \(\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|/\|x_k-x^*\|\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Anderson becomes locally superlinear when its implicit inverse multisecant models act increasingly like the inverse residual Jacobian along the generated steps.
assumptions_latex: \(r\) is continuously differentiable near \(x^*\), with \(r(x^*)=0\) and nonsingular \(Dr(x^*)\).
\(x_k\to x^*\) and the implicit inverse models \(H_k\) are uniformly bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \frac{\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|}{\|x_k-x^*\|}\to0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the container, but no source establishes that this particular inverse-model condition, indexed using the generated step, is sufficient for the asserted Anderson superlinear conclusion. An exact local theorem and its full hypotheses are required.

children.title: One-Step Acceleration-Gain Analysis
children.top_down_role: Local comparison of accelerated and baseline residual behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: One-Step Acceleration-Gain Analysis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact one-step residual comparison for affine fixed-point maps and constrained Anderson coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G(x)=Ax+b\) and \(r(x)=G(x)-x\). Given stored points \(x_{k-m},\ldots,x_k\), choose coefficients \(\alpha_i\) with \(\sum_i\alpha_i=1\), and form the Anderson trial point \(x_{k+1}^{AA}=\sum_i\alpha_iG(x_i)\). Then
\[r(x_{k+1}^{AA})=A\sum_i\alpha_i r(x_i).\]
Hence, if \(\alpha\) minimizes \(\|\sum_i\alpha_i r(x_i)\|\) subject to affine feasibility, the one-step gain obeys
\[\|r(x_{k+1}^{AA})\|\le \|A\|\min_{\mathbf 1^T\alpha=1}\left\|\sum_i\alpha_i r(x_i)\right\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an affine map, the next Anderson residual is exactly the map matrix applied to the optimized residual combination, separating mixing gain from baseline propagation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r(x_{k+1}^{AA})=A\sum_i\alpha_i r(x_i)\), with the displayed norm bound for minimizing coefficients.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine residual identity is mathematically consistent and the property kind fits one-step gain analysis, but the record supplies no inspectable citation for the stated Anderson formulation and constrained minimization bound.

children.title: Anderson Beyond Smooth Contractions
children.top_down_role: Convergence routes requiring nonexpansive structure, merit functions, or application-specific regularity.

children.title: Nonexpansive Anderson Geometry Family
children.top_down_role: Safeguard-dependent behavior for proximal and splitting maps.

children.title: Nonexpansive Anderson Regime
children.top_down_role: Safeguarded Anderson behavior for nonexpansive fixed-point maps.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonexpansive Anderson Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometry defining the nonexpansive setting in which unguarded Anderson extrapolation lacks contraction control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space and \(G:H\to H\) have a nonempty fixed-point set. The nonexpansive Anderson regime is defined by
\[\|Gx-Gy\|\le\|x-y\|\qquad(x,y\in H),\]
with Anderson trial points \(y_k=\sum_{i=0}^{m_k}\alpha_iG(x_{k-i})\), where \(\sum_i\alpha_i=1\). Nonexpansiveness controls each application of \(G\), but it does not control affine extrapolation when coefficients may be negative or \(\|\alpha\|_1\) is unbounded. Thus convergence requires additional coefficient control, damping, acceptance tests, or fallback steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonexpansive map controls its own images, but unrestricted Anderson affine combinations can leave that geometry; additional safeguards are therefore required for general convergence claims.
assumptions_latex: Anderson coefficients are affine but need not be convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nonexpansiveness alone supplies no general convergence guarantee for unrestricted Anderson trial points.

children.title: Averaged Anderson Regime
children.top_down_role: Safeguarded Anderson behavior for averaged fixed-point maps.

knowledge_statements.title: Averaged Anderson Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator geometry for Anderson acceleration of averaged fixed-point mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space. The averaged Anderson regime consists of maps
\[G=(1-\theta)I+\theta N,\qquad 0<\theta<1,\]
where \(N:H\to H\) is nonexpansive and \(\operatorname{Fix}G\ne\varnothing\). Equivalently,
\[\|Gx-Gy\|^2\le\|x-y\|^2-\frac{1-\theta}{\theta}\|(I-G)x-(I-G)y\|^2.\]
This descent geometry applies directly to Picard steps \(G(x_k)\). An Anderson trial inherits it only when an acceptance or damping rule ensures the trial satisfies the corresponding Fejér or residual-decrease inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaged maps possess a strict displacement inequality for Picard steps. Anderson trials require acceptance or damping to preserve that descent geometry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The averaged-operator inequality holds; its extension to Anderson trials is conditional on a preserving safeguard.

children.title: Safeguard Dependence
children.top_down_role: Dependence of reliable acceleration on acceptance and fallback mechanisms.

knowledge_statements.title: Safeguard Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating operator-level nonexpansiveness from convergence of extrapolated Anderson iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Nonexpansiveness or averagedness constrains \(Gx-Gy\), not arbitrary affine combinations \(\sum_i\alpha_iG(x_i)\). If negative coefficients are permitted and \(\|\alpha\|_1\) is unbounded, then
\[\left\|\sum_i\alpha_i(G(x_i)-G(z))\right\|\le\sum_i|\alpha_i|\|x_i-z\|\]
contains no uniform Fejér factor, even for \(z\in\operatorname{Fix}G\). Therefore an operator-level fixed-point theorem cannot by itself justify unrestricted Anderson acceleration. A valid global result must additionally bound coefficients or steps, damp extrapolation, accept only sufficient progress, or provide convergent fallback iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonexpansive geometry does not control unrestricted affine extrapolation. Global Anderson convergence consequently depends on coefficient, step, acceptance, damping, or fallback safeguards.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is nonexpansive on a normed space and \(z\in\operatorname{Fix}G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without further control, no uniform Fejér decrease follows from nonexpansiveness alone.

notation.meaning: a fixed point of the map

children.title: Nonsmooth Anderson Regime
children.top_down_role: Problem-dependent theory without classical smooth residual models.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsmooth Anderson Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit of smooth local Anderson theory when the fixed-point residual lacks a classical derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r(x)=G(x)-x\) be locally Lipschitz near a root \(x^*\) but not Fréchet differentiable there. Anderson residual differences and least-squares coefficients remain well defined, yet expansions of the form
\[r(x^*+h)=Dr(x^*)h+o(\|h\|)\]
are unavailable. Consequently, convergence or acceleration cannot be inferred from smooth Jacobian or Dennis–Moré arguments alone. A nonsmooth result must instead specify replacement structure, such as semismoothness with generalized derivatives, piecewise-affine identification, metric subregularity plus safeguarded descent, or a problem-specific merit inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Anderson mixing remains computable for nonsmooth residuals, but smooth Jacobian-based local acceleration theory fails and must be replaced by explicit nonsmooth structure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Classical smooth local Anderson conclusions do not follow without an additional nonsmooth regularity or globalization hypothesis.

notation.meaning: classical derivative whose absence defines the boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record correctly identifies a boundary of classical differentiable analysis, and failure_boundary fits the container. A nonsmooth Anderson source is still required to substantiate the asserted scope and the listed replacement structures.

children.title: Nonconvex Anderson Regime
children.top_down_role: Merit-based and application-specific convergence structures in nonconvex problems.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Anderson Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Merit-based global convergence template for safeguarded Anderson steps in nonconvex problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), \(r=G-I\), and let \(\Phi:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be bounded below on the initial level set. Suppose every accepted Anderson or fallback step satisfies
\[\Phi(x_{k+1})\le\Phi(x_k)-c\|r(x_k)\|^2,\qquad c>0,\]
and all iterates remain in a compact subset on which \(r\) is continuous. Then \(\sum_k\|r(x_k)\|^2<\infty\), so \(r(x_k)\to0\), and every accumulation point is a fixed point. Stationarity follows only when the application supplies the implication \(r(x)=0\Rightarrow0\in\partial\Phi(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a nonconvex setting, sufficient merit decrease and compactness force residual convergence; stationarity additionally requires a problem-specific residual-to-stationarity link.
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi\) is bounded below on a compact set containing all iterates.
Every accepted or fallback step satisfies the displayed sufficient-decrease inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r(x_k)\to0\), and every cluster point lies in \(\operatorname{Fix}G\); stationarity requires the stated implication.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sufficient-decrease argument is mathematically plausible under the stated assumptions, but it is a theorem-like convergence template rather than merely a principle. No source verifies that this exact template is an Anderson result or supplies the application-specific stationarity framework.

children.title: Anderson Globalization Safeguard System
children.top_down_role: Mechanisms that preserve a reliable baseline iteration while selectively accepting accelerated candidates.

children.title: Residual-Acceptance Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Acceptance families based on fixed-point or nonlinear residual progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Acceptance Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic residual test accepting Anderson trials only when prescribed fixed-point progress is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_k\), form an Anderson trial \(y_k\), a fallback point \(p_k=G(x_k)\), and residual \(r=G-I\). Choose \(0<\eta<1\) and a nonnegative reference value \(R_k\). Set
\[x_{k+1}=\begin{cases}y_k,&\|r(y_k)\|\le\eta R_k,\\p_k,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}\]
The reference may be monotone, \(R_k=\|r(x_k)\|\), or nonmonotone, \(R_k=\max_{k-q_k\le j\le k}\|r(x_j)\|\). Stop when \(\|r(x_{k+1})\|\le\varepsilon\); otherwise update the history, excluding rejected data if required by the recovery policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute an Anderson trial and accept it only when its residual beats a prescribed monotone or nonmonotone reference; otherwise take a baseline fixed-point step.
assumptions_latex: Residual evaluations at the trial and fallback points are available.
\(0<\eta<1\), tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), and reference-window rule are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is the first accepted or fallback iterate satisfying \(\|r(x_{k+1})\|\le\varepsilon\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct kind for this container, but the monotone and nonmonotone reference rules, rejection-history policy, and claimed safeguard family have no cited Anderson source.

children.title: Merit-Function Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Problem-aware acceptance through merit or envelope structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Merit-Function Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Problem-aware acceptance test based on sufficient decrease of a lower-bounded merit function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_k\), an Anderson trial \(y_k\), a fallback candidate \(p_k\), merit function \(\Phi\), forcing measure \(\Delta_k\ge0\), and constant \(c>0\), accept
\[x_{k+1}=y_k\quad\text{if}\quad \Phi(y_k)\le M_k-c\Delta_k;\]
otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=p_k\), where the fallback rule must ensure \(\Phi(p_k)\le M_k-c\Delta_k\). Here \(M_k\) is either \(\Phi(x_k)\) or a finite-window maximum of recent merit values. Stop when the application-specific stationarity or residual measure is at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept an Anderson trial only when it gives sufficient merit decrease; otherwise use a fallback step satisfying the same forcing condition.
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi\) is finite on all tested points and bounded below along accepted iterates.
A fallback candidate satisfying the required decrease can be produced.
The forcing measure and stopping tolerance are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every iteration satisfies \(\Phi(x_{k+1})\le M_k-c\Delta_k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but the generic finite-window merit rule and assumed fallback decrease require a source and application-specific conditions. The record does not establish when such a fallback exists or what nonmonotone reference rules preserve convergence.

children.title: Fallback-Restart Recovery System
children.top_down_role: Baseline recovery and history reset following rejected acceleration.

children.title: Fallback Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Recovery through a reliable baseline iteration after rejected acceleration.

knowledge_statements.title: Fallback Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery rule replacing a rejected Anderson trial by a convergence-certified baseline step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), compute an Anderson trial \(y_k\) and test the prescribed acceptance predicate \(A_k(y_k)\). If it holds, set \(x_{k+1}=y_k\). Otherwise choose a baseline operator \(P_k\) for which the governing convergence analysis applies and set
\[x_{k+1}=P_k(x_k).\]
Evaluate the stopping measure at \(x_{k+1}\), and stop when it is at most \(\varepsilon\). The fallback is convergence preserving only if rejected trials do not alter the state used by \(P_k\), and the accepted-step subsequence satisfies the assumptions of the accompanying safeguard theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When an Anderson trial fails its acceptance test, discard it and advance with a baseline step whose convergence theory is known.
assumptions_latex: An acceptance predicate \(A_k\) and tolerance \(\varepsilon\) are specified.
Each fallback operator \(P_k\) satisfies the baseline method's convergence conditions.
A rejected trial does not replace the current accepted state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Rejected trials are replaced by \(x_{k+1}=P_k(x_k)\), preserving the baseline step at those iterations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fallback algorithm matches the container, but preserving individual baseline steps does not by itself establish convergence of the interleaved accepted Anderson sequence. The required accompanying safeguard theorem is neither stated precisely nor cited.

children.title: Restart Safeguards
children.top_down_role: History-reset mechanisms invoked after unreliable accelerated behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Restart Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: History-reset rule controlling ill-conditioning, coefficient growth, or repeated rejection in Anderson mixing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Maintain accepted pairs in an Anderson history \(\mathcal H_k\). Before forming the next trial, restart whenever at least one prescribed trigger holds: the residual-difference least-squares matrix has condition estimate above \(\kappa_{\max}\), the computed coefficients satisfy \(\|\alpha_k\|_1>B\), or \(s_{\max}\) consecutive trials have been rejected. On restart set
\[\mathcal H_k\leftarrow\{x_k\\},\qquad m_k\leftarrow0,
\]
and take \(x_{k+1}=G(x_k)\) or another certified fallback step. Otherwise retain at most the newest \(m_{\max}\) accepted history entries and compute the usual Anderson trial.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reset Anderson memory and take a baseline step when mixing becomes ill-conditioned, coefficients grow too large, or rejection persists.
assumptions_latex: Thresholds \(\kappa_{\max}\), \(B\), \(s_{\max}\), and maximum memory \(m_{\max}\) are fixed.
The post-restart baseline step is well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each triggered restart clears extrapolative memory and produces a baseline successor from the current accepted iterate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but the combined condition-number, coefficient-norm, and rejection-count restart policy is uncited. The display also contains malformed set notation and a stray line-break command in the assignment to the history, which must be repaired after the sourced policy is established.

children.title: Post-Rejection History Recovery
children.top_down_role: History-management choices following candidate rejection.

knowledge_statements.title: Post-Rejection History Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery policy after a safeguarded Anderson proposal is rejected.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a fixed-point map \(T:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), residual \(F=I-T\), memory limit \(m\), and rejected proposal \(y_k\), set the fallback iterate to \(x_{k+1}=T(x_k)\). Discard all history pairs involving \(y_k\). Either restart by setting \(\mathcal H_{k+1}=\varnothing\), or truncate the accepted history to its newest \(r<m\) pairs and append \((x_{k+1}-x_k,F(x_{k+1})-F(x_k))\) only after evaluating the fallback point. Stop when \(\lVert F(x_{k+1})\rVert\leq\varepsilon\); otherwise form the next Anderson subproblem solely from \(\mathcal H_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After rejecting an Anderson step, take a Picard fallback, remove rejected-point data, and restart or truncate the history before rebuilding it from accepted iterates.
assumptions_latex: \(T:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is evaluable at every accepted iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_k\notin\mathcal H_{k+1}\), and every retained secant pair is generated by accepted iterates.

children.title: Line-Search Anderson Families
children.top_down_role: Anderson variants globalized through directional step acceptance.

knowledge_statements.title: Line-Search Anderson Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backtracking globalization of an Anderson search direction by residual merit decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=I-T\), \(\phi(x)=\tfrac12\lVert F(x)\rVert^2\), and let \(d_k^A\) be an Anderson direction. Given \(0<\rho<1\), \(0<c<1\), and a predicted decrease \(q_k>0\), test \(\alpha_j=\rho^j\) in increasing order of \(j\geq0\) and accept the first trial \(x_k+\alpha_jd_k^A\) satisfying \(\phi(x_k+\alpha_jd_k^A)\leq\phi(x_k)-c\alpha_jq_k\). If no acceptable trial is found within the prescribed search budget, set \(x_{k+1}=T(x_k)\) and invoke history recovery. Stop when \(\lVert F(x_{k+1})\rVert\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backtrack along an Anderson direction until residual merit sufficiently decreases; otherwise take a Picard fallback and repair the history.
assumptions_latex: \(T:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) and the trial residuals are evaluable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An accepted accelerated trial satisfies \(\phi(x_{k+1})<\phi(x_k)\); otherwise \(x_{k+1}=T(x_k)\).

children.title: Trust-Region Anderson Families
children.top_down_role: Anderson variants globalized through bounded local model regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Anderson Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trust-region acceptance and radius control for residual models built from Anderson history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(x_k\), construct from Anderson history a residual model \(M_k(s)\) with \(M_k(0)=F(x_k)\). Choose \(s_k\) satisfying \(\lVert s_k\rVert\leq\Delta_k\) and positive predicted reduction \(p_k=\lVert M_k(0)\rVert^2-\lVert M_k(s_k)\rVert^2\). Evaluate \(r_k=(\lVert F(x_k)\rVert^2-\lVert F(x_k+s_k)\rVert^2)/p_k\). Accept \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) when \(r_k\geq\eta_1\); otherwise reject it and take a prescribed fallback. Contract \(\Delta_k\) after poor agreement and permit expansion when \(r_k\geq\eta_2\) and \(\lVert s_k\rVert=\Delta_k\), where \(0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restrict an Anderson-model step to a radius, compare actual with predicted residual reduction, and update both the iterate and radius from that ratio.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance requires \(r_k\geq\eta_1\), while the radius responds to model agreement and boundary activity.

children.title: Restricted-Step Globalization
children.top_down_role: Shared mechanisms for limiting unreliable accelerated candidates.

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Step Globalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Globalization by explicitly limiting displacement from the current accepted iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an Anderson proposal \(y_k^A\), radius \(\Delta_k>0\), and residual \(F=I-T\), define \(d_k=y_k^A-x_k\) and \(\lambda_k=\min\{1,\Delta_k/\lVert d_k\rVert\}\), with \(\lambda_k=1\) when \(d_k=0\). Form \(z_k=x_k+\lambda_kd_k\). Accept \(x_{k+1}=z_k\) only if \(\lVert F(z_k)\rVert\leq(1-\sigma_k)\lVert F(x_k)\rVert\) for a prescribed \(0\leq\sigma_k<1\); otherwise take \(x_{k+1}=T(x_k)\) and repair the history. Stop when the accepted residual norm is at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clip the Anderson displacement to a prescribed radius and accept it only after a residual test; otherwise use the baseline fixed-point step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert z_k-x_k\rVert\leq\Delta_k\), and every accepted restricted step satisfies the prescribed residual test.

children.title: Alternating Anderson–Picard Families
