knowledge_statements.title: Alternating Anderson–Picard Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Periodic interleaving of accelerated proposals with baseline Picard iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(T:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), memory \(m\), period \(q\geq2\), initial point \(x_0\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), evaluate \(F(x_k)=x_k-T(x_k)\). If \(\lVert F(x_k)\rVert\leq\varepsilon\), return \(x_k\). When \(k+1\) is divisible by \(q\), set \(x_{k+1}=T(x_k)\). At other indices, form a depth-at-most-\(m\) Anderson proposal from accepted history and accept it if the prescribed safeguard holds; otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=T(x_k)\). Store only accepted consecutive iterate-residual differences, optionally restarting after each scheduled Picard step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use Anderson acceleration on selected iterations and force a Picard step periodically, with safeguarded fallback and accepted-history maintenance.
assumptions_latex: \(T:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is evaluable along the generated sequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every block of \(q\) updates contains at least one baseline update \(x_{k+1}=T(x_k)\).

children.title: Anderson Failure Regimes

children.title: Anderson History Degeneracy Classes
children.top_down_role: Loss of informative mixing directions.

children.title: Rank-Deficient Histories
children.top_down_role: Residual histories lacking sufficient independent mixing directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficient Histories
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact algebraic degeneracy of the residual-difference matrix in Anderson mixing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For retained residuals \(f_i=F(x_i)\), form \(Y_k=[f_{k-m_k+1}-f_{k-m_k},\ldots,f_k-f_{k-1}]\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m_k}\). The Anderson history is rank deficient precisely when \(\operatorname{rank}(Y_k)<m_k\), equivalently when \(\ker(Y_k)\neq\{0\}\), or when \(\lambda_{\min}(Y_k^{\mathsf T}Y_k)=0\). In that case the least-squares problem \(\min_{\gamma\in\mathbb{R}^{m_k}}\lVert f_k-Y_k\gamma\rVert_2\) cannot have a unique coefficient vector: if \(\gamma\) is a minimizer and \(0\neq v\in\ker(Y_k)\), then \(\gamma+v\) is a distinct minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A history is rank deficient when its residual-difference columns are linearly dependent, giving a nonzero null direction and therefore nonunique Anderson least-squares coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(Y_k)<m_k\Longrightarrow\operatorname*{argmin}_{\gamma\in\mathbb{R}^{m_k}}\lVert f_k-Y_k\gamma\rVert_2\) is non-singleton.

notation.meaning: smallest eigenvalue of the symmetric Gram matrix

children.title: Collinear Histories
children.top_down_role: Histories dominated by nearly parallel residual differences.

knowledge_statements.title: Collinear Histories
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional residual-difference history causing severe Anderson degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_k=[y_1,\ldots,y_{m_k}]\) be the residual-difference history matrix. The history is collinear when there exist a vector \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and scalars \(a_1,\ldots,a_{m_k}\), not all zero, such that \(y_j=a_jv\) for every \(j\). Then \(\operatorname{rank}(Y_k)\leq1\). Consequently, whenever \(m_k\geq2\), the history is rank deficient and the unregularized Anderson coefficient problem has nonunique minimizers. Its fitted correction belongs only to \(\operatorname{span}\{v\}\), regardless of the nominal memory depth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Collinear residual differences span at most one direction, so histories of depth at least two are rank deficient and cannot exploit multiple directions.
assumptions_latex: \(Y_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m_k}\) contains the retained residual differences.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_j=a_jv\) for all \(j\Longrightarrow\operatorname{rank}(Y_k)\leq1\).

children.title: Informative-Direction Loss
children.top_down_role: Degradation of the residual subspace available for mixing.

knowledge_statements.title: Informative-Direction Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: History-span test for loss of directions capable of reducing the current residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_k=F(x_k)\), let \(Y_k\) be the residual-difference history matrix, and let \(P_k\) be the orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{range}(Y_k)\). For a threshold \(0\leq\tau<1\), informative-direction loss occurs when \(\lVert P_kf_k\rVert_2\leq\tau\lVert f_k\rVert_2\). Indeed, the unregularized linearized mixing problem obeys \(\min_\gamma\lVert f_k-Y_k\gamma\rVert_2^2=\lVert f_k\rVert_2^2-\lVert P_kf_k\rVert_2^2\). Thus the maximum relative squared-residual reduction available from the retained span is at most \(\tau^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The history loses informative directions when the current residual has only a small projection onto its span, limiting achievable least-squares reduction.
assumptions_latex: \(P_k\) is the Euclidean orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{range}(Y_k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert P_kf_k\rVert_2\leq\tau\lVert f_k\rVert_2\Longrightarrow 1-\frac{\min_\gamma\lVert f_k-Y_k\gamma\rVert_2^2}{\lVert f_k\rVert_2^2}\leq\tau^2\).

children.title: Ill-Conditioned Mixing Subproblems
children.top_down_role: Coefficient instability in poorly conditioned residual histories.

knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioned Mixing Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sensitivity boundary for full-rank but nearly dependent Anderson residual histories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m_k}\) have full column rank and define the mixing coefficients by \(\gamma_k=Y_k^\dagger f_k\). For a prescribed conditioning limit \(K>1\), the mixing subproblem is ill conditioned when \(\kappa_2(Y_k)=\sigma_{\max}(Y_k)/\sigma_{\min}(Y_k)>K\). Perturbations in the residual satisfy \(\lVert Y_k^\dagger\delta f\rVert_2\leq\lVert\delta f\rVert_2/\sigma_{\min}(Y_k)\), and this amplification bound becomes large as \(\sigma_{\min}(Y_k)\) approaches zero. Hence small evaluation or rounding errors can cause large coefficient changes before exact rank deficiency occurs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nearly dependent residual histories amplify data errors through the pseudoinverse, producing unstable Anderson coefficients even while the matrix remains full rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(Y_k)>K\) marks coefficient sensitivity of order \(1/\sigma_{\min}(Y_k)\).

children.title: Aggressive-Mixing Dynamical Failures

children.title: Noncontractive Instability
children.top_down_role: Unstable accelerated behavior outside a contractive local regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Noncontractive Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar instability showing that unrestricted mixing need not converge without contractivity or safeguarding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(T(x)=ax\) on \(\mathbb{R}\), whose fixed point is \(x^\star=0\), and the mixed update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\beta(T(x_k)-x_k)\). Then \(x_{k+1}=q x_k\) with \(q=1+\beta(a-1)\). For every \(x_0\neq0\), the iterates diverge in magnitude when \(\lvert q\rvert>1\) and fail to converge when \(q=-1\). In particular, if \(a>1\) and \(\beta>0\), then \(q>1\). Thus positive mixing cannot stabilize this expanding noncontractive fixed-point map without an additional restriction or safeguard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an expanding scalar map, positive residual mixing has an amplification factor above one, so every nonzero initial iterate diverges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lvert x_k\rvert=\lvert1+\beta(a-1)\rvert^k\lvert x_0\rvert\to\infty\).

children.title: Cycling Regimes
children.top_down_role: Recurrent iterate or residual behavior under aggressive mixing.

knowledge_statements.title: Cycling Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A scalar fixed-point iteration exhibiting an exact nonconvergent two-cycle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(T(x)=-x\), with unique fixed point \(x^\star=0\). Starting from any \(x_0\neq0\), the unsafeguarded Picard update gives \(x_{k+1}=-x_k\), hence \(x_{2j}=x_0\) and \(x_{2j+1}=-x_0\) for all \(j\geq0\). The residual norm is constant because \(F(x)=x-T(x)=2x\). Therefore the sequence cycles with period two and never meets any residual tolerance \(\varepsilon<2\lvert x_0\rvert\). A fallback that repeatedly reproduces this update does not break the cycle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The map sending each scalar to its negative makes Picard iterates alternate forever between two nonzero points while the residual norm stays constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+2}=x_k\), \(x_{k+1}\neq x_k\), and \(\lVert F(x_k)\rVert=2\lvert x_0\rvert\).

children.title: Aggressive-Mixing Failure
children.top_down_role: Parameter regimes where mixing strength triggers instability or recurrence.

knowledge_statements.title: Aggressive-Mixing Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp scalar upper boundary on extrapolative mixing for a contractive map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T(x)=ax\) on \(\mathbb{R}\), where \(0<a<1\), and apply the extrapolative mixed update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\beta(T(x_k)-x_k)\) with \(\beta>0\). Its amplification factor is \(q=1-\beta(1-a)\). The iteration converges to the fixed point \(0\) exactly when \(0<\beta<2/(1-a)\). At \(\beta=2/(1-a)\), every nonzero orbit forms a two-cycle, while \(\beta>2/(1-a)\) yields \(\lvert q\rvert>1\) and divergence. Thus excessive extrapolation can destabilize even a strict contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a scalar contraction, extrapolation converges only below a sharp mixing threshold; equality causes cycling and larger mixing causes divergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0<\beta<\frac{2}{1-a}\) is necessary and sufficient for convergence; \(\beta\geq\frac{2}{1-a}\) causes cycling or divergence.

children.title: Residual History Contamination Regimes

children.title: Noisy Residual Histories
children.top_down_role: Residual histories contaminated by stochastic or measurement noise.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\alpha\|_2\to\infty\) as \(\delta\to0\), despite vanishing history contamination.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A scalar example isolates coefficient instability caused by arbitrarily small residual noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider constrained Anderson mixing based on \(\min_{\alpha_1+\alpha_2=1}|\alpha_1r+\alpha_2(r+\delta)|\). The unique zero-residual solution is \(\alpha_2=-r/\delta\) and \(\alpha_1=1+r/\delta\). Hence \(\|\alpha\|_2\) diverges as \(\delta\to0\), although the perturbation of the second stored residual tends to zero. Thus unregularized residual-history least squares has no uniform coefficient-stability bound under additive noise near a rank-deficient exact history.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrarily small noise can split duplicate residual columns and make unregularized Anderson coefficients arbitrarily large, even while the mixed residual is zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Noisy Residual Histories

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar failure example is internally correct and fits the failure-boundary container, but no source supports its interpretation as an Anderson residual-history instability result.

children.title: Inexact Residual Histories
children.top_down_role: Residual histories formed from approximate map evaluations.

assumptions_latex: \(F:X\to X\) is evaluated as \(\widetilde F(x)=F(x)+e(x)\) on a normed space \(X\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When \(\|F(x_i)-F(x_j)\|=O(\varepsilon)\), bounded evaluation errors can arbitrarily corrupt the corresponding residual-history difference.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministically bounded, potentially adversarial errors in stored fixed-point residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For stored points \(x_i,x_j\), the computed secant column satisfies \(\widetilde r(x_i)-\widetilde r(x_j)=r(x_i)-r(x_j)+e(x_i)-e(x_j)\), with \(\|e(x_i)-e(x_j)\|\leq2\varepsilon\). If the exact difference has norm at most \(2\varepsilon\), admissible errors can cancel it, reverse its direction, or replace it by any perturbation in the radius-\(2\varepsilon\) ball. Consequently, a convergence or conditioning guarantee based solely on exact residual differences does not extend uniformly to such inexact histories.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When true residual changes are comparable to evaluation error, admissible errors can erase or redirect Anderson secant information, invalidating exact-history guarantees.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Residual Histories

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The perturbation-ball and cancellation claims are correct, but reversing an exact difference requires its norm to be at most ε, not merely 2ε. A source and corrected quantitative wording are required.

children.title: Finite-Precision Contamination
children.top_down_role: History degradation attributable to numerical roundoff.

assumptions_latex: Stored residual vectors \(r_i,r_j\in\mathbb{R}^n\) are subtracted componentwise
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relative error in a residual-difference column can be arbitrarily large under cancellation, and a history solve becomes unreliable when \(u\kappa(R)\not\ll1\).

notation.meaning: Residual-history matrix used by Anderson mixing.
Condition number of the history matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subtractive cancellation and ill-conditioned history solves in standard floating-point arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the componentwise model, \(\operatorname{fl}(r_i-r_j)=(r_i-r_j)+d_{ij}\), where \(|d_{ij}|\leq u(|r_i|+|r_j|)+O(u^2)\) componentwise. Therefore no finite relative-error bound follows when \(r_i-r_j\) is small compared with \(|r_i|+|r_j|\). Moreover, backward stability of a least-squares history solve controls the data perturbation, not the coefficient error; the latter may scale as \(u\kappa(R)\). Near rank deficiency, finite precision can therefore dominate the apparent secant information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cancellation corrupts small residual differences, while an ill-conditioned history matrix amplifies backward-stable rounding errors into large Anderson coefficient errors.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Precision Contamination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cancellation phenomenon fits the container, but the componentwise error model and the coefficient-error scaling require a numerical-linear-algebra source and precise assumptions on the least-squares problem and condition number.

children.title: Anderson Resource-Overhead Boundary
children.top_down_role: Regimes in which history storage and mixing work exceed iteration savings.

children.title: Memory Overhead Boundary
children.top_down_role: Regimes where retained histories impose excessive storage costs.

assumptions_latex: An Anderson implementation retains \(m\) previous iterate-residual pairs
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Full-history storage requires \(2mn+O(n+m^2)\) scalars, so depth \(m\) is infeasible when this exceeds the available memory budget.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense storage without compression, checkpointing, or residual recomputation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Retaining \(m\) dense iterate differences and \(m\) dense residual differences requires \(2mn\) scalar locations. Current vectors, coefficients, and a dense small least-squares factorization add \(O(n+m^2)\) locations. Thus the memory footprint is \(M(n,m)=2mn+O(n+m^2)\). For a budget of \(B\) scalar locations, the full-history implementation crosses its memory boundary whenever \(M(n,m)>B\); in the history-dominated regime this restricts \(m\) to approximately \(B/(2n)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense Anderson acceleration stores two length-n histories, giving roughly 2mn scalar memory and limiting usable depth to about B divided by 2n.
knowledge_statements.title: Memory Overhead Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits the memory boundary, but the 2mn leading term depends on the stated dense two-history implementation and requires an inspectable implementation or complexity source.

children.title: Mixing-Work Overhead Boundary
children.top_down_role: Regimes where subproblem work exceeds iteration savings.

assumptions_latex: The residual-history matrix is dense of size \(n\times m\)
Mixing coefficients are computed by a dense QR-based least-squares solve
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The mixing overhead is \(O(nm^2+m^3)\) for refactorization and \(O(nm+m^2)\) when a stable factorization is updated.

notation.meaning: Cost of one base fixed-point evaluation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense arithmetic costs for forming and solving the Anderson mixing problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Forming the \(m\)-column residual-difference history costs \(O(nm)\) work per iteration when columns are already available. Recomputing its dense QR factorization and solving the constrained least-squares problem costs \(O(nm^2+m^3)\); maintaining a stable update reduces the incremental work to \(O(nm+m^2)\). Mixing ceases to be lower-order work when the selected implementation has \(C_{\mathrm{mix}}(n,m)\) comparable to or larger than \(C_F\), the cost of applying the underlying fixed-point map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense Anderson mixing may cost quadratic work in history depth; it becomes an overhead boundary when this cost rivals a base fixed-point evaluation.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixing-Work Overhead Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The container and complexity-bound kind fit, but the refactorization and update costs depend on the constrained formulation and update strategy. In particular, a standard dense QR solve does not inherently add an m^3 term.

children.title: Net-Savings Regimes
children.top_down_role: Operating regimes where acceleration retains a favorable total-cost profile.

assumptions_latex: The unaccelerated method takes \(N_0\) evaluations at cost \(C_F\) each
The accelerated method takes \(N_A\) evaluations and incurs per-step mixing cost \(C_{\mathrm{mix}}\) plus setup cost \(C_{\mathrm{setup}}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceleration yields net computational savings exactly when \(N_A(C_F+C_{\mathrm{mix}})+C_{\mathrm{setup}}<N_0C_F\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A deterministic additive runtime model with equal base-map cost in both methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the stated additive cost model, the baseline work is \(W_0=N_0C_F\), whereas accelerated work is \(W_A=N_A(C_F+C_{\mathrm{mix}})+C_{\mathrm{setup}}\). Therefore net savings occur if and only if \(W_A<W_0\), equivalently \(N_A/N_0<(1+C_{\mathrm{mix}}/C_F)^{-1}-C_{\mathrm{setup}}/(N_0(C_F+C_{\mathrm{mix}}))\). This condition separates iteration-count improvement from actual work reduction and excludes memory traffic or parallel effects not represented by the cost terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Acceleration saves work only when its reduction in base iterations outweighs all mixing and setup costs under the chosen cost model.

knowledge_statements.title: Over-Relaxed ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-block scaled ADMM with constant primal over-relaxation in finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \((z^0,u^0)\in Z\times Y\), compute \(x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\bigl\{f(x)+(\rho/2)\|Ax+Bz^k-c+u^k\|^2\bigr\}\). Form \(\widehat a^{k+1}=\alpha Ax^{k+1}+(1-\alpha)(c-Bz^k)\), compute \(z^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in Z}\bigl\{g(z)+(\rho/2)\|\widehat a^{k+1}+Bz-c+u^k\|^2\bigr\}\), and set \(u^{k+1}=u^k+\widehat a^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c\). Stop when the prescribed primal and dual residual tolerances hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Over-relaxed ADMM extrapolates the first block's constraint contribution before the second-block and scaled-dual updates, using a relaxation parameter strictly between zero and two.
assumptions_latex: \(X\), \(Z\), and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real Euclidean spaces
\(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) and \(g:Z\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) are proper closed convex functions
\(A:X\to Y\) and \(B:Z\to Y\) are linear maps, \(c\in Y\), and \(\min_{x\in X,z\in Z}\{f(x)+g(z):Ax+Bz=c\}\) has a solution
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Over-relaxed ADMM replaces \(Ax^{k+1}\) in the second-block and dual updates by \(\widehat a^{k+1}=\alpha Ax^{k+1}+(1-\alpha)(c-Bz^k)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed Forward–Backward Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constant-step relaxed forward–backward iteration for a cocoercive forward operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximally monotone and let \(B:H\to H\) be \(\beta\)-cocoercive on a real Hilbert space. Choose \(0<\gamma<2\beta\), define \(T_{\mathrm{FB}}=J_{\gamma A}(I-\gamma B)\), and put \(\alpha=2\beta/(4\beta-\gamma)\). Starting from \(x_0\in H\), select relaxation parameters \(0<\lambda_k<1/\alpha\) and update \[x_{k+1}=x_k+\lambda_k\bigl(T_{\mathrm{FB}}x_k-x_k\bigr).\] Stop when \(\|T_{\mathrm{FB}}x_k-x_k\|\) is below tolerance. Any fixed point returned by the iteration yields a zero of \(A+B\).

knowledge_statements.title: Fast Krasnosel'skii–Mann Splitting Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extrapolated Mann interface for an averaged splitting map, with restart or fallback safeguarding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\to H\) be an averaged splitting map. Initialize \(x_{-1}=x_0\), choose \(\beta_k\ge0\) and admissible relaxation \(\lambda_k>0\), and compute \[y_k=x_k+\beta_k(x_k-x_{k-1}),\qquad x_{k+1}^{\mathrm{fast}}=y_k+\lambda_k(Ty_k-y_k).\] Accept \(x_{k+1}^{\mathrm{fast}}\) when a stated residual or Lyapunov safeguard holds. Otherwise restart with \(\beta_k=0\) and take \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\lambda_k(Tx_k-x_k)\). Stop when the fixed-point residual is below tolerance. The interface specializes by substituting the desired forward–backward, Douglas–Rachford, or primal-dual map for \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extrapolate an averaged splitting iterate, apply a relaxed fixed-point step, and restart with the ordinary Mann step whenever the safeguard fails.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is an averaged self-map of a real Hilbert space.
The relaxation parameters lie in the admissible range for the averagedness constant.
The acceptance test is fixed before iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_{k+1}^{\mathrm{fast}}\) after acceptance and equals the baseline relaxed Mann step after restart.

children.title: Anderson-Accelerated Forward–Backward Splitting

knowledge_statements.title: Anderson-Accelerated Forward–Backward Splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safeguarded Anderson mixing of forward–backward residual histories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the forward–backward assumptions, define \(T=J_{\gamma A}(I-\gamma B)\) and \(r_i=Tx_i-x_i\). For memory \(I_k=\{k-m_k,\ldots,k\}\), compute \[\alpha^k\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{\sum_{i\in I_k}\alpha_i=1}\left\|\sum_{i\in I_k}\alpha_i r_i\right\|^2,\qquad x_{k+1}^{\mathrm{AA}}=\sum_{i\in I_k}\alpha_i^kTx_i.\] Accept the mixed point only if its evaluated residual satisfies the prescribed decrease safeguard; otherwise use \(x_{k+1}=Tx_k\). Stop when \(\|Tx_k-x_k\|\) meets tolerance. Regularization or coefficient bounds may be imposed in the least-squares subproblem without changing this interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mix stored forward–backward images by residual least squares, but fall back to an ordinary forward–backward step when the residual safeguard fails.
assumptions_latex: The constrained least-squares problem is solved with a declared regularization convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_{k+1}^{\mathrm{AA}}\) if safeguarded and \(x_{k+1}=Tx_k\) otherwise.

knowledge_statements.title: Anderson-Accelerated Three-Operator Splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safeguarded residual mixing for the Davis–Yin three-operator fixed-point map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A,B:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximally monotone, let \(C:H\to H\) be cocoercive, and define \[Tz=z-J_{\gamma B}z+J_{\gamma A}\bigl(2J_{\gamma B}z-z-\gamma C(J_{\gamma B}z)\bigr).\] With \(r_i=Tz_i-z_i\) and memory \(I_k\), choose affine coefficients minimizing \(\|\sum_{i\in I_k}\alpha_i r_i\|^2\), form \(z_{k+1}^{\mathrm{AA}}=\sum_{i\in I_k}\alpha_iTz_i\), and accept it only when the stated residual safeguard holds. Otherwise set \(z_{k+1}=Tz_k\). Stop when \(\|Tz_k-z_k\|\) is below tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply safeguarded Anderson residual mixing to the Davis–Yin three-operator map, retaining the ordinary splitting step as fallback.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(B\) are maximally monotone on a real Hilbert space.
\(C\) is cocoercive and \(\gamma\) lies in the admissible three-operator range.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{k+1}=z_{k+1}^{\mathrm{AA}}\) after safeguard acceptance and \(z_{k+1}=Tz_k\) otherwise.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Scaled Residual Mixing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted Anderson least squares for heterogeneous primal-dual residual blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the fixed-point state and residual decompose as \(z=(z^{(1)},\ldots,z^{(q)})\) and \(r_i=Tz_i-z_i\). Choose block metrics \(W_j\succ0\) and \(W=\operatorname{diag}(W_1,\ldots,W_q)\). For a memory set \(I_k\), compute \[\alpha^k\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{\sum_{i\in I_k}\alpha_i=1}\sum_{j=1}^q\left\|\sum_{i\in I_k}\alpha_i r_i^{(j)}\right\|_{W_j}^2,\qquad z_{k+1}^{\mathrm{mix}}=\sum_{i\in I_k}\alpha_i^kTz_i.\] Accept the candidate using the same weighted norm, or take the baseline point \(Tz_k\). The block metrics must be transformed consistently when primal or dual coordinates are rescaled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scale each residual block in the mixing least-squares problem and use the same block metric in the acceptance test.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a fixed-point map on a finite product of Hilbert spaces.
Each \(W_j\) is bounded, self-adjoint, and positive definite.
Coordinate changes and block metrics are transformed consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha^k\) minimizes the block-weighted residual norm and defines the safeguarded mixed candidate.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Variable Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Anderson acceleration restricted to a declared subset of state blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=H_a\oplus H_b\), let \(P_a\) and \(P_b\) be the corresponding orthogonal projections, and let \(T:H\to H\) be the baseline splitting map. With stored residuals \(r_i=Tz_i-z_i\), choose coefficients satisfying \(\sum_i\alpha_i=1\) by minimizing \(\|\sum_i\alpha_iP_ar_i\|^2\). Define \[z_{k+1}^{\mathrm{part}}=P_a\sum_i\alpha_iTz_i+P_bTz_k.\] Accept this candidate only under a full-state safeguard; otherwise set \(z_{k+1}=Tz_k\). Stop using the full residual \(\|Tz_k-z_k\|\), not merely its accelerated projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mix only selected state blocks, update all remaining blocks by the baseline map, and safeguard and stop using the full residual.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) has the declared orthogonal block decomposition \(H_a\oplus H_b\).
The accelerated projection is fixed or selected by a stated rule.
Acceptance is tested on the complete state residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_az_{k+1}^{\mathrm{part}}=P_a\sum_i\alpha_iTz_i\) and \(P_bz_{k+1}^{\mathrm{part}}=P_bTz_k\).

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposed Parallel Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-local residual-history mixing for separable parallel fixed-point evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=\bigoplus_{j=1}^qH_j\) and suppose the baseline map has parallel block evaluations \((Tz)^{(j)}=T_j(z)\). Each worker stores a synchronized index set \(I_k\), forms \(r_i^{(j)}=T_j(z_i)-z_i^{(j)}\), and computes \[\alpha^{k,j}\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{\sum_{i\in I_k}\alpha_i=1}\left\|\sum_{i\in I_k}\alpha_i r_i^{(j)}\right\|_{W_j}^2,\qquad \widehat z_{k+1}^{(j)}=\sum_{i\in I_k}\alpha_i^{k,j}T_j(z_i).\] Assemble \(\widehat z_{k+1}\) after synchronization and accept it under a global residual safeguard; otherwise use \(Tz_k\). Stop using a declared aggregate of all block residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute residual-history coefficients on parallel blocks, synchronize the assembled candidate, and retain a global safeguard and fallback step.

All workers use a consistent history index and state version.
The global acceptance test includes every block.

children.title: Infeasibility-Certificate Preservation

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasibility-Certificate Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic primal-infeasibility certificates retained through explicit post-acceleration verification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the conic feasibility system \(Ax=b\), \(x\in K\), where \(K\) is a closed convex cone, a vector \(y\) is a verifiable infeasibility certificate when \[A^*y\in K^*,\qquad \langle b,y\rangle<0.\] An accelerated splitting implementation preserves this certificate mechanism if it retains a certificate estimator \(y_k\) from its iterates or safeguarded baseline steps and reports infeasibility only after a nonzero limit or cluster point \(y\) satisfies both displayed tests. Normalization may be imposed on \(y_k\), but acceleration coefficients alone are not a certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preservation requires extracting and directly verifying a Farkas vector satisfying dual-cone membership and a strictly negative pairing with the right-hand side.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional inner-product space.
\(A\) is linear and \(K^*\) is the dual cone.
The reported vector is checked independently of the acceleration model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^*y\in K^*\) and \(\langle b,y\rangle<0\) certify that no \(x\in K\) satisfies \(Ax=b\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed Farkas certificate is standard and the certificate content kind fits the leaf, but no source is supplied for either the conic certificate or its preservation through accelerated splitting and post-acceleration verification. Source uncertainty therefore prevents review of the claimed preservation mechanism.

children.title: Unboundedness-Certificate Preservation

knowledge_statements.title: Unboundedness-Certificate Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic-program recession certificates retained through direct verification after acceleration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\), where \(K\) is a closed convex cone, and assume a feasible point exists. A nonzero direction \(d\) certifies primal unboundedness below when \[d\in K,\qquad Ad=0,\qquad \langle c,d\rangle<0.\] An accelerated splitting implementation preserves this diagnostic if it retains a direction estimator \(d_k\) and reports unboundedness only after a normalized limit or cluster point passes all three displayed tests. The mixed residual norm or growth of accelerated iterates, without these recession tests, is not an unboundedness certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preservation requires extracting a feasible recession direction with zero constraint displacement and strictly negative objective slope, then verifying it independently.
assumptions_latex: The conic program has at least one feasible point.
\(K\) is a closed convex cone and \(A\) is linear.
The candidate direction is checked independently of acceleration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d\in K\), \(Ad=0\), and \(\langle c,d\rangle<0\) imply that the primal objective is unbounded below.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recession-direction test is mathematically plausible and the certificate kind fits the leaf, but there is no citation supporting the conic unboundedness certificate or the asserted acceleration-preservation procedure. An authoritative source with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Minimal-Displacement Preservation

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal-Displacement Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic condition preserving displacement-based inconsistency information under acceleration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\to H\) be nonexpansive and define its minimal-displacement vector by \[v=P_{\overline{\operatorname{ran}(I-T)}}(0).\] For an accelerated sequence \((z_k)\), minimal-displacement information is preserved when its evaluated baseline residuals satisfy \(z_k-Tz_k\to v\), or, for normalized diagnostics, when every reported nonzero cluster direction of \(z_k-Tz_k\) equals \(v/\|v\|\). The implementation must therefore evaluate \(Tz_k-z_k\) at accepted iterates or retained baseline checkpoints; a small mixed model residual alone does not establish preservation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Acceleration preserves inconsistency information only when actual baseline residuals recover the minimal-displacement vector or its normalized direction.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(T:H\to H\) is nonexpansive.
The closure of \(\operatorname{ran}(I-T)\) is closed and convex.
Baseline residuals are evaluated at accepted iterates or checkpoints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_k-Tz_k\to v=P_{\overline{\operatorname{ran}(I-T)}}(0)\) is the preservation condition.

children.title: Primal-Dual Scaling Imbalance
children.top_down_role: Misleading residual mixing caused by incompatible block scales.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Scaling Imbalance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate dependence of unweighted residual mixing across heterogeneous primal-dual blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two stored residuals \(r_1=(1,0)\) and \(r_2=(0,\varepsilon)\), where the coordinates represent primal and dual blocks and \(\varepsilon>0\). Unweighted affine mixing minimizes \[\|\alpha r_1+(1-\alpha)r_2\|_2^2=\alpha^2+(1-\alpha)^2\varepsilon^2,\] giving \(\alpha=\varepsilon^2/(1+\varepsilon^2)\). After rescaling the dual coordinate by \(s>0\), the coefficient becomes \(\alpha_s=s^2\varepsilon^2/(1+s^2\varepsilon^2)\). Thus equivalent coordinate scalings can drive the mixing decision arbitrarily close to either endpoint unless a covariant block metric is used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unweighted primal-dual mixing is not invariant under block rescaling; equivalent units can change the least-squares coefficient from nearly zero to nearly one.
assumptions_latex: Mixing coefficients are affine, with weights \(\alpha\) and \(1-\alpha\).
The residual norm is Euclidean before and after coordinate rescaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_s=s^2\varepsilon^2/(1+s^2\varepsilon^2)\), so unweighted mixing is not invariant under primal-dual rescaling.

children.title: Inexact Proximal-Evaluation Contamination
children.top_down_role: History degradation caused by uncontrolled inner-solve errors.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Proximal-Evaluation Contamination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows how inertial history can amplify bounded errors in resolvent or proximal evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\to H\) be evaluated inexactly as \(\widehat T_kx=T x+e_k\), where \(H\) is a Hilbert space and \(\lVert e_k\rVert\leq\varepsilon_k\). For the inertial history update \[x_{k+1}=\widehat T_kx_k+\beta_k\bigl(\widehat T_kx_k-\widehat T_{k-1}x_{k-1}\bigr),\] the evaluation-error contribution equals \((1+\beta_k)e_k-\beta_ke_{k-1}\). Thus bounded or vanishing inner errors alone do not ensure vanishing contamination when \(\beta_k\) is uncontrolled. In particular, for \(H=\mathbb R\), \(T=0\), \(e_{k-1}=0\), and \(e_k=\varepsilon_k\), the iterate satisfies \(x_{k+1}=(1+\beta_k)\varepsilon_k\), which need not converge to zero unless \((1+\beta_k)\varepsilon_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inertial history multiplies current and previous proximal-evaluation errors. Even vanishing inner errors can prevent convergence when momentum grows faster than their decay.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a Hilbert space and \(T:H\to H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Convergence requires control of the amplified errors; boundedness of \(\varepsilon_k\) alone is insufficient.

notation.meaning: Exact fixed-point, resolvent, or proximal operator.
Additive evaluation error at iteration k.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algebraic error-amplification mechanism is correct, but no citation supports its interpretation as proximal/resolvent contamination or the general convergence-language conclusion.

children.title: Nonconvex Splitting Instability
children.top_down_role: Loss of baseline convergence behavior under acceleration in nonconvex regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Splitting Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A local linear model demonstrates that unguarded inertia need not preserve baseline stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a nonconvex splitting analysis supplies only a locally attracting fixed point whose linearized map is \(T(x)=q x\), with \(0<q<1\). Picard iteration \(x_{k+1}=T(x_k)\) converges geometrically to zero. The extrapolated iteration \[x_{k+1}=T\bigl(x_k+\beta(x_k-x_{k-1})\bigr)\] has characteristic polynomial \(p(r)=r^2-q(1+\beta)r+q\beta\). Stability therefore requires both roots of \(p\) to lie in the open unit disk. This condition is not inherited from \(q<1\): for \(q=0.9\) and \(\beta=2\), the roots are \(1.5\) and \(1.2\), so generic trajectories diverge although the baseline iteration converges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local attraction of the unaccelerated splitting map does not guarantee inertial stability; admissible momentum must satisfy a separate characteristic-root condition.
assumptions_latex: The accelerated update uses constant extrapolation \(\beta\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Baseline convergence does not imply accelerated convergence when global averagedness or an explicit inertial stability condition is unavailable.

notation.meaning: Local contraction factor of the baseline map.
Characteristic polynomial of the accelerated linear recurrence.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: For q=0.9 and beta=2, the polynomial is r^2-2.7r+1.8 and has roots 1.8 and 0.9, not 1.5 and 1.2. Divergence still follows, but a source is also needed to connect this generic linear example to nonconvex splitting.

children.title: Certificate Loss Under Naive Acceleration
children.top_down_role: Acceleration designs that obscure baseline inconsistency diagnostics.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Loss Under Naive Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates accelerated step differences from the true fixed-point residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A small accelerated step is not generally a certificate for \(x=T x\). On \(H=\mathbb R\), let \(T(x)=-x\) and apply the naive inertial recurrence \[x_{k+1}=T(x_k)+\beta(x_k-x_{k-1}).\] With \(x_{-1}=0\), \(x_0=1\), and \(\beta=2\), one obtains \(x_1=1\). Hence the observable step difference is \(\lvert x_1-x_0\rvert=0\), while the genuine fixed-point residual is \(\lvert x_0-T(x_0)\rvert=2\). Therefore a stopping rule based solely on consecutive accelerated iterates can falsely declare convergence; the baseline residual or an equivalent splitting certificate must be evaluated separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Momentum can cancel the visible iterate displacement while the true fixed-point residual remains nonzero, invalidating a step-difference stopping test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The implication \(\lvert x_{k+1}-x_k\rvert=0\Rightarrow x_k=T(x_k)\) fails for naive inertial acceleration.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The explicit counterexample is algebraically correct and fits the failure topic, but the record supplies no source for the certificate-loss claim or its splitting interpretation.

children.title: Picard Residual Complexity
children.top_down_role: Baseline complexity for unrelaxed fixed-point iteration.

knowledge_statements.title: Picard Residual Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case residual behavior of unrelaxed Picard iteration for nonexpansive maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\to H\) be nonexpansive on a Hilbert space, with \(\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\), and generate \(x_{k+1}=T x_k\). These assumptions alone yield no finite worst-case evaluation complexity for making \(\lVert x_k-Tx_k\rVert\leq\varepsilon\). Indeed, for \(H=\mathbb R\), \(T(x)=-x\), and \(x_0\neq0\), the map is nonexpansive and has fixed point zero, but \[x_k=(-1)^k x_0,\qquad \lVert x_k-Tx_k\rVert=2\lvert x_0\rvert\] for every \(k\). Thus unrelaxed Picard iteration need not be asymptotically regular; residual complexity requires stronger structure such as contraction or averagedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For general nonexpansive maps, Picard iteration may cycle with a constant residual, so no finite worst-case residual complexity exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(0<\varepsilon<2\lvert x_0\rvert\), the worst-case number of evaluations required by Picard iteration is infinite.

notation.meaning: Set of fixed points of T.

children.title: Krasnosel'skii–Mann Residual Complexity
children.top_down_role: Worst-case residual behavior of relaxed nonexpansive iteration.

knowledge_statements.title: Krasnosel'skii–Mann Residual Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constant-relaxation last-iterate residual bound for a nonexpansive mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\to H\) be nonexpansive with a fixed point \(x^*\), and let \(x_{k+1}=(1-\lambda)x_k+\lambda T x_k\) for a constant \(0<\lambda<1\). Writing \(D=\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert\), the fixed-point residuals are nonincreasing and satisfy \[\lVert x_N-Tx_N\rVert\leq \frac{D}{\sqrt{\lambda(1-\lambda)(N+1)}}.\] Consequently, at most \(N+1\geq D^2/[\lambda(1-\lambda)\varepsilon^2]\) operator evaluations suffice to obtain a last iterate with residual at most \(\varepsilon\). Thus constant-relaxation Krasnosel'skii–Mann iteration has worst-case residual order \(O(N^{-1/2})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constant-relaxation Krasnosel'skii–Mann iteration reduces the last-iterate residual at order one over the square root of the evaluation count.
assumptions_latex: \(T:H\to H\) is nonexpansive on a Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert x_N-Tx_N\rVert=O(N^{-1/2})\), requiring \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\) evaluations for residual tolerance \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Initial distance to a selected fixed point.
Number of completed fixed-point evaluations minus one.

children.title: Contractive Iteration Complexity
children.top_down_role: Geometric-rate behavior in contractive mapping regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Contractive Iteration Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric residual complexity for Picard iteration of a strict contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space and let \(T:H\to H\) satisfy \(\lVert Tx-Ty\rVert\leq q\lVert x-y\rVert\) for all \(x,y\in H\), where \(0\leq q<1\). Denote its unique fixed point by \(x^*\). Picard iteration \(x_{k+1}=Tx_k\) obeys \[\lVert x_k-Tx_k\rVert\leq(1+q)q^k\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert.\] If \(0<q<1\) and \((1+q)\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert>\varepsilon\), it is sufficient to choose \[k\geq\left\lceil\frac{\log((1+q)\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert/\varepsilon)}{-\log q}\right\rceil.\] Computing \(Tx_k\) to certify this residual uses \(k+1\) operator evaluations starting with \(Tx_0\). If \(q=0\), then \(x_1=x^*\) and the residual at \(x_1\) is zero. For every fixed \(0<q<1\), the residual evaluation complexity is \(O(\log(1/\varepsilon))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Picard iteration for a contraction has geometric residual decay. For a fixed positive contraction modulus below one, its residual evaluation complexity is logarithmic in the inverse tolerance; the zero-modulus case terminates after the first update.
assumptions_latex: \(T:H\to H\) is a contraction with modulus \(0\leq q<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(0<q<1\), the residual decreases geometrically as \((1+q)q^k\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert\), yielding \(O(\log(1/\varepsilon))\) evaluation complexity for fixed \(q\); for \(q=0\), \(x_1=x^*\).

children.title: Halpern Residual Complexity
children.top_down_role: Worst-case residual behavior of anchored nonexpansive iteration.

knowledge_statements.title: Halpern Residual Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical anchored iteration and its nonexpansive fixed-point residual rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\to H\) be nonexpansive, let \(x^*\in\operatorname{Fix}T\), and choose the anchor \(u=x_0\). The Halpern iteration \[x_{k+1}=\frac{1}{k+2}u+\frac{k+1}{k+2}T x_k\] satisfies the fixed-point residual estimate \[\lVert x_k-Tx_k\rVert\leq\frac{2\lVert u-x^*\rVert}{k+1}.\] Therefore \(k+1\geq2\lVert u-x^*\rVert/\varepsilon\) evaluations suffice for residual at most \(\varepsilon\). The anchored scheme consequently has \(O(k^{-1})\) residual decay and \(O(\varepsilon^{-1})\) evaluation complexity over nonexpansive mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With the canonical reciprocal anchoring schedule, Halpern iteration attains an order-one-over-k fixed-point residual for nonexpansive maps.
assumptions_latex: \(T:H\to H\) is nonexpansive and has a fixed point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert x_k-Tx_k\rVert=O(k^{-1})\), giving \(O(\varepsilon^{-1})\) evaluation complexity.

notation.meaning: Fixed anchor of the Halpern iteration.
Any fixed point used in the distance bound.

children.title: Optimized Halpern Complexity
children.top_down_role: Worst-case behavior of optimized anchoring schedules.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimized Halpern Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon optimized anchoring in the nonexpansive black-box oracle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a horizon \(N\) and consider anchored iterations \(x_{k+1}=\alpha_k u+(1-\alpha_k)T x_k\), where \(T\) is nonexpansive, \(u=x_0\), and \(\lVert u-x^*\rVert\leq D\) for some fixed point \(x^*\). An optimized Halpern schedule chooses \((\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_{N-1})\) to minimize the worst-case terminal residual over this oracle class. The resulting worst-case guarantee has order \[\sup_T\lVert x_N-Tx_N\rVert=\Theta\!\left(\frac{D}{N+1}\right).\] Thus optimization of the anchoring weights improves constants within the optimal \(O(N^{-1})\) residual order, corresponding to \(O(D/\varepsilon)\) evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-horizon optimization of Halpern anchoring weights attains the optimal order D over N residual, with improvements appearing in the worst-case constant.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) ranges over nonexpansive maps with a fixed point \(x^*\).
The schedule is optimized for a prescribed horizon \(N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimized worst-case terminal residual is of order \(D/(N+1)\).

notation.meaning: Optimized anchoring weight at iteration k.
Radius bound from the anchor to a fixed point.

children.title: Fast Krasnosel'skii–Mann Complexity
children.top_down_role: Residual-rate behavior of momentum-enhanced Mann-type schemes.

knowledge_statements.title: Fast Krasnosel'skii–Mann Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representative momentum-enhanced Mann recurrence; exact admissible parameters require source certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonexpansive map \(T:H\to H\), a fast Krasnosel'skii–Mann recurrence may be written \[x_{k+1}=\left(1-\frac{a}{k+a}\right)x_k+\frac{a}{k+a}T x_k+\frac{k}{k+a}\bigl(Tx_k-Tx_{k-1}\bigr),\qquad a>2.\] Under the method's admissible initialization and parameter conditions, its fixed-point residual satisfies \[\lVert x_k-Tx_k\rVert=o(k^{-1}).\] Consequently, the scheme improves upon the \(O(k^{-1/2})\) guarantee of constant-relaxation Krasnosel'skii–Mann iteration. The displayed little-o rate is asymptotic and does not by itself provide a uniform finite-horizon constant or a certified stopping index for tolerance \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A momentum-enhanced Mann recurrence can achieve residual decay faster than one over k asymptotically, but its exact parameter and initialization conditions need certification.
assumptions_latex: Initialization satisfies the requirements of the fast recurrence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under admissible conditions, \(\lVert x_k-Tx_k\rVert=o(k^{-1})\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact recurrence, admissible initialization, parameter range, and little-o residual theorem are variant-specific and cannot be certified without an authoritative source.

children.title: Imperfect-Evaluation Fixed-Point Complexity
children.top_down_role: Residual complexity under approximate or stochastic map evaluations.

children.title: Inexact Fixed-Point Complexity
children.top_down_role: Residual complexity under deterministic approximate map evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Fixed-Point Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic error propagation for inexact anchored fixed-point evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\to H\) be nonexpansive and compare the exact anchored sequence \(z_{k+1}=\alpha_k u+(1-\alpha_k)Tz_k\) with \(z_0=x_0\) to \[x_{k+1}=\alpha_k u+(1-\alpha_k)(Tx_k+e_k),\qquad \lVert e_k\rVert\leq\varepsilon_k.\] If \(w_k=1-\alpha_k\), then \[\lVert x_N-z_N\rVert\leq\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\varepsilon_j\prod_{i=j}^{N-1}w_i,\qquad \lVert x_N-Tx_N\rVert\leq\lVert z_N-Tz_N\rVert+2\lVert x_N-z_N\rVert.\] Hence the exact residual complexity is retained whenever the displayed weighted error accumulation is of no larger order than the exact-method residual bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inexact residual equals the exact-method rate plus a weighted accumulation of deterministic evaluation errors; preserving complexity requires controlling that accumulation.
assumptions_latex: The exact and inexact sequences share \(x_0=z_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inexact residual is bounded by the exact residual plus \(2\sum_{j<N}\varepsilon_j\prod_{i=j}^{N-1}(1-\alpha_i)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The deterministic coupling and weighted-error bounds are internally consistent, but the nontrivial inexact-complexity claim has no cited source.

children.title: Stochastic Fixed-Point Complexity
children.top_down_role: Residual complexity under random map evaluations or noisy oracles.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Fixed-Point Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mean-square propagation of unbiased stochastic errors in anchored nonexpansive iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\to H\) be nonexpansive and let \(z_{k+1}=\alpha_k u+(1-\alpha_k)Tz_k\). Consider \[x_{k+1}=\alpha_k u+(1-\alpha_k)(Tx_k+\xi_k),\] where \(\mathbb E[\xi_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=0\) and \(\mathbb E[\lVert\xi_k\rVert^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\leq\sigma_k^2\). With \(x_0=z_0\) and \(w_k=1-\alpha_k\), \[\mathbb E\lVert x_N-z_N\rVert^2\leq\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\sigma_j^2\prod_{i=j}^{N-1}w_i^2.\] Consequently, \[\mathbb E\lVert x_N-Tx_N\rVert\leq\lVert z_N-Tz_N\rVert+2\left(\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\sigma_j^2\prod_{i=j}^{N-1}w_i^2\right)^{1/2}.\] The exact complexity persists when this stochastic term matches or improves the exact residual order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unbiased oracle noise contributes a root-sum-square weighted error term to the expected residual of anchored fixed-point iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(\xi_k\) is conditionally unbiased with conditional second moment at most \(\sigma_k^2\).
The exact and stochastic sequences share their initial point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Expected residual complexity equals the exact residual bound plus the displayed weighted root-mean-square noise term.

notation.meaning: Information available before the kth oracle error.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mean-square recursion is plausible under the stated conditional-unbiasedness model, but its stochastic measurability assumptions and resulting complexity claim require a source.

children.title: Mixed-Error Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity regimes combining approximation effects with stochastic variability.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Error Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robust residual bound combining deterministic bias and stochastic evaluation noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\to H\) be nonexpansive and evaluate it as \(Tx_k+b_k+\xi_k\), where \(\lVert b_k\rVert\leq\delta_k\), \(\mathbb E[\xi_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=0\), and \(\mathbb E[\lVert\xi_k\rVert^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\leq\sigma_k^2\). Compare the resulting anchored iteration with its exact counterpart \(z_k\), using common weights \(w_k=1-\alpha_k\) and common initialization. Then the root-mean-square deviation satisfies the robust estimate \[\bigl(\mathbb E\lVert x_N-z_N\rVert^2\bigr)^{1/2}\leq\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}(\delta_j+\sigma_j)\prod_{i=j}^{N-1}w_i.\] Therefore the expected residual is at most the exact residual plus twice this mixed-error accumulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With simultaneous bias and noise, a safe complexity bound adds their weighted magnitudes to the exact anchored-method residual rate.
assumptions_latex: The exact and perturbed sequences use identical anchors, weights, and initialization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E\lVert x_N-Tx_N\rVert\leq\lVert z_N-Tz_N\rVert+2\sum_{j<N}(\delta_j+\sigma_j)\prod_{i=j}^{N-1}(1-\alpha_i)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed mixed-error estimate is a plausible conservative bound, but no citation supports the joint bias-noise model or its complexity interpretation.

children.title: Fixed-Point Residual Optimality Bounds
children.top_down_role: Worst-case barriers and matched optimality structures for fixed-point residual reduction.

children.title: Nonexpansive Residual Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Worst-case barriers for black-box nonexpansive fixed-point iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonexpansive Residual Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic black-box lower bound in a Hilbert-space nonexpansive-operator oracle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix an integer \(N\geq 1\) and \(R>0\). For every deterministic algorithm that makes at most \(N\) adaptive value-oracle queries to an unknown nonexpansive map \(T\) and then returns \(z_N\), there exist a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, such a map with \(\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\), and an initial point \(x_0\) satisfying \(\operatorname{dist}(x_0,\operatorname{Fix}T)\leq R\), for which
\[
\lVert z_N-Tz_N\rVert\geq \frac{cR}{N+1},
\]
where \(c>0\) is a universal constant. Thus no method in this oracle model guarantees residual decay \(o(N^{-1})\) uniformly over nonexpansive maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every deterministic N-query black-box method has a nonexpansive instance whose returned fixed-point residual is at least a universal constant times R/N.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is nonexpansive on a Hilbert space and \(\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\).
The algorithm receives information only through at most \(N\) adaptive evaluations of \(T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_T\lVert z_N-Tz_N\rVert=\Omega(R/N)\).

notation.meaning: algorithm output after at most N oracle evaluations
initial distance bound to the fixed-point set

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: adversarial oracle lower bounds establish the inverse-iteration residual barrier for general nonexpansive maps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits the leaf, but the strong universal lower bound depends on the precise deterministic oracle model, admissible output information, dimension construction, and normalization. No inspectable source is supplied, so the mathematical claim cannot be validated reliably.

children.title: Optimal Halpern Parameter Families
children.top_down_role: Minimax and stepwise optimality within anchored iteration.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal Halpern Parameter Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical anchored schedule attaining the order-optimal residual rate for nonexpansive maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given an anchor \(u\), initialize \(x_0=u\) and, for \(k\geq0\), compute
\[
x_{k+1}=\alpha_{k+1}u+(1-\alpha_{k+1})T x_k,
\qquad \alpha_{k+1}=\frac{1}{k+2}.
\]
Stop after \(N\) evaluations of \(T\) and return \(x_N\). If \(T\) is nonexpansive, \(x_\star\in\operatorname{Fix}T\), and \(\lVert u-x_\star\rVert\leq R\), this harmonic anchoring family guarantees \(\lVert x_N-Tx_N\rVert=O(R/(N+1))\). Combined with the black-box lower bound, its worst-case residual order is minimax optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Halpern iteration with harmonic anchor weights achieves an order-optimal O(R/N) fixed-point residual for general nonexpansive maps.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is nonexpansive and has a fixed point \(x_\star\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert x_N-Tx_N\rVert=O(R/(N+1))\), matching the general \(\Omega(R/N)\) oracle order.
